author: AfricanFeminism
title: Morocco’s First Woman Prime Minister and the Terms of Freedom
content:
Something changes when a woman occupies an office men have treated as their natural inheritance. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri’s

appointment

 on 29 September 2026 makes that change visible in Morocco. For women whose competence is routinely scrutinised, the pleasure is neither naïve nor trivial.


But the woman forming a government and the woman labouring in the fields, raising children without pay and denied an equal share of her inheritance encounter power differently. Representation changes who governs; emancipation changes what all women have the power to do. That distinction shifts our attention from PM Mansouri’s gender to the politics of the centre-right

 Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM

)

, which she leads. Will its programme redistribute the resources and rights on which women’s freedom depends?


The history beneath the headline


Calling women’s leadership foreign to Morocco requires forgetting its history. Historian Osire Glacier

documents

 women’s authority long before the contemporary premiership. Kenza al Awrabiya, the Amazigh mother of Idris II, helped secure the Idrisid dynasty, founded in the late eighth century in what is now Morocco. Zaynab al Nafzawiyya influenced eleventh-century Almoravid politics around Aghmat, near Marrakech. Sayyida al Hurra governed Tétouan, a city in northern Morocco, during the sixteenth century. Khnata bint Bakkar intervened in eighteenth-century dynastic politics.


Across the region,

Dihya

 is remembered as an Amazigh queen who led resistance to the Arab conquest in the Aurès, in present-day Algeria, during the late seventh century. Tuareg oral tradition remembers

Tin Hinan

 as a queen and founding ancestress of noble lineages in the Ahaggar, in present-day southern Algeria.


These histories expose how male authority is made to appear natural. Fatima Mernissi’s

The Forgotten Queens of Islam


challenges that selective memory. Colonialism also reorganised authority: French Protectorate administrators

reshaped

 customary courts around imperial priorities. What survives as tradition can carry the history of political intervention. 


Religious interpretation can give exclusion another claim to permanence. Islamist and other conservative opponents invoke this

hadith

 against women’s political authority:


«لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً»


Usually translated as saying that a people governed by a woman will not prosper, it becomes a prohibition irrespective of her competence. Asma Lamrabet, a

Moroccan Islamic feminist thinker

, questions turning a

narration linked

 to Persia’s dynastic succession into a universal ban. She reads it against the Qur’anic Queen of Sheba, whose judgement demonstrates capable leadership. Her argument contests male authority’s claim to divine necessity.


PAM’s promises and its record


Women have long contested how authority is distributed within the family. Fatima Sadiqi

documents

the Union de l’Action Féminine’s 1992 million-signature campaign to reform the Moudawana, Morocco’s family code. The 2004 reform abolished wives’ duty of obedience but retained unequal inheritance and exceptions to the marriage age of eighteen. Proposals announced in December 2024 left fundamental equality demands unresolved. In October 2025, more than sixty civil society organisations and public figures

joined to call for comprehensive reform

. Rights in Morocco have advanced through organised demands, not the gender of an officeholder.


PAM, a centre-right party founded in 2008,

advocates

 social modernisation and positions itself against the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD). It entered government in 2021 alongside the National Rally of Independents and conservative nationalist Istiqlal. Opposition to Islamist conservatism, however, does not itself entail reforming the laws and economic conditions that subordinate women.


PAM’s

2026 programme

 promises improved widow pensions, childcare, safe transport, a women’s enterprise fund and labour inspection. The commitments leave inheritance equality, abortion reform and decriminalisation of consensual same sex relations unaddressed. Mansouri called for

banning child marriage

 without exceptions in 2024, yet PAM’s electoral programme

omits that commitment

. Employment can support independence, but a wage does not cancel criminalisation or unequal property rights. The programme leaves those constraints intact.


Even PAM’s narrow promise to increase …

author: Willy Mutunga
title: Book Review: From Mau Mau to Ruto-Must-Go: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism
content:
I recently read a review of the book, 

From MAU MAU to RUTO-MUST-GO: A Scrapbook of Essays on Kenya’s Struggle Against Imperialism,

 

by Teddy Odira, a young lawyer in Nairobi who published in The Platform for Law, Justice, and Society. I shared the review with one of the co-editors of the book, Shiraz Durrani, and asked him what he thought. This is was his response via a WhatsApp text:


It’s a brilliant review, I think. He understands the undercurrents that the book explores and identifies key issues, like land, that have driven resistance. He also sees resistance as an on-going, incomplete struggle. Very well done!


What is well said by another is mine. In this review, I want to glorify the work of the artist movements in Kenya for breathing life into the Constitution of Kenya, 2010, particularly

Article 33

 that decrees freedom of expression. This freedom of expression has limitations. It is the freedom of artistic creativity that is glorified in two of the articles in the book. They glorify cartoonists and Social Justice Theatre (SJCCTT). Freedom of artistic creativity in Kenya is valued by others, including the two mentioned. The others include: poets, spoken word artists, graffiti artists, songwriters, singers, comedians, filmmakers, and others. Freedom of artistic creativity has been a radical site of struggle in the implementation of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010. Freedom of expression under the Constitution has been the subject of a recently published scholarly work.


This Constitution has been described as progressive and transformative because of the process of its making, its texts on objectives, purpose, and vision to reform, by non-reformist reforms, which maintain the status quo in Kenya. While the ruling elite find the Constitution inconvenient and abstract, these sites of struggle have used provisions of the Constitution to craft political demands, breathe life into these sites through uprising, robust public participation, mass action, and public interest litigation. The quest for an authentic patriotic alternative political leadership is a continuous struggle anchored in these constitutional sites of struggle that the ruling elite has refused to implement. It is argued that such an alternative political leadership that is authentic and patriotic will implement the Constitution by consolidating gains made, and rescuing the weaknesses that are encountered during the process of its implementation.


Glorification


A: In Praise of Cartoonists: Ruo Kimani-Ruo


Ruo Kimani-Ruo praises the cartoonists in words that should not be paraphrased:


…,

there has emerged an unprecedented form of political cartoons artwork which has been launched in Kenya with sizzling, scorching, blistering cartoon editorials and other graphics and caricatures of public figures that express the artists’ opinions, with celebrated cartoon artists Celeste and Maddo


being joined by Yoko and others-all freely and fearlessly expressing their opinions on public issues and the individuals in government and thereby shedding light on the public mood on issues.…


With these political cartoons, the artists have had a field day and typically combined artistic skills, hyperbole and satire to question authority. The cartoons have drawn attention to, among other things, corruption, electoral inequalities, political abductions and other social ills including violence- and the Consolidated Fund at Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) where billions of shillings are being ‘siphoned and stashed in offshore accounts in the West; and suspicions of embezzlement.


The genius of the cartoonists that I have encountered over decades lies in the interpretation of their work for the powers that be, and the citizens themselves. They are always armed with many interpretations of their cartoons. They use those interpretations to either stay safe when confronted by elites and their machinery of violence, or to mobilize the citizens around the key messages. They invariably keep their mouths shut and let their work engage both the enemy and the friend. Their work requires great critical thinking, taking ideological and political positions in breathing life into the provisions of the Constitution to energize non-reformist reforms.

Zachary J Patterson

author: Frey Blake-Pijogge, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Attending the Arctic Circle Gathering as an Inuk Youth was transformative and inspiring
content:
Frey Blake-Pijogge helps facilitate a workshop about “the Arctic we are building” on Oct. 9 — part of the Arctic Indigenous Youth Cohort at the Arctic Circle Assembly in Reykjavík, Iceland.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


The shaking of hands and small smiles welcome me to Reykjavík, Iceland. So does the rain. 


I meet the rest of the Arctic Indigenous Youth Cohort the evening before the annual Arctic Circle Assembly starts, all of us tired after journeying from our many time zones that tightly span the planet’s North. 


On the streets downtown, people are buzzing. Reykjavík feels alive. And everywhere in the city of nearly 150,000, I see signs about the global assembly, held from Oct. 8-10. 


Federal Foreign Minister Anita Anand addresses more than 2,500 participants representing Arctic nations at this year’s Arctic Circle Assembly in Iceland from Oct. 8-10.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


Every October, the world’s northernmost capital city hosts the

event

, the largest annual gathering of its kind. Organizers

say

 more than 2,500 people from 75 countries attended this year.


Over three days, participants take in the event’s more-than-200 sessions — including panel discussions, round tables, forums, and workshops, their topics ranging from climate change to Arctic sovereignty, military defence, arts, and more. 


The Arctic Indigenous Youth Cohort program is run by the federal government’s

Global Arctic Leadership Initiative

.


Iceland hosted the three-day international assembly at Reykjavík’s Harpa Concert Hall and Conference Centre.

Photo by Frey Blake-Pijogge


The next morning, I arrive at Harpa Concert Hall and take in the ambiance of the crowd: the space is brimming with loud laughter and the steady, excited talking of delegates.


We meet in the designated Youth lounge — each of us bringing their own perspectives and skills from around the Arctic. Our cohort includes Indigenous Youth from “Canada,” the “U.S.,” Greenland, Norway, Finland, and Sweden.


Participants attend a session on at the annual Arctic Circle Assembly in Iceland on Oct. 9.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


The first day of the assembly goes by in a blur, as I’m jet-lagged and still getting used to the three-hour time change.


I attend sessions on the geopolitics of

polar climate research

; one on why media coverage of the Arctic is the “

final frontier in public interest reporting

”; how the region today is seen through the eyes of Youth leaders; and short presentations by student researchers from fields of biology, law, language, children, and computer science. 


All three days’ sessions are unique, yet echo similar themes.


It’s clear that Indigenous peoples are at the forefront of many of the international discussions. 


An Oct. 9 session hosted by the Pulitzer Center brought media experts together to talk about ‘All eyes on the Arctic, the final frontier of public interest reporting.’

Photo courtesy

Darryl Lyon


Graduate students from around the world present their Arctic research across academic disciplines.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/ACA


“Indigenous peoples have so much richness to offer,”

said

 the Inuit Circumpolar Council’s international chair Aluki Kotierk, former president of Nunavut Tunngavik. “I think states realize that.


“Many Indigenous peoples from the Arctic … have been very instrumental in Arctic diplomacy, and even globally.”


For the rest of the assembly, whether meeting people outside of panels or at the Youth lounge, I feel a huge sense of awe to see how us Inuit from all around Inuit Nunangat are at the forefront of these urgent global discussions. 


Youth at the Arctic Circle Assembly hold a discussion during the events.

Photo courtesy Oli Haukur Myrdal/Arctic Circle Assembly


Another thing I notice is how powerfully Inuit are showing up at the event — representing our culture through our voices, leadership and perspectives, adorned with our beaded earrings, our silapak (pull-over top), our furs, and our kakiniit (tattoos) and tunniit. 


Throughout the assembly, I meet people who are Sámi, Iñupiaq, Métis, Inuvialuk, Gwich’in — and from many other nations.


READ MORE:


Indigenous leaders give the UN a roadmap for protecting their peoples


They fill me with a powerful sense of shared kinship I’ve not experienced anywhere else, except with other Indigenous people.


Simply put, I hold this kinship …

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Police seize liquor, cash in Nunavik-Quebec investigation
content:
A man from Chambly, Que., and a woman from Kangiqsujuaq could face charges following a police investigation into the illegal possession and sale of alcohol.


The Sûreté du Québec’s Contraband Investigation Unit, working with the Nunavik Police Service, searched a property in Kangiqsujuaq on Wednesday.


The investigation, which began in June, also led to a search in Chambly on Tuesday, after investigators determined the two cases were linked.


The searches resulted in the seizure of nearly eight litres of various alcoholic beverages and close to $12,000 in Canadian currency, according to a news release issued Thursday by the Quebec provincial police.


The individuals involved are a 34-year-old man from Chambly and a 32-year-old woman from Kangiqsujuaq. The news release did not provide their names. They could face charges related to illegal possession of alcohol and selling it without the required permits under Quebec’s Act respecting offences relating to alcoholic beverages.

author: Sharon Lerner
title: Trump Admin Giving $1M to Group Studying Crime Against White South Africans
content:
The new award comes after the administration cut human rights funding to nations in crisis.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

After slashing funding for programs that documented atrocities and protected human rights abroad, President Donald Trump’s State Department is now granting one of its first new human rights awards to a controversial South African organization that promotes the disputed notion that white farmers are a violently targeted, persecuted group, according to multiple sources knowledgeable about the funding.

The group expected to receive the nearly $1 million award, AfriForum, is a nonprofit that advocates on behalf of Afrikaners, a subset of South Africa’s white population. The organization says its members, who have a “God-given calling,” fight for Afrikaner interests and self-governance. The money will be used to “document hateful rhetoric and violent acts” against Afrikaners and other minority populations in the country.

The new award comes from a State Department bureau tasked with promoting democracy and human rights internationally. Until last year, those funds were mainly spent in poor and authoritarian nations — to fight corruption in the Democratic Republic of Congo, for example, or combat child exploitation and sexual abuse in Afghanistan. Since Trump returned to office, his appointees have transformed the bureau, gutting its staff, canceling programs and reorienting some of its funding toward conservative causes in Europe.

Samuel Samson, who was appointed as a deputy assistant secretary to the State Department bureau by Trump, has claimed the U.S. has a “civilizational” connection to Afrikaners, who descend primarily from Dutch migrants and predominantly speak Afrikaans. Samson, who has met with far-right leaders in Europe since joining the administration last year, has framed the U.S. government’s financial support for Afrikaners as grounded in “a common heritage, a common culture, a common way of life, shared history and ultimately a common anthropology.”

There’s a long shared political history between Afrikaner groups and white nationalists in the U.S., said Audie Klotz, a political science professor at Syracuse University who has studied those connections. But, she said, “There’s no heritage connection here. It’s pure scientific racism. In the history of U.S. immigration, there’s no direct connection between South Africa and the United States.”

AfriForum met with the Trump administration in February 2025 to plead for help. The group told officials that Afrikaners are subject to racial discrimination and murders that are more frequent and asked the administration to “act strongly against hate speech that incites violence” against them, according to a statement.

South Africa is plagued by high rates of violence, and some Afrikaners have been tortured and murdered. But independent researchers have found those killings represent a tiny fraction of murders across the country, whose victims are disproportionately people living in poor urban areas, where residents are predominantly Black. Official government statistics, and two formal inquiries into the matter, do not reveal a pattern of targeted violence against Afrikaners.

But Trump subscribes to the idea that white farmers face a “genocide” and has cited disproportionate violence against them as a reason for punishing Africa’s wealthiest nation. In February 2025, he issued an executive order that cut off hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to South Africa and welcomed Afrikaners to the U.S. as refugees. Since then, the administration has opened the doors to more than 16,000 white South Africans while halting virtually all other immigration. Officials recently told Congress they plan to invite as many as 17,500 Afrikaner refugees to the U.S. in 2027.

AfriForum did not respond to specific questions for this story but said that “our understanding is that the allocation has not yet been finalised. Should the allocation indeed be awarded to AfriForum, we will make a public announcement in this regard.”

The new award is the administration’s latest show of support for the Afrikaner cause. author: Savanna Craig
title: Akwesasne community members fighting the opening of a Hyperscale data center
content:
A few minutes’ drive outside the borders of Akwesasne Mohawk Territory, industrial sites line the perimeter.


One aluminum reduction and smelting site now operates as a digital currency mining facility.


The facility is set to expand, opening the doors to a new hyperscale data center. The center will be another facility on the list of many that border Akwesasne, Kanienʼkehá꞉ka territory.


A truck with three Kanienʼkehá꞉ka women drive past the facility. As they pass, a group of men nail up “no trespassing signs” along the facility.


“You’re on native land,” Dana Leigh Thompson shouts from the driver’s window. Thompson has been fighting to protect Akwesasne’s land, water and people for decades from outside corporate industry.


“We don’t care how many signs they put up [saying] no trespassing,” says Thompson. “This is our land. This is the land of the Kanienʼkehá꞉ka. Period.”


Three industrial and commercial sites are located near Akwesasne. In the United States these are known as Superfund sites.


Johnson-Zafiris and Sunday plan for future MUSH events in Dana Leigh Thompson’s library. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


The digital currency mining facility once operated as Reynold’s Metals. For decades, the aluminum reduction and smelting site released high amounts of toxic polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) into the environment.


A significant amount of U.S. Superfund sites are located on or near Indigenous land. Indigenous communities in North America are disproportionately exposed to environmental contaminants, including PCBs, according to a

study from 2012

.


“There are 1,373 Superfund sites on or adjacent to indigenous communities in the United States,” says Thompson.


Two other Superfund sites line the border of Akwesasne.


The defunct

General Motors site leaked

 aluminum die casting contributing to PCB contamination.


Thompson stands on her land, neighbouring the former General Motors site.


“What happens when a boat passes, all the water goes out, pulls it out, then it acts like a suction cup,” she explains, explaining that the pollutants are pulled from the site where PCB contamination is buried in the ground.


The third Superfund site, Alcoa Grasse River, discharged PCBs on the land and neighbouring wetlands from the 1950s to the mid 1970s.


An anti-data center sign sits across from a digital mining facility, owned by the same company set to open the data center. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


‘Ranatakárias’


In July 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump signed an

executive order

 to accelerate federal permits of data center infrastructure. Within it, it states environmental reviews should be expedited to turn Superfund sites into data centers.


His efforts to expedite the conversion of Superfund sites into data centers, like the ones that line Akwesasne, has granted him the name “Ranatakárias” in Akwesasne.


“What that translates into is ‘town destroyer,’” says Thompson.


Now one of these sites will be expanding to develop a 1.5 million square foot hyperscale data center.


New York Digital Investment Group operates a digital mining facility on the old Reynold’s Metals site. The group has partnered with North Country Collocation Services to open the data center.


Wetlands surround the proposed three buildings that will inhabit the new hyperscale data center.


APTN News reached out to both New York Digital Investment Group and North Country Collocation Services for an interview request but didn’t receive a response.


Thompson is a mentor for the next generation. The next generation leading the fight against industrial and commercial sites from opening along Akwesasne are a group that calls themselves MUSH.


“We modeled ourselves after MASH, Mohawks Agree on Safe Health, which was created in 1981, during the height of all of the health effects and the environmental impacts that were happening to our people in the surrounding communities,” says Marina Johnson-Zafiris.


Sunday and Johnson-Zafiris walk through land being surveyed across from the where the data center will be built. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


Johnson-Zafiris is a member of MUSH – Mohawks United Safety and Health – alongside Ronni Sunday.


The two focus their post-secondary studies on focuses related to their work at MUSH.


“I’m a masters student at Paul Smith College, studying natural resource conservation,” says Sunday, announcing to an audience.


The duo presented their work to an audience of students, researchers and …

author: Marcelle Edenlord
title: Idaho’s OB/GYN Crisis was on the Ballot: Despite Idaho Voting No, the Nation Voted Yes
content:
Following the overturning of Roe, Idaho state law criminalizes abortion at all stages, except in the context of rape or incest that has been formally reported to law enforcement or to prevent the death of the mother. Within fifteen months of the ban’s enactment, 60 OB/GYN physicians stopped practicing obstetrics in Idaho.

As of 2024, 43% of obstetricians have stopped practicing, left the state, closed their practices within the state, or retired in response to harsh legislation. This has left over half of Idaho’s 44 counties without obstetricians, leaving the 23 practicing OB/GYN’s to serve 569,000 Idahoans.

This flight of providers is not a coincidence but rather a clear response to legislation that poses major threats to individuals seeking obstetrician services and physicians. The law’s narrow exceptions and criminal penalties can leave providers concerned about whether an abortion is legally permitted when a patient’s health is at risk. Physicians can be subject to two to five years in prison and risk losing their medical license and being sued for up to $20,000 per family member who chooses to file a lawsuit. This said, the ban’s language is unclear and has left many doctors unsure how to legally interpret the state’s policies and limitations, despite the significant consequences that can follow misinterpretation.

Additionally, this legislation specifically targets women in rural areas, as it causes them to travel significantly more to reach care. One doctor shared, “I have definitely seen people arrive to our hospital much sicker than they should be, and that’s all due to the time that they have to travel.”

This is specifically dangerous for pregnant women, as they are uniquely vulnerable to life-risking complications. Reports state several instances of hemorrhaging pregnant women being airlifted out of state to receive urgent, life-saving abortion care. Given that rural areas have already been reported to struggle to retain and recruit doctors, policies that cause massive flights of physicians are detrimental to women in rural areas and across the state.

As tragic as this is, it is in no way surprising, as 90% of the US has better maternal pregnancy outcomes than Idaho. Since these restrictive policies have been enacted, three labor and delivery wings have closed. Additionally, doctors of all specialties are seven times less likely to apply to work in states with restrictive abortion policies for their residency training.

The effects of Idaho’s abortion laws were also at the center of the state’s November 3 election. Idahoans had the opportunity to vote for safety and health through the Reproductive Freedom and Privacy Act. Tragically, the proposition failed. This said, it lost by 82,807 votes, with 385,716 voters sharing support. This act would have enabled reproductive healthcare decisions to be made between a doctor and patient without the state’s influence until a fetus is viable. It would additionally have freed providers and patients alike from the threat of punitive consequences.

As devastating as this loss is, abortion was on the ballot across the nation and Idaho’s loss is the minority. In Nevada, Missouri and Virginia, abortion rights have been defended or established. Idahoans deserve to have the opportunity to make private decisions with their providers about their healthcare. Providers should not have to choose between their professional obligations and state law. Nationally, the country is reckoning with the heartbreaking consequences anti-choice legislation has caused. Idaho will see justice prevail; it’s just a matter of time.

author: William D. Hartung
title: The Democrats have a mandate for peace — here are 4 urgent priorities
content:
This article

The Democrats have a mandate for peace — here are 4 urgent priorities

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Voters in the midterm elections dealt a decisive blow to Trump’s war agenda and have created new possibilities for challenging militarism and ending the debacle in Iran. The blue tsunami that swept across the country was driven by

many issues

, including tariffs, corruption and higher prices, but voter discontent was rooted in opposition to the war against Iran and the high fuel costs and inflation that resulted. 


The election outcome presents an opportunity for activists to intensify pressures to end the war, reverse excessive arms spending, restore necessary funding for vital social and environmental priorities, and protect democracy. We need to elect a government that will build the foundations for a forward-looking, progressive foreign policy by expanding essential diplomatic capabilities and restoring U.S. support for global cooperation.


The current electoral realignment can be compared to the dramatic political transformation that occurred in the 2006 midterm elections. That year, the Iraq war was the

decisive issue

 in helping Democrats pick up 31 seats in the U.S. House of Representatives and six in the Senate. Then as now, affordability and immigration were important issues, but the dominant concern was war in the Middle East. As analysts argued at the time, Iraq was the “

Archimedean lever

” that shifted voters toward Democrats. 


But when the new Congress assembled in 2007, Democratic Party leaders equivocated. Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi and Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid proposed a legislative agenda for the new Congress that ignored Iraq. 


Embed from Getty Images


As Tom Hayden wrote in  “Ending the War in Iraq”, antiwar activists were furious. Constituents bombarded Democratic leaders with demands to prioritize withdrawal from Iraq. Protesters gathered outside Pelosi’s San Francisco home. An estimated 100,000 people marched in an antiwar rally in Washington, D.C. 


Democratic leaders quickly got the message and agreed on a legislative strategy to establish a timetable for withdrawal, which Congress subsequently adopted. 


We may need to exert similar pressures now to ensure that the new Congress fulfills its political mandate to end the Iran war and takes action to reverse other elements of Trump’s dangerous foreign policies. 


The threats to peace have grown significantly in recent years, and they are enormous and multifaceted. An unending, illegal war in Iran and related carnage throughout the Middle East; the arming of repressive regimes, up to and including enabling genocide in Gaza and occupation and ethnic cleansing in Lebanon; the skyrocketing of military-related spending (proposed at more than

$1.5 trillion

 this year) and an accelerating nuclear arms race. All of this is occurring while the Pentagon is

moving

 rapidly towards the deployment of AI-driven weapons systems that can operate without human pilots or human control.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


The threat or use of force has taken precedence over diplomacy, economic development and peacebuilding programs. The White House has rebuked democratic allies in Canada and Europe while coddling authoritarian regimes in Russia and Saudi Arabia. 


The human, economic and environmental consequences of these militarist policies have been disastrous —

trillions

 of dollars wasted,

hundreds of thousands

 of lives lost and

tens of millions

 of people driven from their homes.      


The pursuit of peace abroad depends on the defense of democracy at home. Legislators must protect democracy by removing obstacles to the exercise of basic rights, including the right to vote, the right of assembly, freedom of speech and an end to discrimination based on race, gender, religion and sexual preference. We need to create an America where every person is cherished, and every person is treated with the dignity they deserve — and then we need to extend that ethos to the rest of the world.


For cooperation, not confrontation


On the foreign policy front, we must demand congressional and executive action on the following major goals:

author: Chad Nelson
title: La Guerra dei Politici contro gli Immigrati è un Diversivo
content:
Di

Chad Nelson

. Originale.

The Political Class’s War on Immigrants is a Diversion

, del 30 gennaio 2015. Traduzione italiana di

Enrico Sanna

.


Al dibattito sulla nomina a ministro della giustizia di Loretta Lynch, il 28 gennaio scorso, i repubblicani erano ansiosi di chiederle fino a che punto avrebbe spinto la sua politica amica di quella categoria di persone che il governo definisce “immigrati clandestini”. In un

confronto di idee

,

Jeff Sessions

, repubblicano, severo in materia di immigrazione, chiedeva chi, secondo la Lynch, ha il diritto di lavorare in America. In particolare, chi ne ha “più diritto”: un immigrato in regola, un cittadino o qualcuno entrato illegalmente nel paese? La Lynch ha saggiamente ignorato le tre ipotesi e ha risposto che vorrebbe che tra i lavoratori americani ci fosse anche chi non ha documenti.


Il modo di porre la domanda di Sessions, e le risposte implicitamente suggerite, dicono molto sul modo di pensare distorto della classe politica. Secondo il pensiero antiimmigrazione bipartitico, il Congresso avrebbe, come nota Sheldon Richman, “il diritto di concedere il permesso di lavorare”. Cosa che purtroppo è diventata legge comune. Oggi, chi ha diritto ad un posto di lavoro lo decidono perlopiù i burocrati di Washington e gli interessi particolari che si giocano così il diritto di

vendere

 i loro servizi in monopolio. Tu pensi di essere libero di svolgere un lavoro che hai scelto, in realtà gli innumerevoli requisiti imposti dallo stato limitano drasticamente quella tua scelta. E se sei abbastanza fortunato da superare tutti gli ostacoli, la possibilità di mantenere l’attività è spesso impedita dalla palude normativa.


I politici confidano in questo enorme potere per tenere al giogo i loro soggetti. Il diritto di dare un lavoro, con tutti gli annessi e connessi che accompagnano il potere di offrire un privilegio, permette alla classe politica di arricchirsi nel modo più efficiente possibile. Quando il lavoro, che si tratti di immigrati irregolari o afroamericani, diventa lavoro in nero, i politici perdono la capacità di intercettarlo e estorcere tributo. Non rispettare quell’intrico fatto di tasse e norme amministrative e professionali, per non dire del sistema di licenze che imbriglia intere professioni, può significare la fame. Si tratta di una struttura falsamente fatta passare per protezione di produttori e consumatori.


I burocrati non temono l’immigrazione clandestina. Temono l’impossibilità di sfruttare il lavoro degli immigrati irregolari. Sessions e gli altri come lui al Congresso nascondono le loro paure dietro la retorica del “noi contro loro”, in un’astuta messinscena al servizio di importanti fini politici. Con questo trucchetto i politici vogliono far credere di essere preoccupati non per la perdita del loro guadagno personale, ma per il “vostro” posto di lavoro, la “vostra” sanità, la “vostra” pensione. A chi è in norma (e paga le tasse) dicono che sta svolgendo un compito patriottico. Non bisogna odiare la scrematura dei loro stipendi, al contrario c’è da esserne fieri perché così si contribuisce al benessere generale. Il nemico è chi lavora senza permesso, chi distrugge il nobile impiego di chi è in norma. “Voi” siete i buoni e “loro” i cattivi. Gli immigrati senza documenti, politicamente impotenti, sono un facile bersaglio di Washington, servono a nascondere la finta isteria dei politici dietro una maschera umanitaria come neanche la peggiore agenzia pubblicitaria potrebbe fare.


Questa isteria, è bene dirlo, è rivolta a: 1) i disoccupati e i precari americani e 2) i pensionati. Il “noi contro loro” si rafforza quando ti dicono che se non si ferma l’immigrazione puoi perdere qualcosa. Chi ha un buon lavoro sicuro ed è relativamente indipendente dallo stato ha poche ragioni per preoccuparsi per qualcosa che riguarda il lavoro e i meccanismi retributivi altrui. Sono i vecchi, molti dei quali immigrati o discendenti di immigrati, che generalmente sono poco tolleranti verso la nuova ondata migratoria dal sud. Questa alterizzazione fa facile presa sui vecchi, i quali difficilmente conoscono gli immigrati e finiscono per credere che la loro presenza porta alla disintegrazione della cultura americana.


È lo stato, vera fonte di insicurezza e rovina culturale, a derubare i lavoratori e le persone oneste. Sondare le ragioni dietro l’interesse dei politici per l’immigrazione, svelarne i veri motivi, e allo stesso tempo riconoscere l’umanità dei nostri …

author: Victoria Valenzuela
title: Incarcerated Los Angeles Youth Fought for the Right to Hug Their Parents — and Won
content:
This story was co-published with


Truthout

.


Mercedes Maradiaga sat across from her 19-year-old son in the Los Padrinos Juvenile Hall in Los Angeles in complete devastation. Her son had at that point been incarcerated at the prison for two years and she had visited him every weekend. But that day in September 2024 was especially hard because it was their first visit since he had been beaten by officers earlier that week in a space in the jail where there were no cameras. The guards had jumped on and kicked him, and he needed surgery for a torn ACL. All she wanted was to give him a hug and reassure him that she was there. However, because of the no-contact visit policies at Los Padrinos, she was unable to give him that comfort.


Even during birthdays and holidays, they weren’t allowed to embrace. The boy endured the jail’s horrible living conditions — including rat infestations and flooded toilets — but couldn’t hug his mom for a moment of escape.


“I couldn’t even let him know I’m here just with the little hug,” Maradiaga said. “It would have meant everything to him. It was sad, and I did that for four years.”


Los Padrinos had

reopened a year earlier

 in 2023, after being shut down in 2019 due to conditions that violated the Board of State and Community Corrections (BSCC) standards, including abuses by staff. Six officers were criminally charged with

assault and child abuse

 for using pepper spray on several teenage girls. Reports

also cited a decreasing youth population

 as a factor for closure, yet staff

claimed to feel “outnumbered.”

 When Los Padrinos closed, youth were shuffled to another facility called Central Juvenile Hall — and then in 2023, that facility was closed down due to similar issues. Los Padrinos reopened, and just months later, the abuses restarted. In 2025,

30 officers were criminally charged

 by the California Attorney General with child endangerment and abuse, conspiracy, and battery for encouraging “gladiator fights” that pit youth against each other.


Olivia Shields, a justice transformation policy coordinator at Urban Peace Institute, described the constant closing and reopening of BSCC facilities as a “cycle of noncompliance.” Shields said the Los Angeles County Probation Department has ultimately failed with these maneuvers to address the core issue: unmet youth needs — which won’t be addressed through incarceration but through coordinated care in the form of individualized, robust support systems and resources.


“Rather than decarcerate these populations of young people and find community-based alternatives or step-downs for as many of them as possible, they basically shift the youth around from facility to facility to avoid noncompliance,” Shields said.


Long before the closing of Los Padrinos in 2019, the facility had a bad reputation among Angelenos. Maradiaga recalled hearing disturbing stories about the facility in the ’80s when she was a kid.


“I think it needs to be shut down,” Maradiaga said. “I think that there needs to be a better way for the youth. I don’t think locking them away from their family is the answer.”


The Appeal in Your Inbox


Subscribe to our newsletters for regular updates, analysis and context straight to your email.


          Sign Up


Barred From Basic Human Contact


When Ilana Parach, executive director and co-founder of

Hoops 4 Justice

, went inside Los Padrinos with a basketball and mentorship program, she quickly learned about what youth were facing inside. She felt it was important to give them a platform to express their needs directly, so she pivoted to working with them on legislation.


“They made a list of specific programs they wanted — resources for their families, reentry support,” Parach said. “At the bottom of that list, they wrote, ‘We want to hug our moms.’”


Incarcerated youth directly told her that one parent who hugged her son during a visit on his birthday then had her visit terminated and future visits suspended for two weeks. She said another youth was incarcerated for three years and had no choice but to watch his mother cry during the visits because she couldn’t hug him.


Contact visitation policies vary across California and are often left at the discretion of correctional officers. Parach said youth and staff both told her that Los Padrinos stopped allowing contact visits after the pandemic. Parach said that during meetings of the board of supervisors, she heard officers citing staffing shortages …

title: In the Crosshairs of the Far-Right Advance : An Update on Anti-Fascists and Anarchists in Greece
content:
Anarchist graffiti from Athens, Greece (2026)


The anarchist movement in Greece faces a new wave of repression. Urged on by the US and its obsession with combatting “far-left extremism,” the Greek state has targeted anti-authoritarians with new legal charges and attacked demonstrations, while fascists carry out street attacks and plot their return to the halls of power. Amidst a landscape of ongoing austerity, terrorism designations, lethal prisons, and ferocious wildfires, anarchists nonetheless continue to forge a combative culture of revolutionary solidarity.


In this article, we present an interview with an anarchist comrade in Athens assessing the current situation among anarchists and anti-fascists in Greece, along with analysis of the US’s role in advancing state repression and fantasies of Western supremacy.


The US and Greece: A Right-Wing Alliance to Defend “The West”


Earlier this month, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio delivered a speech at the Pnyx in Athens. With the historic Acropolis and the Parthenon—that ancient symbol of Western democracy, constructed with slave labor—in the background, he delivered a warning message to Greece’s political and business elite.


“The course we take will determine whether the West maintains its place at the head of the world or resigns itself to a future of atrophy and servitude and decline,” Rubio cautioned. “We will either choose to act now or lose the choice to act at all.” Lamenting how “nationalism became a dirty word,” he called for renewed militarism, praised Christian faith and martyrdom, and announced a new counterterrorism information-sharing program between the two countries. His statements were calculated to reinforce the colonial legacy of Western dominance over the rest of the world, while urging the worst of Greek society to imitate America’s current political trajectory.


US Secretary of State Marco Rubio constructs an elaborate photo op for his defense of nationalism, militarism, and “the West” (October 7, 2026).


The speech came in the wake of a conference Rubio convened in July that aimed to coordinate intensified repression against “far-left extremism.” The following month, the US government imposed a “global terrorist” designation on the Italy-based

Autistici/Inventati (A/I) tech collective

, which operated the free publishing platform NoBlogs.org.


Greece’s right-wing politicians and business leaders benefiting from the country’s endless austerity measures are heeding Rubio’s call to preserve the hubris of the so-called West. Meanwhile, governments are collaborating to escalate repression against any truly revolutionary movements that challenge the world’s current status quo.


Greece’s strategic importance to Western powers is rooted in its symbolic status as the birthplace of “Western Civilization,” as well as its strategic location in the world today. The country offers the US access to four military sites, including a dedicated Navy base in Crete’s Souda Bay. Those with a longer memory have not forgotten how the US supplied napalm to Greece’s fascist forces, who worked with the Nazis during World War II and later with the British and US in a Cold War anti-communist alliance. Fascists dropped American napalm on Greek partisan resistance fighters during the civil war from 1946 to 1949, scorching bodies and charring forests, leaving the countryside scarred to this day.


More recently, the Greek people were pummeled by the 2008 global economic crisis, brought on in part by Wall Street firms such as Goldman Sachs that raked in immense profits while destabilizing the world’s economy and immiserating millions. The US then contributed to the austerity measures imposed on Greece in 2010 by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), leading to years of ferocious resistance to neoliberal capitalism and government complicity.


Today, Greece’s current New Democracy regime upholds

the legacy of the brutal military junta

 of 1967-1974, promoting the image of Greece as a symbol European supremacy as invoked by Rubio. Despite its nationalist rhetoric, the government continues to lick the boots of the US, crushing opposition in the streets and enforcing a never-ending precarity on the majority of Greece’s increasingly exhausted and numb population.

author: CMI Argentina
title: La derrota del trumpismo y la resistencia al negocio tecnológico
content:
La victoria demócrata en ambas cámaras del Congreso estadounidense y el rechazo a los centros de datos constituyen un duro golpe para Donald Trump y sus aliados multimillonarios. Las caídas de las acciones tecnológicas exponen, además, las contradicciones financieras de la expansión de la inteligencia artificial. Mientras las corporaciones buscan nuevos territorios para sus inversiones, Milei ofrece Argentina con el RIGI y el proyecto de Súper RIGI.


Por Adrián Flores, Red Eco Alternativo


La derrota contundente para Trump en las elecciones de medio término del 3 de noviembre, además de expresar un repudio a las políticas de su administración, presenta otro resultadoespecialmente significativo: el rechazo ciudadano a la expansión de los centros de datos, una de las apuestas estratégicas del bloque político y económico que sostiene a Trump.


De las 41 medidas locales sobre centros de datos votadas ese día, 40 favorecieron restricciones, prohibiciones o mayores controles. En Alhambra, California, el 82% respaldó la prohibición de estas instalaciones; en Edgewater, Florida, la falta de aceptación a nuevas construcciones alcanzó el 77%. En conjunto, las medidas expresaron una resistencia territorial que alcanzó a diez estados.


La derrota republicana y este rechazo a los megaproyectos tecnológicos forman parte de una misma coyuntura política: el cuestionamiento a una alianza que reúne a la ultraderecha, el capital financiero y los multimillonarios tecnológicos.


La nube tiene dueño, consume recursos y necesita territorios


La resistencia a los centros de datos permite observar una de las contradicciones centrales del capitalismo tecnológico.


La inteligencia artificial se presenta como una revolución inmaterial, alojada en la nube. Sin embargo, su funcionamiento depende de una infraestructura material gigantesca: edificios repletos de servidores, minerales, redes de transmisión, enormes cantidades de electricidad y agua para refrigerar los equipos.


La carrera por dominar este mercado no es solamente una competencia científica. Es también una disputa por el control de recursos estratégicos y por la apropiación de la riqueza que genera su utilización.


Las corporaciones buscan energía barata, disponibilidad de agua, suelo, beneficios fiscales y gobiernos que garanticen condiciones favorables. Las comunidades, en cambio, enfrentan la presión sobre sus fuentes de agua, el incremento de la demanda eléctrica, la transformación de sus territorios y los costos de infraestructura que muchas veces terminan socializándose.


No se trata de rechazar los avances tecnológicos. Se trata de discutir quién los controla, para qué se desarrollan y quién paga su expansión. El conocimiento y la capacidad de procesamiento quedan concentrados en unas pocas compañías, mientras los territorios aportan los bienes comunes necesarios para sostener sus negocios.


Las denuncias de las comunidades donde ya funcionan


Las advertencias no son hipotéticas. En regiones donde los centros de datos llevan años funcionando, vecinos y organizaciones ambientales vienen denunciando sus consecuencias sobre la vida cotidiana y los bienes comunes.


En The Dalles, Oregón, donde Google opera varios centros de datos desde 2006, organizaciones ambientalistas y habitantes cuestionan el enorme consumo de agua y la falta de transparencia sobre los acuerdos entre la empresa y el municipio. Según datos oficiales analizados por la radio pública OPB, Google utilizó más de 434 millones de galones de agua en 2024, alrededor de un tercio del consumo total de la ciudad. Las denuncias también apuntan a la presión sobre las fuentes de abastecimiento y a las dificultades de la población para acceder a información sobre los contratos y las prioridades de uso durante períodos de sequía.


En el norte de Virginia, unas de las mayores concentraciones de centros de datos del mundo, organizaciones vecinales y ambientalistas denuncian el ruido permanente de los sistemas de refrigeración y los generadores, el consumo de agua y electricidad y la expansión de estas instalaciones sobre zonas residenciales y rurales. En Prince William County, asociaciones vecinales llegaron a presentar reclamos formales por el ruido industrial durante las 24 horas. En otros puntos del estado, las protestas lograron frenar proyectos que pretendían instalarse cerca de viviendas.


Estos testimonios muestran que detrás de las promesas de innovación y crecimiento económico existe una realidad que las …

author: anred
title: ¿Qué pasó en Guernica?, el gobierno de Alberto y la represión a la última ola de tomas de tierras
content:
Sergio Berni, entonces ministro de Seguridad bonaerense, se jactaba de desalojar cinco tomas de tierra por semana. Era plena pandemia, cientos de miles de familias que no podían pagar alquileres o vivían hacinadas buscaron una salida en la ocupación de terrenos. Ocurría la última gran ola de “tomas de tierras” durante el gobierno de Alberto Fernández que terminó marcada por la represión, las promesas incumplidas y el abandono. Guernica se convirtió en el caso visible y emblemático de aquella crisis: la organización de más de 2 mil familias en tierras “compradas” en dictadura destinadas a un country, la resistencia al desalojo y la exposición mediática obligaron al gobierno provincial a abrir una negociación que estuvo atravesada por titubeos, dilaciones y propuestas que no resolvían el problema habitacional. Por ANRed | Imagen: German Romeo Pena


Primero es necesario contar que la “ocupación de tierras “ tras la dictadura fue una modalidad habitual de las clases trabajadoras más empobrecidas para adquirir sus viviendas ante la sucesiva falta de respuesta habitacional que dieron las democracias posteriores, es decir ni el Estado y menos el mercado resolvieron la crisis habitacional. Para aquel entonces los últimos datos eran delCenso Nacional de 2010, el déficit habitacional alcanzaba 3,5 millones de vivienda entre ellas 1,3 millones de viviendas faltantes y 2,2 millones de viviendas que no proveían  las condiciones mínimas para mantener un nivel de vida digno. 9 millones de personas que eran inquilinos, cifras que actualmente se han agravado en el último censo del 2022.


Luego el desenlace del conflicto en Guernica, disputa que estuvo atravesado por la crisis política y económica que sacudía al gobierno de Alberto Fernández. En septiembre de 2020, la disparada de los dólares paralelos, la presión empresaria y la preocupación oficial por la inestabilidad económica habilitaron una ofensiva política contra las tomas de tierras. Sergio Massa, junto con la intendenta de Presidente Perón, Blanca Cantero, impulsaron una posición de endurecimiento frente a las ocupaciones. Cantero convocó a intendentes del conurbano que reclamaban una respuesta judicial y policial, mientras se consolidaba un bloque político que exigía terminar con la toma y enviar una señal contra nuevas recuperaciones. Guernica comenzaba a ser presentada como un antecedente peligroso que debía clausurarse para evitar que se multiplicara.


14 intendentes piden desalojar tomas de tierras y Berni se publicita defendiendo la «propiedad privada»


La tensión se agravó en octubre con la ocupación de la estancia Casa Nueva, perteneciente a la familia Etchevehere, en Entre Ríos. La iniciativa fue impulsada por Dolores Etchevehere junto al Proyecto Artigas, con el acompañamiento de Juan Grabois y militantes vinculados del Movimiento de Trabajadores Excluidos (MTE), que proponía desarrollar un proyecto agroecológico en esas tierras. La reacción de empresarios y la derecha política que venía presionando por desalojar Guernica reaccionó de inmediato: el conflicto se convirtió en una bandera contra las recuperaciones de tierras y en una supuesta amenaza generalizada a la propiedad privada. La disputa con los Etchevehere intensificó la presión política y mediática sobre el gobierno nacional. Dentro del Frente de Todos también se profundizaron las diferencias: mientras un sector intentaba sostener la negociación y encontrar una salida habitacional, Massa, Berni y los intendentes reclamaban hacer cumplir la orden judicial. Las negociaciones impulsadas inicialmente desde Nación, con participación de funcionarios vinculados al Movimiento Evita, contemplaron una posible relocalización colectiva, pero naufragaron en medio de las disputas internas entre el Movimiento Evita y La Cámpora. Desde septiembre, Andrés Larroque quedó al frente de las conversaciones provinciales, cada vez más condicionadas por la presión judicial y política.


Finalmente, el 28 de octubre, cuando todavía se discutía una última prórroga y existían conversaciones para evitar una intervención violenta, la Justicia rechazó el pedido de postergación y la gobernación cancelo las negociaciones inventando justificaciones. En la madrugada del 29, unos 4.000 efectivos de la Policía Bonaerense.. La decisión terminó imponiendo la línea de Berni y de los intendentes: el desalojo como respuesta disciplinadora frente a las recuperaciones de tierras, antes que una solución de fondo a la emergencia habitacional. author: Natália Perez
title: Tsunami azul nas midterms: será o fim da era Trump?
content:
As eleições de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos, conhecidas como

midterms

, terminaram na última terça-feira, 3 de novembro. Nelas, os eleitores escolhem os representantes da Câmara, parte dos integrantes do Senado e governadores estaduais. O Partido Democrata conquistou a maioria dos votos. Para a cientista política Tatiana Vargas-Maia, convidada do Pauta Pública desta semana, essa vitória representa um reequilíbrio das forças políticas nos Estados Unidos e pode indicar tendências importantes para a próxima disputa presidencial, em 2028.


Na conversa com Andrea Dip, a cientista política e professora de Economia e Relações Internacionais da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul analisa o que muda, de fato, nos dois anos que restam do mandato de Trump, e o que esse recado das urnas pode significar para a extrema direita para o Brasil, que acaba de sair de uma eleição em que a relação com os Estados Unidos também esteve em jogo.


Para Tatiana, o fato de Trump declarar que vai aceitar os resultados é uma sinalização de moderação, mas ela ressalta: “Eu não sei se ele consegue se moderar durante muito tempo. Eu acho que isso permanece para a gente observar. Tem um outro elemento que nós precisamos começar a considerar, que é como é que o Partido Republicano se articula pós Donald Trump.”


Tatiana Vargas-Maia é cientista política e professora de Economia e Relações Internacionais da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul


Leia os principais pontos da conversa e ouça o podcast completo abaixo.


EP 241


											Tsunami azul nas midterms: será o fim da era Trump? – com Tatiana Vargas-Maia


6 de novembro de 2026


					·


				Cientista política analisa as causas e as possíveis consequências da vitória democrata nas eleições legislativas dos EUA


0:00

Veja mais episódios desta série


Para começar eu queria ouvir a sua avaliação geral sobre a eleição de meio-mandato nos Estados Unidos, na qual os democratas retomaram o controle das duas casas no Congresso. Como você analisa esses resultados e os impactos para Donald Trump?


Acredito que estamos de frente, possivelmente, de um cenário mais interessante do que muitas pesquisas estavam antecipando às vésperas da eleição. Muitos analistas estavam também, talvez, um pouco céticos que poderia acontecer a retomada democrata, tanto do Senado quanto da Casa dos Representantes, além de vitórias significativas em diversos governos dos estados. É muito interessante interpretarmos esses dados em contraste com as eleições de 2024. Naquele momento, os resultados demonstraram uma guinada significativa do eleitorado americano para a direita, ou seja, cada vez mais pessoas votando nos republicanos, o que garantiu a partir de 2025 a possibilidade do Trump governar com relativo baixo atrito.


Para entendermos melhor: a composição da Casa dos Representantes e do Senado nos Estados Unidos serve como um contrapeso para o Executivo Federal, para a presidência. Quando o presidente e as casas estão alinhadas, dominadas pelo mesmo partido, isso reduz significativamente o atrito que o presidente pode encontrar para avançar questões políticas e pautas que ele considera interessantes. Nós vimos o efeito disso nos dois primeiros anos do mandato de Donald Trump. Comparando o governo de 2017 com o que começa em 2025, em 2025 percebia-se um governo muito mais desinibido e com decisões inclusive muito polêmicas, como a questão da imigração e da dimensão comercial internacional dos Estados Unidos.


Agora, essa vitória democrata que muito da mídia americana e dos analistas tem chamado de uma onda, ou agora com os resultados confirmados, de um ‘tsunami azul’, na verdade reequilibra, digamos assim, o jogo de forças dentro dos Estados Unidos. Também indica algumas tendências de mudança muito interessantes para as próximas eleições presidenciais, em 2028. É um cenário muito fascinante para pensarmos não apenas em termos analíticos – que a mim interessa pontualmente –, mas, sobretudo, a dimensão de uma certa vitalidade democrática, inclusive no contexto dos Estados Unidos.


Sobre Trump, assim que ele retornou à Casa Branca, em seu segundo mandato, assinou várias ordens executivas, as executive orders, que são decretos presidenciais que não exigem a aprovação prévia do Congresso, inclusive algumas bem polêmicas. Mesmo com a derrota nesse


midterm

, o resultado pode frear o Trump ou ele é capaz de seguir impondo suas pautas, mesmo sem apoio?

author: La Zarzamora
title: Lanzamiento de Black Onions, un listado de sitios web anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion
content:
Publicado originalmente en Montréal Contre-information

Nos complace anunciar el lanzamiento de Black Onions, una nueva iniciativa que tiene como objetivo ofrecer una lista estable y actualizada periódicamente de sitios anarquistas y antiautoritarios con extensión .onion. Los sitios .onion son sitios web accesibles a través del navegador Tor mediante direcciones que terminan en «.onion».

En los últimos meses, algunos gobiernos han atacado las infraestructuras de comunicación de nuestros movimientos con renovado vigor; buena prueba de ello son la conferencia internacional sobre el «terrorismo de extrema izquierda» celebrada en Estados Unidos en julio, así como la inclusión del proveedor de servicios de alojamiento militante italiano Autistici/Inventati en una lista de sanciones relacionadas con el terrorismo a finales de agosto.

Para bien o para mal, la comunicación pública de nuestros movimientos tiene lugar en gran medida en Internet, lo que la hace vulnerable a los mecanismos tecnológicos de censura. A diferencia de los sitios web convencionales, los sitios .onion son menos vulnerables a la censura, ya que no utilizan nombres de dominio y permiten ocultar la ubicación del servidor, del mismo modo que el navegador Tor oculta tu propia ubicación al visitar el sitio. Consideramos que los sitios .onion son nuestra mejor baza para seguir comunicándonos en línea dentro del movimiento anarquista, especialmente si los intentos de censura se intensifican en el futuro.

El problema recurrente de los sitios .onion es que sus direcciones, compuestas por 56 caracteres aleatorios, son imposibles de memorizar. Black Onions tiene como objetivo resolver este problema. Te recomendamos guardar en los marcadores del navegador Tor, o en un archivo en tu ordenador, las direcciones .onion que utilizas habitualmente; pero si necesitas una dirección que aún no has guardado, ¡encuéntrala en Black Onions!

Accede a Black Onions a través de cualquiera de las siguientes direcciones:

– blackonions.gd – blackonions.li – blackonions.st – (próximamente, una dirección .onion)

Para establecer una base de confianza en esta nueva iniciativa, los siguientes proyectos anarquistas han avalado nuestra propuesta mediante declaraciones firmadas con PGP: Act For Freedom Now!, un proyecto de contrainformación activo desde 2008 , y el No Trace Project, un proyecto contra la represión activo desde 2021.

¡Utiliza sitios .onion! ¡Resiste a la censura!

author: Darío Aranda
title: La salud no es lo primero: en Argentina se utilizan 167 agrotóxicos prohibidos en otros países
content:
Por Javier Souza Casadinho*


Los plaguicidas autorizados en Argentina que están prohibidos o no autorizados en otros países alcanzan la cifra de 167 productos, y 35 de ellos son Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos (PAP) según los criterios establecidos por la FAO (organismo de Naciones Unidas para la agricultura y la alimentación) y la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS). Entre las

empresas responsables sobresalen


Syngenta, Bayer, Adama, Corteva y Atanor

. En Argentina, cada año, su utilizan 580 millones de litros de venenos del agro.


Incremento en el uso de plaguicidas


El

modelo productivo agrícola en la Argentina

 ha experimentado una profunda transformación en las últimas décadas, caracterizada por la expansión de la frontera agropecuaria y la adopción consolidada de paquetes tecnológicos dependientes de fertilizantes sintéticos y agroquímicos, mal denominados "fitosanitarios".


En este contexto cobran especial relevancia los Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos (PAP). En Argentina, la problemática adquiere dimensiones críticas debido a los volúmenes de aplicación y a la cercanía de las zonas de cultivo con núcleos poblacionales. Los casos más frecuentes y documentados de exposición e impacto ambiental, que en ocasiones derivan en

demandas judiciales

, involucran a principios activos de amplio uso

como el glifosato, el paraquat, la atrazina, el 2,4-D y la cipermetrina

.


Lejos de limitarse a un único sector, estas sustancias se emplean de manera intensiva y extensiva en distintas matrices productivas que configuran el mapa productivo del país, abarcando

desde la agricultura extensiva de cereales y oleaginosas hasta economí

as regionales como el cultivo de tabaco y la horticultura

. Un informe del Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA) señala que “la Argentina se caracteriza por tener un importante consumo anual de productos fitosanitarios, los cuales son de origen nacional por síntesis o formulación y muchos son importados. En los 36 millones de hectáreas cultivadas,

se utilizan 230 millones de litros de herbicidas y 350 millones de litros de otros productos

 fitosanitarios”.


Una comparación entre la superficie sembrada de cereales y oleaginosas y el consumo de plaguicidas desde 1990 hasta la actualidad muestra que el aumento en el uso de plaguicidas ha sido muy superior al incremento en la superficie cultivada. En las últimas tres décadas, la superficie sembrada con cereales y oleaginosas creció de 19.000.000 de hectáreas en 1990 a 41.182.000 hectáreas en 2023, lo que representa un aumento del 117 por ciento. En el mismo período, la producción pasó de 38.200.000 toneladas a 140.893.000 toneladas, un incremento del 269 por ciento.


Entre 1990 y 2022, el uso de plaguicidas en Argentina se incrementó de manera exponencial: pasó de 35 millones a 580 millones de kg/litros, lo que representa un aumento del 1.657 por ciento.


Existen diversos factores de índole económica, productiva y ambiental que pueden incidir en el incremento en la utilización de plaguicidas tales como: aumento de las especies de hierbas resistentes a herbicidas, mayor presión de los patógenos (hongos y bacterias)

,

 incremento en la superficie agrícola de alimentos y de biocombustibles, baja de aranceles a la importación de determinados principios activos precursores de plaguicidas, reducción en el precio de ingredientes activos cuyas patentes han caducado, alta demanda de insumos por parte de la horticultura y fruticultura para mantener la calidad formal de los productos, el

cambio climático

 junto a modificaciones en las legislaciones que regulan el registro, uso y comercialización de estos insumos.


Foto: Nicolás Mendiola – Greenpeace


Los Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos (PAP)


Según el Código de Conducta sobre Manejo de Plaguicidas (adoptado por la FAO y la OMS en 2013) y de las Guías sobre PAP, los Plaguicidas Altamente Peligrosos pueden definirse como:


Los que presentan niveles particularmente altos de peligro agudo o crónico para la salud o el ambiente, conforme a los sistemas de clasificación aceptados a nivel internacional, como los de la OMS o del SGA (Sistema Globalmente Armonizado).


Por estar incluidos en acuerdos o convenios jurídicamente vinculantes.


Aquellos que aparecen como causantes de daño grave o irreversible a la salud humana o al ambiente, en las condiciones de uso en un país, pueden ser considerados y tratados como altamente peligrosos.


Desde la

Red Internacional de Acción …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: «Cuanto peor, mejor» no es una opción para la clase trabajadora  Por qué votaré el 29N
content:
«Cuanto peor, mejor» no es una opción para la clase trabajadora


Por qué votaré el 29N


«Cuanto peor, mejor» no es una opción para un padre. No es una opción para la clase trabajadora. Por eso, el 29N votaré contra el PP-VOX: por sentido común, por responsabilidad con la gente que quiero y porque formo parte de esa clase trabajadora, que somos mayoría en todos los sentidos. Somos quienes movemos las ruedas de la historia, pero también somos manipulados y manipulables, y conviene no olvidarlo.


Sin carné y sin ilusiones.


No soy del PSOE. Tampoco del Frente Amplio ni del próximo invento que se monten. No soy de Podemos ni estoy afiliado a ninguno de los partidos que van a pedir el voto. Pero soy clase trabajadora consciente, y esa conciencia me dice que no quiero un Gobierno del PP-VOX que gobierne contra mis intereses hasta terminar de robarnos todos los derechos que nos quedan.


Una obligación con los nuestros.


Tenemos una obligación con nosotros mismos, con los nuestros y con las futuras generaciones. Una generación que no es capaz de dejar a la siguiente una sociedad mejor es una generación de fracasados. Y no hay peor manera de fracasar que cruzarse de brazos mientras la derecha y la ultraderecha nos desmontan lo poco que hemos conquistado con décadas de lucha.


La socialdemocracia no es la solución, pero el abismo tampoco.


Sé que la socialdemocracia no es la solución, porque no va a la raíz de los problemas. Soy consciente de que lo que ha hecho es insuficiente, frustrante y, en ocasiones, inútil. Sufro las consecuencias de una sociedad desigual en la que la macroeconomía va como un tiro y la microeconomía de la mayoría va como el culo. Pero la solución no es un suicidio colectivo, y estar ante un precipicio no significa que tengamos que saltar, como han hecho en Argentina o Paraguay.


De la pobreza a la miseria.


Sé lo que es enfermar y pasar de la pobreza a la miseria, porque los trabajadores estamos desprotegidos bajo una socialdemocracia que forma parte del sistema. Precisamente por eso, también sé que ir de Guatemala a Guatepeor es una decisión estúpida que traerá todavía más sufrimiento a más gente. A quienes siempre pagan la factura: los de abajo.


Votar no es rendirse.


Votar contra el PP-VOX no es rendirse ni darle un cheque en blanco a nadie. Es frenar al enemigo más inmediato para seguir teniendo terreno donde organizarnos, sindicarnos y pelear por lo que de verdad importa: la raíz del problema. Esa pelea no se gana desde el desastre; se gana desde la organización, en los centros de trabajo y en los barrios.


Que nadie nos quite lo único que tenemos: el sentido de clase. El 29N, que cada uno vote según su conciencia, pero sin perder de vista quién gana y quién pierde si dejamos que el precipicio se nos acerque un paso más.


 


¡Até á vitoria sempre!


 


André Abeledo Fernández

title: Tons of oak trees cut down on Mount Gabar
content:
Tree felling continues on the Mişarê Plain of Mount Gabar in Şırnak countryside. Logging activities, which have intensified in the region recently, have reportedly accelerated with the approach of winter on the mountain slopes facing the Eruh (Dihê) district of Siirt (Sêrt).

Footage recorded on the Mişarê Plain in Eruh showed tons of oak trees felled on different dates lined up along the roadside for transportation. The logs, stacked on top of one another, were seen stretching for hundreds of meters.

Meanwhile, the Şırnak and Siirt bar associations had previously filed criminal complaints with the chief public prosecutors’ offices, demanding an end to the tree felling in the region.

author: Brian Hioe
title: May Chin Indictment Gestures Toward Extensive Reach of Chinese United Front Work
content:
INDEPENDENT PAN-BLUE legislator Kao Chin Su Mei, also known as May Chin or Ciwas Ali, and who is an Indigenous legislator of the Atayal people, has been indicted for Chinese United Front work. According to prosecutors, Chin accepted more than 170 million NTD, which was funneled to organizations, relatives, and other bodies in order to conduct influence operations aimed at winning elections. Prosecutors are seeking 14 years for Chin, who was previously facing charges about illegally importing Chinese COVID-19 vaccines for distribution among her constituents.

The networks of these organizations were managed by her office director, Chang Chun-chieh, and legislative assistants Chen Chih-huang and Lin Yi-chun. Chang is currently under investigation for having fled overseas by boat in order to avoid arrest, with authorities conducting raids earlier this month to find the vessel on which he escaped. Chang and Chen reportedly coordinated United Front efforts, while Lin acted as an intermediary with China. Chin has been accused of using her influence as a legislator in order to influence government policy in arms sales, defense, cross-strait relations, and international relations.

For her part, Chin has denied participation in such United Front work, suggesting that she did not need Chinese support to win elections. Chin also raised questions about why she was apparently under surveillance for two decades before authorities acted on it, instead framing charges against her as politically motivated persecution by the Lai administration.

Rumors about Chin’s involvement in United Front efforts targeting Indigenous communities have been longstanding. China has long directed United Front outreach toward Indigenous communities, with the hopes that they will vote pan-Blue, as has often historically been the case. Such United Front outreach also aims to show Indigenous communities the benefits of unification with China, often by touting the supposed benefits that ethnic minority communities receive in China.

If Chin has finally been targeted by authorities, it is to be seen to what extent the KMT rallies behind her. Though Chin is a pan-Blue independent, she caucuses with the KMT and is generally understood to act in concert with the party. But it is possible that prosecutors will also take action on cases of other pan-Blue legislators who receive support from China. One notes that KMT legislative caucus leader Fu Kun-chi has faced charges of receiving campaign merchandise to be distributed among potential voters that was supplied by China. As Fu’s political network is rooted in Indigenous-heavy Hualien, it is possible that there are further ties to Chinese United Front work by him or other KMT politicians.

At the same time, it is also to be seen how the general public understands prosecution against Chin or other KMT legislators. Certainly, the public was willing to accept prosecution against former Taipei mayor Ko Wen-je on corruption charges, as well as other pan-Blue figures who have faced corruption charges, such as former Yilan magistrate Lin Zi-miao. But it remains to be seen whether they accept the validity of charges against Chin and other pan-Blue legislators implicated in United Front activity.

author: Daniel Aloc
title: #TrumpOut: Sampung awiting Pilipino laban sa imperyalismong US at Pax Silica
content:
Nakatakdang bumisita sa Pilipinas si United States President Donald Trump para sa ika-49 na Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit na gaganapin sa Metro Manila sa Nobyembre 16–18, 2026. Ngunit sa halip na salubungin nang pagdiriwang, naghahanda ang mga progresibo at makabayang organisasyon sa malawakang pagkilos upang ipahayag ang pagtutol sa patuloy na panghihimasok at dominasyon ng Estados Unidos sa bansa.

Bitbit ang mga panawagang “Trump Out” at “Reject Pax Silica,” tinututulan ng mga mamamayan ang mga patakarang lalong magtatali sa Pilipinas sa pang-ekonomiyang interes ng US. Kabilang dito ang planong pagtatayo ng Pax Silica industrial hub sa Tarlac.

Kaugnay nito, mahalagang pakinggan ang mga awiting Pilipinong tumatalakay sa imperyalismo, panghihimasok ng dayuhan, at pandarambong sa likas na yaman. Narito ang sampung kantang dapat pakinggan at muling balikan sa pagbisita ni Trump.

Ang title track ng compilation album na inilabas sa kasagsagan ng kampanya para sa pagpapalayas sa mga base militar ng US sa Pilipinas.

Binibigyang-diin ng kanta ang panganib na dulot ng presensiya ng mga base militar, na maaaring maglagay sa Pilipinas bilang target ng mga bansang kaaway ng US.

Sa gitna ng tumitinding tensiyon sa rehiyon, partikular sa pagitan ng Pilipinas at China, nararapat lamang itanong: seguridad ba ng mamamayang Pilipino ang pangunahing pinangangalagaan ng US, o ang sarili nitong estratehikong interes sa rehiyon?

Sabi nga ni Chickoy Pura: “Paalam na, paalam na sa’yo Uncle Sam / Sa inyo ka na maglaro ng baril-barilan!”

Totoong cute ang mga tuta, aspin man o may lahi. Ngunit kapag ginagamit ang salitang “tuta” upang ilarawan ang isang lider na sunud-sunuran sa dikta ng dayuhan, nagiging matalim itong pampulitikang insulto.

Madalas makita sa mga plakard tuwing rali ang katagang “Tuta ng Kano” bilsng pagpuna sa pangulong inuuna ang interes ng imperyalistang US kaysa sa kapakanan at soberanya ng mamamayang Pilipino. Tumpak na tumpak ang paglalarawang ito sa administrasyong Marcos Jr., na sagad-sagaring tuta ng Kano.

Sa mahabang kasaysayan ng bansa, paulit-ulit nang nagpalit ng mga pangulo, ngunit nanatiling nakatali ang Pilipinas sa Estados Unidos. Umaasa pa rin ang gobyerno sa suporta ng Washington sa gitna ng sigalot sa West Philippine Sea, sa ilusyon ng Mutual Defense Treaty, habang patuloy na ipinapatupad ang mga polisiyang pang-ekonomiyang nakasandig sa interes ng dayuhang kapital.

Isang satirikong alegorya tungkol sa historikal na relasyon ng Pilipinas at Estados Unidos ang Pinggan. Bahagi ng compilation album na Karapatang Pantao, ginagamit ng kanta ang kuwento nina Juan at Sam upang ilarawan ang di-pantay at mapagsamantalang ugnayan ng dalawang bansa.

Mahalagang balikan ang mensahe ng Pinggan: hindi tunay na pagkakaibigan ang isang relasyong ang makapangyarihan lamang ang nakikinabang habang patuloy na pinagsasamantalahan ang mahina. Hindi maituturing na patas ang ugnayan kung ang isang panig lamang ang nagdidikta ng mga tuntunin at ang kabila ang kailangang sumunod.

Isinulat nina Ed Formoso at Joey Ayala para sa album na Ikalawang Yugto ng supergroup na Lokal Brown, tinatalakay ng Pay U ang isang mahalagang suliranin ng ekonomiya ng Pilipinas: ang pagiging import-dependent at export-oriented nito.

Sa kabila ng likas na yaman at lakas-paggawa ng bansa, nananatiling nakasandig ang malaking bahagi ng ekonomiya sa pag-aangkat ng mga yaring produkto at pagluluwas ng mga hilaw na materyales. Sa ilalim ng neoliberal na balangkas, napahihina ang kakayahan ng Pilipinas na paunlarin ang sariling industriya, palakasin ang agrikultura, at makamit ang tunay na pagsasarili sa ekonomiya.

Ngunit sa halip na paunlarin ang sariling kakayahan sa produksyon, patuloy na itinatali ang bansa sa pandaigdigang sistemang pang-ekonomiya kung saan nananatiling nakikinabang ang malalaking dayuhang korporasyon.

Tampok ang tinig ni Bayang Barrios at isinulat ni Danny Fabella, inilalahad ng Igpaw, Mindanao ang mapaminsalang epekto ng malawakang pagmimina sa mga mamamayan ng Mindanao.

Sa ngalan ng tubo, napipilitang lumikas ang mga katutubo mula sa kanilang mga lupang ninuno upang bigyang-daan ang mga dambuhalang minahan. Kaakibat ng mga proyektong ito ang pagkasira ng kagubatan at mga ilog, gayundin ang pagkitil sa kabuhayan at karapatan ng mga komunidad na matagal nang nangangalaga sa kanilang mga lupain.

author: Mekong Review 2
title: The death of a scammer Tonggo Simangunsong
content:
Poipet, near the Thailand–Cambodia border. Credit: wattana / Shutterstock.com I t was the end of 2024. Almost five months after losing his job at a food and beverage company, thirty-nine-year-old Rasdy Fawzi told his wife, Kiki Tresia Ginting, that he was going to accept a job in Cambodia. Kiki was concerned, and for good reason. The man who’d offered him the job was part of a scam syndicate; the recruitment agency was unregistered and the work Fawzi would be undertaking was illegal. She’d heard stories of young Indonesians trapped in Cambodia, tortured and forced to work as scammers. “I worried and asked my husband about his safety if he worked there, but he said, ‘That’s okay, it’s fine, don’t worry’,” she recalls. Fawzi reassured her many times that his friend had been there, too, and he trusted him. He believed that he was too old for any company in Indonesia to want to hire him for the same role he’d had in mobile sales marketing with his previous employer. While going to Cambodia was risky, the salary offered would be more than enough to support their small family. It was an opportunity he didn’t want to pass up. In the end, there was nothing Kiki could do but let him go and pray for his safety. To read the rest of this article, and to access all Mekong Review content, please subscribe .
