title: Eskişehir Tepebaşı Belediyesi davası: 5 kişi tahliye edildi
content:
Tepebaşı Belediye Başkanı Ahmet Ataç | Fotoğraf: DHA

Eskişehir Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nca yürütülen soruşturması kapsamında geçen mayıs ayında Tepebaşı Belediyesi’ne operasyon düzenlendi. Gözaltına alınan 22 kişi işlemlerinin ardından adliyeye sevk edilirken, 7’si kamu görevlisi 12 kişi tutuklandı. 10 kişi ise adli kontrol kararıyla serbest bırakıldı.

Eskişehir Cumhuriyet Savcılığı’nda hazırlanan iddianameyle 4’ncü Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’ne dava açılırken, 15 kamu görevlisi hakkında zimmet suçundan 5 yıldan 12 yıla kadar, diğer 7 kişi hakkında ise ‘suça iştirak veya yardım’ iddiasıyla 2 yıl 6 aydan 6 yıla kadar hapis cezası talep edildi.

İddianamede Tepebaşı Belediyesi’nde aralarında özel kalem müdürü ve başkan yardımcısının da bulunduğu kamu görevlilerinin, organizasyon firma sahipleri D.A.'nın ve T.G.'nin üzerinden belediye bütçesinden yapılan ödemeleri zimmetlerine geçirdikleri öne sürüldü.

Eskişehir 4’ncü Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’ndeki davanın yaklaşık 11 saat süren ilk duruşmasına mahkeme heyeti tutuklu olan Süleyman U., Celal T., Fatma Begüm A., Ceren Aytaç A. ve Filiz T.’nin tahliyesine karar verirken, tutuksuz yargılanan Murat Ç.’nin ise tutuklanmasına hükmetti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı " trans kadın Arya" için yapılacak eylemi yasakladı
content:
İstanbul Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, TOBB ETÜ yurdunda yaşamını yitiren 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya için adalet talebiyle yapılmak istenen eylemi yasakladı.


“Arya’ya Ne Oldu?” İnisiyatifi’nin bugün Kadıköy Süreyya Operası önünde düzenlemek istediği eylem öncesinde polis, LGBTİ+’ların etrafını sardı.


Gazeteci Yusuf Çelik'in aktardığı bilgilere göre, bir süre polisle görüşen LGBTİ+’lar, eylemi gerçekleştirmeden alandan ayrıldı.


Kaymakamlık açıklaması


Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, TOBB ETÜ yurdunda yaşamını yitiren 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya için adalet arayan "Arya'ya Ne Oldu?" İnisiyatifi'nin bugün Kadıköy'de yapacağı eylemi yasakladı. Video: @21yusufcelk https://t.co/Of4HXkLOAP


— bianet (@bianetorg_)

November 8, 2026


Çelik'in aktardığı bilgiye göre, Kadıköy Kaymakamlığı, yasak kararını 2911 Sayılı Toplantı ve Gösteri Yürüyüşleri Kanunu ile 5442 Sayılı İl İdaresi Kanunu’na dayandırdı.


Kaymakamlığın açıklamasında, “İntihar değil cinayet! 19 yaşında TOBB ETÜ yurdunda intihara sürüklenerek katledilen Arya’nın hesabını sormak için sokaklardayız!” sloganıyla yapılması planlanan eylemin toplumda infial uyandırabileceği ve “toplumsal iç barışı tehdit edebileceği” öne sürüldü.


Açıklamada ayrıca eyleme katılacak gruplarla yurttaşlar arasında provokatif olaylar yaşanabileceği iddia edildi.


Kaymakamlık, 8 Kasım saat 00.00’dan itibaren bir gün süreyle ilçe genelindeki tüm açık alanlarda basın açıklaması, yürüyüş, oturma eylemi, miting ve benzeri etkinliklerin yanı sıra bu etkinliklere yönelik çağrı yapılmasını, bildiri dağıtılmasını ve stant açılmasını da yasakladı.


Yasak kararı, bugün saat 16.50’de kamuoyuna duyuruldu.


Ne olmuştu?


TOBB Ekonomi ve Teknoloji Üniversitesi (TOBB ETÜ) İngiliz Dili ve Edebiyatı Bölümü öğrencisi 19 yaşındaki trans kadın Arya, 13 Nisan’da üniversitenin yurdunda yaşamını yitirmişti.


Arya’nın ölümünün ardından arkadaşları ve üniversiteli LGBTİ+ toplulukları, olayın tüm yönleriyle aydınlatılması talebiyle “Arya’ya Ne Oldu İnisiyatifi”ni kurdu. İnisiyatif, Arya’nın eğitim ve yurt yaşamı boyunca sözlü, fiziksel ve dijital şiddete maruz bırakıldığını, yurt yönetimi ve bazı öğrenciler tarafından hedef gösterildiğini açıklamıştı.


Soruşturmada Arya’nın telefon ve bilgisayar gibi temel dijital materyallerinin henüz incelenmediğine dikkat çeken inisiyatif, ölümün yalnızca bireysel bir karar olarak değerlendirilmemesi gerektiğini vurgulamıştı. İnisiyatif, sistematik transfobinin ve kurumsal ihmallerin de soruşturulmasını talep etmişti.


(YÇ/EMK)

author: Antifa
title: Berlin – Timo Grönke – Ein Ausstieg ist noch keine Aufarbeitung.
content:
Der Name Timo Groenke ist vielen Antifaschist*innen in Berlin sicher ein Begriff. Mindestens in den Jahren 2024 und 2025 war er ein wichtiger Akteur in jugendlichen Neonazinetzwerken. Heute präsentiert er sich hingegen öffentlich als Neonazi-Aussteiger. Er versuchte zunächst linke Demonstrationen zu besuchen und engagiert sich seit Kurzem bei den Grünen in Marzahn-Hellersdorf. Diese schnelle Abkehr von der Neonaziszene in Kombination mit dem direkten Versuch, in andere Strukturen zu gelangen, wirft für uns Fragen auf. Deshalb möchten wir einige Gedanken zum vermeintlichen Ausstieg von Timo Grönke veröffentlichen.


Eines vorweg: Menschen können sich verändern und wir begrüßen es grundsätzlich, wenn Menschen die Neonaziszene dauerhaft verlassen. Dabei spielt es selbstverständlich eine Rolle, wie alt die Personen waren als sie in die Szene eingestiegen sind, wie lange sie darin waren und welche Aufgaben sie übernommen haben. Es geht uns ausdrücklich NICHT darum zu sagen: „Einmal Nazi, immer Nazi“. Aber ein seriöser Ausstieg bedeutet mehr, als sich von ehemaligen Kameraden zu distanzieren. Ein Ausstieg bedeutet, für einen dauerhaften Bruch mit der Szene zu sorgen, und sich damit auseinanderzusetzen, warum extrem rechte Weltbilder als politisch ansprechend empfunden wurden. Das ist um einiges vielschichtiger als einfach eine neue Geschichte über sich selbst zu erzählen.


Im Fall von Timo Grönke kommt es aus unserer Sicht zu einer erheblichen Verkürzung der eigenen Taten in der Vergangenheit, wodurch er eine tiefergehende Auseinandersetzung mit seiner Schuld umgeht. Aufarbeitung wird stattdessen auf sozialarbeiterische Angebote, wie das zurecht kritisierte „Violence Prevention Network“ oder polizeiliche Stellen ausgelagert. Insgesamt entsteht der Eindruck, dass Grönkes Hauptgrund für die Auseinandersetzung mit seiner Zugehörigkeit in der Neonaziszene vor allem der Druck von außen war. Auf Repression folgt ein „Deradikalisierungsprogramm“ und der Austausch mit Repressionsorganen. Aus seinen Erzählungen entsteht der Eindruck, dass er nicht mehr Nazi ist, weil er seinem Hobby als Schiedsrichter aufgrund von antifaschistischem Druck nicht mehr nachgehen konnte und die anderen Neonazis nicht besonders nett zu ihm waren. Zur Rechtfertigung seines jahrelangen Engagements verbreitet Grönke nun öffentlich die bekannte Erzählung vom jungen Mitläufer, der eigentlich nur durch seine Suche nach Anerkennung in die Szene geraten sei. Allerdings lässt dieses Narrativ wesentliche Aspekte seiner damaligen Aktivitäten unerwähnt. Eine ideologische Aufarbeitung und eine umfassende inhaltliche Distanzierung bleiben aus.


Aus den antifaschistschen Veröffentlichungen zu Timo Grönke wird schnell klar, dass er keineswegs nur ein unauffälliger Akteur am Rand war, der nur – wie er behauptet – deswegen ins Visier der Ermittlungsbehörden geriet, weil er lediglich auf Anweisung von Gruppenleiter Julian Milz Feuerwerkskörper in seiner Tasche mitgeführt hätte. Grönke war zu seiner Zeit als jugendlicher Neonazi einer der aktivsten Akteure des Netzwerks um „Deutsche Jugend Voran“ in Berlin. Er machte nicht nur still mit, sondern versuchte selbstständig Menschen nach rechts zu politisieren und zu mobilisieren.


Grönke inszenierte sich einige Zeit auf Demonstrationen als eine Art Journalist/Influencer und betätigte sich als Fotograf, dessen Fotos eine extrem rechte Selbstdarstellung bedienten. Daneben betrieb er – wenn auch wenig erfolgreich – ein rechtes Internetprojekt unter dem Namen „DEaktuell“. Dort behauptete er bereits damals, politisch neutral zu sein, verbreitete aber gleichzeitig rechte Inhalte und zeigte unkritisch Personen, wie seinen ehemaligen Kameraden Julian Milz. Seine Darstellungen waren bereits damals durchaus widersprüchlich: Während er die Gewalt von Julian Milz einerseits nach dessen Razzia auf seinem Instagram-Account strategisch kritisierte, unterstützte er andererseits die Öffentlichkeitsarbeit für seine Kameraden mit seinem Internetprojekt. Insgesamt zeichnete sein Auftreten ein durchaus sprunghaftes Bild. So unterstützte Grönke zunächst die Neonazi-Demonstrationen, die Ferhat Sentürk in Berlin organisierte, wetterte aber nur kurz danach gegen diese mit dem Wortlaut „Scheißt auf die Tü****demo“.


Timo Grönke war dementsprechend nicht einfach ein Verstärker der Ansichten von DJV und Konsorten. Er verbreitete eigenständig rechte Inhalte. So postete er beispeilsweise Anfang 2025 selbstständig Aufrufe zur Störung eines …

Al concluir el encuentro, los participantes cantaron el himno nacional y dejaron sus velas encendidas frente al Palacio de Justicia.


Antes de las 20.30, cuando la plaza ya estaba vacía, el personal de seguridad de la Corte Suprema las apagó y las retiró.


La Ley de Financiamiento Universitario fue aprobada por el Congreso y ratificada por los dos tercios de ambas cámaras, cuando anularon el veto presidencial inicial. Sin embargo, el Poder Ejecutivo la incumple: al promulgarla en octubre de 2025 mediante el Decreto 759, le introdujo un condicionante ilegal para su ejecución, que el Parlamento estableciera las fuentes de financiamiento y asignara las partidas presupuestarias correspondientes.


Sin embargo, la Justicia declaró inconstitucional el decreto del Ejecutivo que frena la aplicación de la ley y ordenó su cumplimiento inmediato para la actualización salarial de docentes y no docentes, además del refuerzo de becas estudiantiles.


A pesar de los fallos en contra por parte del Fuero Contencioso Administrativo, el Gobierno Nacional presentó recursos de apelación para no aplicar la norma.

author: Anne Marxze Umil
title: Trump out! | Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest
content:
Photo by Emman Capones/Pinoy Weekly

We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US.

Progressive groups launch 12 days of protest as the visit of US President Donald Trump to the Philippines approaches.

“Trump is not welcome here in the Philippines, he is not welcome anywhere in the world,” said International League of Peoples’ Struggles-Philippines Secretary General Arnold Padilla in a press conference on Wednesday, November 4.

Trump is scheduled to visit the Philippines on November 16 to sign the Pax Silica initiative also in time for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit.

“Under the banner of Trump Out, we shall hold daily actions ranging from rallies, indoor assemblies, public forums, pickets, concerts, teach-ins, camp-outs, and vigils aimed to express the Filipino people’s strong objection to Trump’s visit,” Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) Chairperson Teddy Casiño said.

Casiño added in Filipino, “Trump represents the largest imperialist power, which sows war, terror, oppression, and plunder across the world. This includes military aggression against Iran, support for genocide, the imposition of economic sanctions and intervention in Venezuela, Cuba, and other countries; military escalation in the Philippines and across the Asia-Pacific; and brutal repression of immigrants and critics within his own country.”

For Ana Marie Nemenzo of the Network Opposed to Pax Silica, Trump should be declared as persona non grata and barred from entering the country.

“We don’t want this lunatic to come to our country. He is a mass murderer who has initiated wars around the world, led by and benefiting the US. This shows that imperialism remains very much alive and must be opposed because it poses a major threat to the planet and endangers the lives of ordinary people around the world,” she added.

Nemenzo said the Philippines has not been truly free. She said since the so-called independence in 1946, the Americans have kept the Philippines tied to the U.S. economy. She also criticized the presence of soldiers and its equipment in the country and urged the public to join the movement to drive U.S. military forces out of the country.

Nemenzo also added that Pax Silica will only further tie the Philippines “to an economic framework that primarily benefits powerful countries seeking access to our critical resources.”

“We know that the Philippines is among the most vulnerable countries. The loss of people’s livelihoods must be a paramount concern,” she added, saying that her organization, Women’s Health is one in the campaign against Pax Silica.

For Pastor Allan Sarte, secretary general of Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association, Trump is the number one enabler of (then Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu that killed 70,000 citizens of Gaza, more than 20,000 of which are children. “We cannot in conscience welcome Trump in the Philippines,” he said.

Not only the Filipinos are rejecting Trump, Bayan said the glaring defeat of Trump’s party in the U.S. midterm elections is a powerful boost to the Trump Out campaign.

“The Democratic Party’s landslide victory, wresting control of both Houses of Congress and defeating Republicans even in traditional strongholds like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina, is a resounding repudiation of Trump and his rule,” the group said in a statement.

The group said the results of the election is a reflection of the growing disgust and rejection by the American people of Trump’s corrupt, authoritarian, war mongering, racist, anti-immigrant and over all anti-people policies. “They show that even in his own country, Trump faces mounting opposition to his disastrous leadership,” Bayan said.

The group expressed their solidarity with the American people who are resisting Trump’s attacks on their democratic rights, livelihoods, and welfare.

“They see through his collusion with his big corporate backers to enrich himself. They oppose his war on Iran and belligerence towards other countries’ sovereignty,” Bayan said. (RVO)

author: Vinil Kumar
title: Western Sydney Airport is a gift to business
content:
It’s rare for aviation executives and prime ministers to party in Western Sydney. But the opening of Sydney’s second airport, Western Sydney International (WSI), was an unmissable photo opportunity. Attendees included Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, his predecessors Tony Abbott and Scott Morrison, Jetstar CEO Stephanie Tully and NSW Premier Chris Minns. 

After the first passenger flight departed, the exodus back to the leafy Eastern Suburbs began, leaving behind the roar of turbo-fan engines that will only grow more frequent once the fanfare around the airport subsides.

The new airport is a monument to twenty-first century capitalism: a feat of human ingenuity, subordinated to corporate interests, with working-class people paying the price.

Background

Sections of business have long campaigned for a second major airport in Sydney. 

The established Sydney Kingsford Smith Airport at Mascot is boxed in by residential suburbs and Botany Bay. A third runway was opened in 1994, but community protests won a night-time curfew and hourly flight limits. 

Aviation is central to supply chains and corporate Australia wanted a new airport with minimal restrictions on its use.

After 60 years of 

proposals, disputes and false starts

, the project was revived in 2012, with the release of the Joint Study on Aviation Capacity in the Sydney Region by the federal and New South Wales governments. Its co-authors included the incoming Business Council of Australia head, Jennifer Westacott. 

The 

report

 warned Kingsford Smith airport would reach capacity by 2027 and unmet passenger and freight demand could cost as much as $60 billion by 2060. It argued the curfew “creates impediments for night-time movements of freight”, but that “an opportunity exists for a 24-hour freight facility to be established at a secondary airport”. Proximity to future warehousing and distribution centres made Western Sydney an enticing option.

Although the proposal for an airport at Badgerys Creek was rejected by the state and federal governments at the time, the 

Daily Telegraph

 immediately launched a 

renewed campaign

 for one. It was joined in its 

lobbying

 by the National Australia Bank, Harvey Norman, Crown Resorts, Channel 7 and executives from Western Sydney University. Backing was also 

secured

 from the peak body of local councils in Sydney. 

The Sydney Business Chamber, Western Sydney, led by former Labor state minister and member for Granville David Borger, 

established the Western Sydney Airport Alliance

 to cohere a local campaign for the airport.

In 2014, Liberal Prime Minister Tony Abbott’s federal cabinet approved the proposal for an airport at Badgerys Creek.  

Local residents objected. “Well, it’s going to make Western Sydney a nightmare to live in”, Geoff Brown, a 40-year resident of Penrith and member of the Western Sydney Conservation alliance, 

told the ABC

 at the time. “Growth and a fair go for Western Sydney doesn’t mean trashing the place, doesn't mean turning it into a wasteland of factories and industrial sites”, he said.

Abbott’s successor, Malcolm Turnbull 

manoeuvred

 to make the new airport a government-run project. The state and federal governments provided 

$29 billion in public funding

. Meanwhile Western Sydney’s hospitals, schools and public housing continued to crumble.

Government control enabled a grander development plan, including the construction of a new CBD around the airport, 

Bradfield City

. Part of Bradfield City’s purpose is military support, by “strengthening the defence industrial base through advanced manufacturing and semiconductor packaging”. 

The government ensured businesses had direct input. “It’s not often you get to help design an airport from scratch,” former Qantas CEO Alan Joyce 

celebrated

 in 2019. WSI’s then-CEO 

warmly welcomed

 the freight industry: “Tell us what size facility you need, tell us what technology you want in it and how you want it designed to optimise your productivity”. Construction company Lendlease was another big winner, scoring a 

$644 million contract

 for the airport’s earth works.

Careful messaging trumpeted WSI’s economic benefits to a dubious public, while noise and environmental concerns were addressed through non-binding consultation. Naming the airport after Australia’s youngest female pilot, Nancy Bird Walton, and highlighting Indigenous culture and sustainability in its design, represented an attempt to further head off …

title: Bangladeş'teki eylemlerde yaralanan bir işçi hayatını kaybetti
content:
Fotoğraf: Wasiul Bahar/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 4.0

Bangladeş'te tekstil işçilerinin aylık asgari ücretin artırılması talebiyle düzenlediği protestolara polisin müdahalesi sürerken, Gazipur'da yaralanan bir işçinin kaldırıldığı hastanede hayatını kaybettiği açıklandı.

Polis, işçileri dağıtmak amacıyla göz yaşartıcı gaz, ses bombası ve plastik mermi kullanırken, şu ana kadar eylemlerde onlarca kişi yaralandı.

Bangladeş'te süren protestolar sonrası Gazipur'da 150'den fazla, Savar ve Ashulia sanayi bölgelerinde ise 264 fabrikada üretim faaliyetlerine ara verilmişti. Yaklaşık 4 milyon işçinin çalıştığı Bangladeş hazır giyim sektörü, ülkenin ihracat gelirlerinin yüzde 80'inden fazlasını karşılıyor ve gayri safi yurt içi hasılasının (GSYH) yaklaşık yüzde 10'unu oluşturuyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Jana Hoger
title: Nach Wiedereröffnung von Tötungsstation: Proteste gegen Behördenentscheidung
content:
Zahlreiche Tierschützende gingen vor der Nationalen Behörde für Veterinärwesen und Lebensmittelsicherheit (ANSVSA) in Bukarest auf die Straße. Anlass war die Entscheidung der Behörde, die zuvor geschlossene und durch ein Unternehmen geführte

Tötungsstation

 „Vetmedan“ von Tierarzt Lazaar in Suraia wieder für den Betrieb zuzulassen. Die Einrichtung war zuvor durch erschütternde Bilder und Berichte über die Zustände dort in die Schlagzeilen geraten. Auf den Aufnahmen ist zu sehen, wie Hunde auf grausamste Weise illegal getötet und massiv misshandelt wurden. Die Demonstrierenden forderten deshalb Konsequenzen für die Verantwortlichen und einen grundlegenden Kurswechsel im Umgang mit

heimatlosen Hunden

 in Rumänien.  


Gemeinsam mit der Nationalen Föderation für Tierschutz (FNPA) kritisieren wir von PETA Deutschland die Wiedereröffnung der Einrichtung scharf. Wir sehen darin ein weiteres Beispiel für ein System, das seit Jahren versagt und unzähligen Hunden schlimmstes und unwiederbringliches Leid zufügt.  


Der Fall Vetmedan: Ein Symbol für ein größeres Problem 


Die Zustände im „

Tierheim

“ Vetmedan sorgten in Rumänien für große Empörung. Versteckte Aufnahmen zeigen mangelnde Versorgung der dort untergebrachten

Hunde

, schlechte Haltungsbedingungen und massives Tierleid, auch bei der Tötung. Diese Bilder lösten in der Öffentlichkeit eine Welle der Kritik aus. Für viele Tierfreund:innen ist die Entscheidung zur Wiedereröffnung der Einrichtung deshalb nicht nachvollziehbar. 


Doch der Fall Vetmedan ist nach Ansicht von PETA und der FNPA weit mehr als ein Einzelfall. Er macht auf ein strukturelles Problem aufmerksam, das Rumänien seit Jahrzehnten begleitet: den Umgang mit heimatlosen Hunden und das korrupte System dahinter. 


Über eine Milliarde Euro ausgegeben – und das „Problem“ besteht weiterhin 


Eine von FNPA und PETA ausgewertete Analyse für den Zeitraum von 2001 bis 2025 zeichnet ein alarmierendes Bild: In diesen 25 Jahren wurden schätzungsweise 2,76 Millionen Hunde eingefangen. Rund 1,28 Millionen Tiere starben in Einrichtungen oder wurden getötet. Gleichzeitig flossen etwa 1,01 Milliarden Euro öffentlicher Gelder in das bestehende System.  


Trotz dieser enormen Ausgaben gibt es weiterhin Hunderttausende heimatlose Hunde in Rumänien. Ein klares Zeichen, dass der bisherige Ansatz des Fangens und Töten nicht nur tierquälerisch, sondern auch vollumfänglich gescheitert ist.  


Straßenhunde leiden unter den untragbaren Umständen in Tötungsstationen in Rumänien.


Statt die Ursachen nachhaltig durch tierschutzgerechte Mittel, wie der

Kastration

 anzugehen, wird ein Kreislauf aufrechterhalten, der Jahr für Jahr neue Leben hervorbringt und neues, massives Leid verursacht. 


Wenn Tierleid zum Geschäftsmodell wird 


Im Mittelpunkt der aktuellen Problematik mit heimatlosen Hunden in Rumänien stehen kommerzielle „Tierheime“. 


Viele Unternehmen unterhalten diese sogenannten Tierheime und erhalten öffentliche Gelder für das Einfangen, Unterbringen und Verwalten von Hunden. Dadurch entsteht ein offensichtlicher Interessenkonflikt: Solange weiterhin Hunde auf der Straße leben, fließen auch weiterhin öffentliche Mittel – im großen Stil. 


Das Einfangen und Töten von Hunden ist mittlerweile landesweit zu einem lukrativen Geschäft geworden, welches aus Steuergeldern finanziert wird. Solange ein wirtschaftlicher Anreiz besteht, wird sich auch das „Problem“ der heimatlosen Hunde nicht verändern.  


Aus Sicht des

Tierschutzes

 muss endlich jeder eingesetzte Euro dazu beitragen, die Zahl der heimatlosen Hunde nachhaltig und human dauerhaft durch Kastrationen zu reduzieren. Langfristig spart dies viele öffentliche Gelder ein – und das Leid der Hunde wird auf nahezu Null reduziert. Denn innerhalb von zehn Jahren gäbe es nahezu keine heimatlosen Hunde mehr, wenn in Kastrationen statt in Einfangen und Töten investiert werden würden. 


Heimatlose Hunde entstehen nicht von allein 


Immer wieder wird so getan, als seien Straßenhunde ein eigenes „Phänomen“. Tatsächlich ist der Grund für ihr Leid jedoch immer menschengemacht. 


Unkastrierte Hunde mit und ohne Halter:in vermehren sich dauerhaft unkontrolliert.

Welpen

 werden einfach auf den Straßen entsorgt und ausgesetzt, ohne dass eine langfristige und tierschutzgerechte Lösung gefunden wird. Solange diese Ursachen nicht bekämpft werden, gelangen immer neue Hunde auf die Straßen. 


Aus diesem Grund ist es dringend an der Zeit endlich zu handeln: weg von Fang- …

author: Stelinsky
title: Τρέξε, άνθρωπε, τρέξε #60
content:
Για ακόμη ένα καλοκαίρι οι άθλιες συνθήκες κράτησης στις ελληνικές φυλακές επιδεινώθηκαν ακόμη περισσότερο με τους/τις κρατούμενους/-ες να έχουν να αντιμετωπίσουν τόσο τον υπερπληθυσμό και την έλλειψη ιατροφαρμακευτικής περίθαλψης όσο και τις εξαιρετικά υψηλές θερμοκρασίες.

Στις γυναικείες φυλακές Θήβας, εν μέσω καύσωνα, τουλάχιστον στις 17 και 18 Ιούλη, δεν υπήρχε καν πρόσβαση σε νερό. Περισσότερες από 600 κρατούμενες δεν είχαν νερό για να πλυθούν, να πιούν, να μαγειρέψουν ενώ η διεύθυνση αποποιούνταν κάθε ευθύνη, κάνοντας λόγο για γενικευμένο πρόβλημα ύδρευσης της περιοχής. Χωρίς καμία πρόβλεψη για τέτοιες καταστάσεις, στις 18/07 η διοίκηση “αντιμετώπισε” το πρόβλημα δίνοντας 3 μεγάλα μπουκάλια νερό σε κάθε κρατούμενη, για όλες τις ημερήσιες ανάγκες.

Αντίστοιχη κατάσταση κατήγγειλαν και οι κρατούμενοι στις φυλακές Τρικάλων όπου, εν μέσω καύσωνα, υπήρχε πρόσβαση σε νερό ελάχιστες ώρες ενώ την υπόλοιπη ημέρα το νερό είτε έρεε ελάχιστα είτε καθόλου. Όπως καταγγέλλουν, η διοίκηση ωθεί τους κρατούμενους στην αγορά εμφιαλωμένου νερού και άλλων αγαθών από τις επιχειρήσεις με τις οποίες συνεργάζεται η φυλακή, ενισχύοντας την κερδοφορία τους στις πλάτες των κρατούμενων και δυσχεραίνοντας περαιτέρω την ήδη υποβαθμισμένη διαβίωση για όσους δεν μπορούν να επωμιστούν το κόστος.

Ακόμη ένα χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα των απάνθρωπων συνθηκών διαβίωσης αποτελεί το γεγονός ότι, στις 30 Ιούλη, στις γυναικείες φυλακές Θήβας, μια κρατούμενη που έπασχε από ζάχαρο έχασε την ζωή της. Πρόκειται για έναν ακόμη θάνατο στις ελληνικές φυλακές, ο οποίος οφείλεται στην πλήρη αδιαφορία του κράτους για τις ζωές των κρατουμένων. Την ίδια ημέρα, ως άμεση αντίδραση, οι κρατούμενες σε τρεις από τις πέντε πτέρυγες δημιούργησαν εντάσεις βάζοντας φωτιά σε στρώματα και σεντόνια ενώ προκάλεσαν και φθορές εντός των πτερύγων. Παράλληλα, σε κείμενο που δημοσίευσαν οι κρατούμενες των γυναικείων φυλακών Κορυδαλλού, αναφέρουν ότι, αφού πληροφορήθηκαν τον θάνατο της κρατούμενης στις φυλακές Θήβας λόγω χορήγησης λάθους φαρμάκου, αρνήθηκαν το μεσημεριανό κλείσιμο στους θαλάμους, στην καταμέτρηση, και παρέμειναν έξω.

Στις 27 Αυγούστου 2026, το Ευρωπαϊκό Δικαστήριο Δικαιωμάτων του Ανθρώπου (ΕΔΔΑ), εξέδωσε καταδικαστικές αποφάσεις για δυο σωφρονιστικά καταστήματα της χώρας και πιο συγκεκριμένα τις φυλακές Αγίου Στεφάνου (Πάτρα) και τις φυλακές ανηλίκων Αυλώνα. Η Ελλάδα καταδικάστηκε για παραβίαση του άρθρου 3 της Ευρωπαϊκής Σύμβασης Δικαιωμάτων του Ανθρώπου (ΕΣΔΑ) λόγω των συνθηκών κράτησης στις δυο παραπάνω φυλακές και πιο συγκεκριμένα λόγω του περιορισμένου προσωπικού χώρου των κρατουμένων, ο οποίος υπολείπονταν του κρίσιμου ορίου των 3 τ.μ. ανά έγκλειστο.

Σύμφωνα με το άρθρο 3 της ΕΣΔΑ, η σοβαρή έλλειψη προσωπικού χώρου μέσα στο κελί αποτελεί ιδιαίτερα βαρύ παράγοντα κατά την εξέταση του κατά πόσον οι συνθήκες κράτησης μπορούν να χαρακτηριστούν εξευτελιστικές.

Η κατάσταση του υπερπληθυσμού στις ελληνικές φυλακές δεν αποτελεί περιστασιακό φαινόμενο αλλά είναι αποτέλεσμα της συστηματικής αυστηροποίησης του ποινικού και σωφρονιστικού κώδικα καθώς και της διαχρονικής άρνησης του κράτους για αποσυμφόρηση των φυλακών.

Οι ισχυρισμοί περί απάνθρωπων συνθηκών κράτησης δύσκολα μπορούν να αμφισβητηθούν, όταν καταγράφονται 10 θάνατοι κρατουμένων στις φυλακές Αγίου Στεφάνου το διάστημα Απρίλη – Ιούνη 2026.

Για την συγκεκριμένη υπόθεση και παρότι δόθηκε εντολή για εισαγγελική έρευνα, ιδίως μετά τις δημόσιες καταγγελίες κρατούμενων και συγγενών, τα μέσα προσπάθησαν να αποδώσουν τις αιτίες των θανάτων σε εξαρτήσεις φυλακισμένων από ναρκωτικά. Παράλληλα, εντάθηκε η καταστολή εντός της φυλακής, και όχι η περίθαλψη, με απανωτές εφόδους μπάτσων σε κελιά και δεκάδες μεταγωγές. Στις φυλακές Αγίου Στεφάνου λειτουργεί μονάδα φαρμακευτικά υποβοηθούμενης θεραπείας του ΟΚΑΝΑ, με χορήγηση υποκατάστατων και συγκεκριμένα μεθαδόνης, η οποία αν συνδυαστεί με άλλες ουσίες ή φάρμακα μπορεί να προκαλέσει σοβαρές αλληλεπιδράσεις, δυνητικά θανατηφόρες. Χωρίς καμία εξαίρεση στον κανόνα, η φυλακή λειτουργεί με υποστελεχωμένο ιατρικό προσωπικό και ελλείψεις φαρμάκων. Κατά τις νυχτερινές ώρες, μάλιστα, δεν υπάρχει καν γιατρός ενώ το ιατρείο λειτουργεί υπάλληλος της φυλακής ο οποίος σε περίπτωση έκτακτου περιστατικού, λαμβάνει τηλεφωνικά οδηγίες από τον γιατρό.

Πέρα από τα παραπάνω, οι κρατούμενοι στοιβάζονται σε θαλάμους των 8 ατόμων με μια τουαλέτα, δεν επιτρέπονται οι οικιακές συσκευές μαγειρέματος και συντήρησης, έχοντας σαν μόνη επιλογή το συσσίτιο το οποίο δεν επαρκεί για την κάλυψη των …

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish political prisoner in Iran denied urgent treatment
content:
The Tehran Prosecutor’s Office continues to block Kurdish political prisoner Motalleb Ahmadian’s transfer outside Evin Prison for urgent medical treatment, despite repeated medical warnings over his deteriorating health and serious complications from a cancerous tumour.


Ahmadian, from Baneh, Kurdistan Province, is in his 17th year of imprisonment and suffers from multiple illnesses.


An informed source told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN): “The Legal Medicine Organisation has repeatedly informed the judge overseeing the prison and the Tehran Prosecutor’s Office that, given the deterioration in Motalleb Ahmadian’s health, he must be transferred outside prison as soon as possible so that he can receive treatment for his multiple illnesses, undergo the necessary medical procedures and recover in suitable conditions.”


The source said the prosecutor’s office had nevertheless refused to approve the transfer, heightening concerns about irreversible harm to Ahmadian’s health and the risk to his life.


Ahmadian has undergone several operations to treat complications caused by the cancerous tumour. During these procedures, his gallbladder was completely emptied, and surgeons also operated on parts of his liver and intestines, the source said.


Repeated operations and damage to his digestive system have severely limited the options for further surgery and increased the risks, including the possible loss of bowel control.


The surgery he currently needs is intended to treat complications caused by the tumour and is not directly related to the main tumour operation, said the source, adding that it required urgent medical attention.


In previous years, Ahmadian’s hospital transfers have repeatedly been cancelled, including at least three scheduled transfers. He has also been denied adequate access to medication and specialist care.


The source expressed concern that his history of multiple operations, damage to internal organs, limited surgical options and urgent treatment needs, combined with the prosecutor’s continued refusal to approve his transfer, placed his health and life at increasing risk.


Sources following his case warned that continued denial of timely treatment could lead to his gradual death.


Ahmadian went on hunger strike on 5 May 2025 to protest the Tehran prosecutor’s refusal to suspend his sentence and the denial of medical treatment.


His continued denial of access to specialised medical care has caused him to lose more than 35 kg, leaving him in a critical and alarming condition.


Ahmadian has long highlighted the impact of medical neglect on his deteriorating health. In a letter written in January 2020, he described his worsening health condition, attributing it to the denial of timely medical care. He noted infections in the testicular region and fractures in three vertebrae caused by torture during detention.


He wrote: “Unfortunately, the prison authorities refused to cover the costs of my surgeries and medications. According to the Prisons Organisation’s regulations, these expenses should be borne by the prison, but I had to pay all costs myself. Due to financial constraints, I stopped seeking further treatment.”


Ahmadian was born in Baneh in 1983 and arrested on 5 October 2010.


After eight months in security detention facilities in Sardasht, Saqqez and Sanandaj, where he says he was held in harsh solitary confinement and subjected to severe physical torture, he was sentenced to 30 years in prison and exile to Minab Prison on charges of “enmity against God” (moharebeh).


Over more than 16 years in custody, Ahmadian has been held in prisons in Saqqez and Sanandaj, Rajaei Shahr Prison in Karaj, Evin Prison and Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary. He is currently held in Evin Prison.

author: Henry A. Giroux
title: Global Youth Rising Up Know There’s No Democracy Without Economic Justice
content:
Youth around the world are rising up against capitalism and for democracy.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Young people are taking to the streets across France, Italy, Belgium, India, Serbia, and Albania, refusing to surrender their futures to a capitalist system that has abandoned them or to a politics that Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor have described as “end times fascism.”

These protests are fueled by mounting anger over deteriorating schools, economic insecurity, unaffordable housing, political corruption, and a ruling class increasingly indifferent to the needs and voices of the young. As far right governments in Europe, the United States, and Latin America cancel out a future plagued by endless wars, climate catastrophe, staggering inequality, deepening poverty, and deteriorating public institutions, young people are rethinking the language of politics, resistance, and hope.

A 21-year-old student protesting in Milan captured this spirit of resistance in an interview with Reuters, declaring: “It’s vital to take part in people’s spontaneous movements born from an explosion of rage that made collective action possible.” She added, “I think the worst damage this ruling class has done to my generation is stealing even the ability to imagine a future, to dream.” Rather than address these grievances, governments have increasingly responded with curfews, protest bans, and brutal police repression, treating the democratic aspirations of young people as threats to be crushed rather than demands for justice to be heard.

These uprisings are driven by more than economic grievances. They express a growing refusal to accept the moral and political cruelty of a system that has declared the young disposable. At their core is a recognition that neoliberal capitalism has robbed an entire generation of the promise of a better future and that austerity is class warfare disguised as economic necessity. As reported in Rolling Stone, Mathys Le Coz Ndzié, a 17-year-old Parisian student, noted: “The current government hasn’t managed to give us a clear picture of the future, or the world we’re heading into. So we feel completely lost. … We haven’t been prepared for the world that’s coming. The one they’ve prepared us for no longer exists.” This war on youth is intensified by the destruction of social protections and the rise of governments that increasingly rely on surveillance, criminalization, and police repression to enforce obedience, especially among the poor and racially marginalized.

Yet out of these conditions of abandonment and repression, something more profound is emerging: a moral and political awakening rooted in the struggle for economic justice and a collective refusal to accept a world in which human dignity is sacrificed to private profit, democracy is hollowed out, and the very possibility of imagining and creating a different future is stolen from an entire generation.

Carlotta Magoga, writing in European Democracy Hub, is right in stating that, “From Serbia to Bangladesh and Senegal, young people are becoming a driving force for a more democratic world. … In search of alternative routes, they are developing new forms of civic engagement — through artistic protest, online campaigns and storytelling — and rewriting the rules of political participation.” Through their courageous presence in the streets, they are fashioning a form of activism “as a way to rethink how democracy works.”

For example, in France, students have challenged overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, and a university admissions system that reinforces class inequality. In Italy, students have joined workers in protests over low wages, unaffordable housing, deteriorating public services, and increased military spending. In Genoa, port workers and students have also protested the use of ports for arms shipments. In Serbia, where opposition to government corruption has been central, students have demanded investigations into public contracts, government spending, and the political control of public institutions. These movements do not all embrace an explicitly anti-capitalist agenda, but their demands expose conflicts over who controls public resources, whose interests governments serve, and how economic and political power is organized and maintained.

Capitalism, in one of its more disingenuous moments, celebrates youth rhetorically as the future but denies …

author: EA Leipzig
title: Einladung: Vernetzungstreffen für Angeklagte wegen „Tag-X“
content:
Einladung: Vernetzungstreffen für Angeklagte wegen „Tag-X“


15.11.26 | 12:30 Kennenlernen | Beginn 13 Uhr


Brandstraße 15 – Linxxnet


Leipzig


Wir, der Ermittlungsausschuss Leipzig wollen alle Menschen, die bereits Anklageschriften im Kontext von „Tag-X“ in Leipzig (Aktionen nach der Urteilsverkündung im ersten Antifa-Ost-Verfahren) erhalten haben zu einem weiteren Vernetzungstreffen einladen. Die Treffen finden bereits seit Oktober 2025 statt und wir freuen uns immer über weitere Menschen die sich an einem gemeinsamen, solidarischen und politischen Umgang mit der Repression beteiligen wollen.


Bei dem Treffen wollen wir mit euch den aktuellen Stand abgleichen und uns gemeinsam zu Strategien der Prozessführung und -begleitung austauschen. Wir können über politische Prozessführung reden und besprechen was wir euch an Unterstützung für den anstehenden Prozess anbieten können. Außerdem soll es darum gehen, wie wir eine kritische Öffentlichkeit gegen die geschehene, bestehende und kommende Repression rund um den Tag-X schaffen können.


Es gibt viele Angeklagte und ein kollektiver Umgang mit der Repression ist sehr wichtig. Wir wollen keine:n von euch damit allein lassen!


Außerdem ist es auch juristisch und strategisch wichtig und ratsam, sich in der Prozessstrategie abzustimmen. Ihr steht zwar meist allein vor Gericht, euch werden aber z.T. ähnliche/gleiche Taten im selben Tatkomplex vorgeworfen.


Wir laden euch deshalb zu einem Treffen am 15.11. um 13:00 Uhr im Linxxnet (Brandstr. 15) in Leipzig ein.


Für die Betroffenen, die nicht nach Leipzig reisen können, wird es wieder die Möglichkeit geben online in einem Audio-call via Signal teilzunehmen. Der Einladungslink vom ersten Treffen ist weiterhin gültig. Falls ihr zum ersten Mal an einem der Vernetzungstreffen teilnehmt, könnt ihr schon um 12:30 Uhr für ein Kennenlernen und Update ins Linxxnet kommen.


Ihr könnt gerne auch eine Unterstützungsperson mitbringen.


Falls ihr euch zum ersten mal einklinkt, meldet euch dafür bitte per Mail bei uns, dem EA-Leipzig (ea-leipzig@riseup.net).


Wir sehen uns am 15.11.!


passiert am 15.11.2026

author: Unknown
title: Siyaset, bürokrasi ve finans dünyası: Fon soruşturmasında tutuklu isimler kimdir?
content:
İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığının sermaye piyasalarında gerçekleştirilen işlemlere ilişkin yürüttüğü fon soruşturması, siyaset, bürokrasi, finans ve akademi dünyasından çok sayıda kişiyi kapsayacak şekilde genişledi.


Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ikinci kez adliyede


5 Kasım 2026


Soruşturma kapsamında tutuklananlar arasında daha önce bakanlık, milletvekilliği, büyükelçilik, Merkez Bankası yöneticiliği ve Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) yöneticiliği görevlerinde bulunmuş 12 isim yer alıyor.


Soruşturmanın merkezinde, bazı yatırım fonları ve şirket hisseleri üzerinden gerçekleştirildiği iddia edilen usulsüz işlemler, piyasa manipülasyonu, örgütlü hareket etme ve sermaye piyasası mevzuatına aykırılık suçlamaları bulunuyor.


Fon soruşturmasında, eski AKP'li Bakan Kaya, tutuklandı


6 Kasım 2026


Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya tutuklandı


Soruşturmanın son aşamasında eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı ve eski AKP Genel Başkan Yardımcısı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, 5 Kasım'da İstanbul Adliyesi'nde şüpheli sıfatıyla ifade verdi.


Savcılık, Kaya'yı “Sermaye Piyasası Kanunu'na muhalefet” ve “suç işlemek amacıyla kurulan örgüte üye olma” suçlamalarıyla tutuklama talebiyle sulh ceza hâkimliğine sevk etti.


Hâkimlik, Kaya'nın tutuklanmasına karar verdi.


Savcılığın sevk yazısında, Kaya'nın Özata Denizcilik hisselerindeki işlemlerine ilişkin SPK tarafından hazırlanan rapora yer verildi.


Yazıda, Kaya'nın kamuya açıklanmamış ve yatırımcıların kararlarını etkileyebilecek nitelikte bilgilere sahip olduğu öne sürüldü.


Savcılık, Kaya'nın hisselerini 16 Eylül'de, ilgili fonların tasfiye kararından bir gün önce sattığını ve işlemlerin olağan takas süresinden farklı biçimde gerçekleştirildiğini belirtti.


Kaya ise daha önce verdiği ifadede yatırım kararlarını kendisinin aldığını, herhangi bir yönlendirme veya özel bilgi aktarımı olmadığını savunarak suçlamaları reddetti.


Aynı soruşturma kapsamında ifade veren Kaya'nın eşi İlyas Kaya ile eski SPK Başkanı İbrahim Ömer Gönül hakkında ise imza yükümlülüğü ve yurt dışına çıkış yasağı şeklinde adli kontrol tedbirleri uygulandı.


Fon soruşturması: SPK’nın üst düzey yöneticileri gözaltına alındı


3 Kasım 2026


Tutuklanan 12 isim kim?


Geçmişte kamu kurumlarında ve finans sektöründe görev yapmış şu isimler bulunuyor:


Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya:

Eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı ve eski AKP Genel Başkan Yardımcısı.


Ertan Aydın:

 Eski AKP Ankara Milletvekili ve eski Başbakan Başdanışmanı.


Mustafa Aksu:

 Eski Tarım ve Orman Bakan Yardımcısı.


Korkmaz Enes Ergun:

 Eski Borsa İstanbul Genel Müdürü.


Erkan Kilimci:

 Eski Türkiye Cumhuriyet Merkez Bankası (TCMB) Başkan Yardımcısı.


Abdulkadir Özkan:

Eski Başbakanlık Başdanışmanı; Diyanet İşleri Başkanlığı ve Millî Eğitim Bakanlığında basın müşavirliği görevlerinde bulundu.


Taha Çakmak:

Eski Türkiye Sigorta ve Türkiye Hayat Emeklilik Genel Müdürü.


Gürol Sami Özer:

 Eski Türkiye Sigorta Genel Müdür Yardımcısı.


Erman Çete:

 Eski SPK Daire Başkanı.


Eren Yeşilyurt:

 Eski Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Gelirler Kontrolörü.


Kerem Alkin:

Eski Türkiye'nin Ekonomik İşbirliği ve Kalkınma Örgütü (OECD) Daimî Temsilcisi, büyükelçi ve ekonomi profesörü.


Emre Alkin:

 Ekonomist, akademisyen ve geçmişte kamu görevlerinde bulunmuş isim.


Akın Gürlek fon yolsuzluğu için “devlet mekanizmasına sızan şebeke” dedi


3 Kasım 2026


SPK ve Borsa İstanbul yönetimi


Soruşturma kapsamında Borsa İstanbul'un eski Genel Müdürü Korkmaz Enes Ergun, 31 Ekim'de gözaltına alındı. Ergun, 3 Kasım'da “rüşvet almak” suçlamasıyla tutuklandı.


Aynı gün, eski SPK Başkan Vekili Enver Usca, eski SPK Kurul Üyesi Bülent Murat Haholu, eski SPK Ortaklar Finansmanı Dairesi Başkanı Kürşat Sait Babuçcu ve eski SPK Piyasa Gözetim ve Denetim Daire Başkanı Ercan Urkan'ın da aralarında bulunduğu altı kişi hakkında gözaltı kararı verildi.


Gözaltına alınanlar arasında Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu (BDDK) Uygulama 4. Daire Başkanı Mustafa Alper Taş ile Tera Holding İdari İşler Direktörü Ümit Sincanlı da yer aldı.


Altı kişi, 6 Kasım'da emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından İstanbul Adliyesi'ne sevk edildi.


Fon vurgunu soruşturması: Taha Çakmak dahil 15 kişi tutuklandı, Nusret Altınbaş teslim oldu


24 Ekim 2026


İçişleri Bakanı: 433 şüpheliden 112'si tutuklandı


İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, 7 Kasım'da yaptığı açıklamada, fon soruşturması kapsamında 433 şüpheli hakkında işlem yapıldığını söyledi.


Çiftçi'nin verdiği bilgilere göre 112 kişi tutuklandı …

author: Charlotte Morritt-Jacobs
title: N.W.T. judge commends mother for forgiveness at sentencing hearing for man who killed her son, Deijean Drybones
content:
Justice David Gates commended Maxine Drybones for the maturity, restraint and forgiveness she showed while delivering an oral victim impact statement at the sentencing of the man convicted of killing her son.


Maxine Drybones spoke about the grief her family has carried since Deijean Drybones was killed in Behchokǫ̀ in August 2023. He was 17 years old.


She also told the court she had forgiven the man responsible and hoped he would find healing and peace.


Gates recognized the significance of her words, particularly given the loss she and her family have endured.


On Nov. 6, 2026, in community court in

Behchokǫ̀

, Zakk Lafferty, now 27, was sentenced to life in prison for second-degree murder. He must serve at least 10 years before becoming eligible to apply for parole. Eligibility does not mean he will automatically be released.


The case went to trial for the first time in October 2025, but the jury was unable to reach a unanimous decision. Gates declared a mistrial, meaning the Crown would have to bring the case before another jury.


Lafferty was tried again in July 2026. A Yellowknife jury found him guilty of second-degree murder, nearly three years after the teenager was killed.


What happened the night Deijean died


Deijean was stabbed in the early morning hours of Aug. 4, 2023, at a home in Behchokǫ̀. The court heard that a group of young people had been drinking together at the house.


Earlier in the evening, Lafferty had become involved in a physical altercation with another person. Deijean recorded part of that fight on his phone.


During the altercation, Lafferty lost his phone and suffered an injury to his right eye.


The Crown’s case was that Lafferty later returned to the home looking for his phone. Prosecutors argued that Deijean was stabbed after Lafferty confronted him about it, believing Deijean was responsible for the earlier assault.


Deijean was taken to the Behchokǫ̀ health centre and then transported to Stanton Territorial Hospital in Yellowknife, where he died shortly before 6 a.m. from a single stab wound to the chest.


The four other people who were in the home that morning testified during the trials. They had been drinking and told the court they had difficulty remembering what happened.


Police never recovered the weapon used in the stabbing. Investigators also did not find Deijean’s DNA on Lafferty’s shirt or hands, evidence that became part of the defence’s challenge to the investigation.


Lafferty’s lawyer argued that RCMP had focused too narrowly on him as a suspect and failed to adequately consider other possibilities. Lafferty maintained he had gone home after the earlier fight.


Deijean, an enthusiastic dene handgames player since the age of five, competed in tournaments across Denendeh. Photo: Maxine Drybones.


Remembering Deijean


In an interview with APTN News, Maxine recalled the joy she and her husband felt after having three girls and finding out they would have a son.


She remembered Deijean as a kind-hearted young man who cared deeply about his friends and family.


“My son’s kind-hearted and he had a lot of friends. He had a heart for everyone. He did not judge and he did not bully anyone,” she said.


She described her son’s empathetic side, someone who intuitively knew when someone was struggling and would take action, going to see that person simply to sit beside them.


“They don’t even have to say anything. He will feel them and he’ll just go to the house and just sit beside them and not say anything,” she said.


Deijean was protective of his sisters, Maxine said. She also lamented how much he would have loved spending time with his nieces and nephews who were born after his death.


“He would have been a great uncle to my grandkids,” she said.


The family moved to Whatì when Deijean was five. Maxine said he quickly developed a love for Dene hand games, drawn in by the sound of the drums. She remembered taking him to games and tournaments whenever she could.


In the courtroom, she wore a shirt with a photograph of Deijean playing at a hand games tournament in Whatì.


More than three years after his death, Maxine said she has learned to live with the loss while supporting her other children.


“You cannot go back and fix things that’s already been done. You just have to look forward in order for you to be strong and just let it go and how to deal with it and how to live with it,” she said.


She credited her faith and the prayers of her family …

author: Unknown
title: Lilia Folt - On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness
content:
Author

: Lilia Folt

Title

: On Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness

Date

: September 27

th

, 2026

Notes

: Originally published in

Dissonant Times

, a grassroots journalism and counter-info project from the Willamette Valley of Oregon.

Source

: Dissonant Times, Retrieved on 11/5/2026 from https://dissonanttimes.org/anarchic-reflections-on-anti-surveillance-mindfulness/


 Surveillance has become a ubiquitous feature of everyday life in America. Cameras watch us from businesses and homes, from bus stops, from cars, from traffic lights. Bluetooth trackers ping our smartphones as we pass by, mapping our movements. The phones themselves illuminate our paths through society by continuously pinging cell towers, providing our cell providers our location data, information that is only a subpoena away, if that. In countless ways, we’ve been made to both passively accept and actively participate in our own surveillance. This vast complex of surveillance doesn’t just gather information about us, it also shapes our behaviors, temperaments, and ways of moving through the world. Surveillance molds us down to the level of subjective, sensory, embodied experience. At that same level we can begin to shake off its hold on us and reclaim ourselves. For that, I am offering a practice I’m calling “anti-surveillance mindfulness,” a form of walking meditation that builds mindful awareness of surveillance cameras. This practice, if taken up consistently, opens onto a broader project of transforming our relationship to the places we live in, a project that itself naturally blossoms into materially transforming public space, as self expands to world in the moment-by-moment practice of mindfulness.


Anti-Surveillance Mindfulness


 Readers may or may not be familiar with the Panopticon. Designed by 18

th

 century English liberal Jeremy Bentham, the Panopticon was a model for an institutional building designed so that a single prison guard can watch all the inmates from a central watch tower. The inmates, meanwhile, cannot tell whether or not they are being watched, and therefore could be watched at any moment. To quote Bentham:


 The more constantly the persons to be inspected are under the eyes of the persons who should inspect them, the more perfectly will the purpose of the establishment have been attained. (...) This being impossible, the next thing to be wished for is, that, at every instant, seeing reason to believe as much, and not being able to satisfy himself to the contrary, he should

conceive

 himself to be so.


 A lot has changed since the 1700’s, but the disciplinary paradigm of surveillance has remained the same. If anything, it has expanded beyond specific institutions to encompass much of society.


 There are cameras everywhere, and we are being watched, and while we are aware of this, we tend to see it as normal and unremarkable, an inevitability we must resign ourselves to. Consciousness of being surveilled fades into the background, becoming a constant assumption of being watched that we internalize. This surveillance consciousness is running us all the more effectively because it is not distinct, because it is

un

conscious. That is why the first step in anti-surveillance mindfulness is becoming conscious of surveillance.


 Mindfulness is at the same time a means and an end, the seed and the fruit. When we practice mindfulness in order to build up concentration, mindfulness is a seed. But mindfulness itself is the life of awareness: the presence of mindfulness means the presence of life, and therefore mindfulness is also the fruit. — Thích Nhất Hạnh,

The Miracle of Mindfulness


 “Mindfulness” is a practice originating in various sects of Buddhism. The mindfulness practices and concepts I’m familiar with have largely been within the school of Zen Buddhism

[1]

.


 The classic mindfulness practice is watching the breath, and that is a great starting point. Take a breath in, the air entering through your nose, your stomach and chest softly expanding as you inhale. Then exhale through the mouth, the stomach and chest settling back down, gently exhaling for a little longer than your inhale. Repeat this several times, deepening your breaths slightly. From there, start to check in with your body. Notice how it feels to be sitting down, or to be standing if you are standing; notice how it feels to be holding this piece of paper, holding your phone, or looking at your computer, however it is that you are reading …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Air Creebec hit by administrative data breach affecting employees and passengers
content:
Air Creebec, a regional Quebec airline owned by the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee, reported a data breach Wednesday affecting both customers and staff.

In a press release, the company announced “an unauthorized intrusion targeting some of its administrative systems.”

The release stresses that the breach did not compromise any systems associated with aircraft, flight operations or flight safety, noting the company’s administrative systems were not connected with aircraft and flight systems, which it said operate independently.

“Initial findings indicate that administrative files were exfiltrated,” states the release. “These files may contain personal information relating mainly to current and former employees, as well as passengers. Others may also contain operational, administrative or financial information related to customers and partners. The review is ongoing.”

Based in the airport of Val d’Or in the Abitibi-Témiscamingue region of western Quebec, roughly 520 kilometres northwest of Ottawa, Air Creebec offers flights to 16 destinations in Quebec and Ontario. The company’s fleet consists of 21 Dash-8 turboprop regional airliners, along with one ATR 72 turboprop air-freighter for cargo, and carries 200,000 passengers per year.

Cybersecurity experts assessing damage

Air Creebec director for Marketing and Business Development Edward Trahan said the breach was identified in October after which company officials immediately brought in cybersecurity experts to analyze the situation.

“They’re currently evaluating what’s going on and what the breach actually contained,” Trahant told APTN News. “The experts are still conducting their review, so there’s no numbers [of victims] at this time that we can give.”

He added that for security reasons, he was not presently willing to name the cybersecurity team currently helping with post-breach recovery.

He said because the attack was designed to go undetected it was hard to determine the date upon which it began, and for how long attackers were able to access Air Creebec’s systems prior to being discovered.

“What I can assure you of is that as soon as [we were] made aware of [it], we acted immediately and did not wait.”

At the moment, Trahant said the attack appeared to have stolen information “related to our employees, past employees too, and maybe even our passengers.”

“But it’s hard to confirm at the moment.”

Company will contact affected parties

He added that a priority for Air Creebec is contacting every one of their staff or customers whose information has been compromised, which cybersecurity experts would undertake to carry out as soon as possible.

“A part of what the cybersecurity experts are doing for us is gathering information to [determine] what kind of protection packages we can provide to people that had their information involved,” said Trahan.

“Those people will be directly contacted in probably the next few days — [but] probably more like [the next] day — about what package they will receive, what protection they’re going to have and how long it’s going to last.”

Trahan said the cybersecurity team was currently in the process of securing all possible intrusion points, but he said the nature of cybersecurity is that 100 per cent protection is impossible.

“It’s just the way of the world,” he said, “but they are closing every possible way to get in and they are getting to the very end of that. As for how they got in initially, we don’t know yet and I don’t want to speculate while the review is still underway.”

Trahan said he and Air Creebec are taking the situation very seriously and are committed to supporting all those affected, and the company said it would be in touch with affected people to offer “appropriate protective measures,” including the possibility of credit-monitoring and identity-protection services.

“Those services will be based on the nature of the information exposed and the risks that were identified,” he said. “So individuals that are eligible to receive this protection will be informed directly and will be given a list of steps to follow in the very near future.”

Jesse joined APTN as a producer after 16 years as a print and web journalist. During seven of those years, he covered the Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee for community newsmagazine The Nation. Jesse’s writing on Indigenous issues has also appeared in Canadian Geographic, the Toronto Star, the Rover, The Eastern Door, Metro, and the Huffington Post.

author: EDRi
title: EU governments call it ‘simplification,’ but their Data Omnibus deal considerably weakens our rights
content:
EU governments have agreed on their position on the Digital Omnibus, retaining changes that threaten fundamental rights to privacy and data protection. With negotiations moving to the European Parliament, MEPs must reject the proposed weakening of GDPR safeguards for AI and pseudonymised data, protect individual rights, and defend ePrivacy against new tracking exemptions. Genuine simplification should make our rights easier to exercise and enforce, not give companies more freedom to exploit our data.

When the European Commission presented its Digital Omnibus in November 2025, it promised to simplify Europe’s digital rules without weakening fundamental rights. Yet, as EDRi and others warned at the time, a majority of its proposals, particularly those regarding General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and ePrivacy, went far beyond reducing administrative burdens. They are part and parcel of a broad deregulatory wave that is devouring most of our rights and safeguards in the name of empty promises of competitiveness and sovereignty.

On 21 October 2026, EU governments agreed on their negotiating position, which has timidly corrected some of the Commission’s most questionable choices, but has mainly endorsed changes that could make exploiting personal data easier while making abuses even harder to challenge.

The result is a deal that weakens important safeguards and makes redress harder. There is also little evidence that weakening these protections will improve Europe’s competitiveness. Some changes may instead reinforce the advantages of Big Tech companies that already control and abuse enormous volumes of information about us and the people around us.

One of the most worrying changes concerns the use of personal data for AI.

The Council retained a dedicated provision, Article 88bis (Article 88c in the Commission’s proposal), explicitly recognising the possibility of relying on the GDPR’s ‘legitimate interest’ legal basis to use personal data when developing or operating AI systems. Under the GDPR, companies can already use this legal basis in certain circumstances, provided they demonstrate a legitimate interest, prove that processing is necessary, and establish that people’s rights do not override that interest.

The Council clarifies that AI development does not automatically constitute a legitimate interest and that existing conditions still apply. But if legitimate interests can already justify certain AI processing, why introduce a special provision?

The concern is that Article 88bis could tilt the legitimate interest assessment in favour of AI companies, giving preferential treatment to a vaguely defined set of technologies primarily owned by autocracy-supporting billionaires, regardless of the exact purpose for which our personal data is going to be used. As recent legal analysis explains, this risks changing how the existing balancing test between legitimate interest and data protection safeguards is applied, even without formally removing its requirements.

Companies could invoke this legislative endorsement to justify extensive data reuse, even when people never reasonably expected their information to be used for AI training. And who benefits most? The same dominant Big Tech corporations that have spent decades accumulating the most intimate information about billions of people.

The Council also retains an exception for sensitive personal data appearing incidentally in AI datasets (proposed Article 9(2)(k) and 9(2)), including information revealing health, political opinions or religious beliefs. Companies must try to avoid collecting and, where collected, remove such data, but may retain them under safeguards when removal proves technically impossible or requires manifestly disproportionate effort.

These conditions might look important, but risk turning difficulties in cleaning datasets into a justification for retaining highly sensitive information. In opaque AI systems, verifying whether such data have genuinely been isolated may often be impossible. In this regard we should bear in mind that companies are mandated to protect our data and rights, and technical choices should not determine how far our fundamental rights extend.

There is some, even if limited, good news. The Council has rejected the Commission’s attempt to rewrite the GDPR’s definition of personal data in Article 4.1 and dropped its proposed Article 41a, which would have allowed the Commission to specify when certain …

author: Scott Timcke
title: The Stories Shaping Africa’s AI Future
content:
In the boardrooms of Addis Ababa and the tech hubs of Nairobi, a new worldmaking project is underway. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of the central arenas where African states negotiate their position in an unequal global order. To speak of “AI in Africa” is not simply to describe the arrival of a technology, but to encounter a set of competing discursive frames through which political desires, developmental ambitions, ethical claims, and governance priorities are translated into technical agendas. As national strategies and regional protocols are rolled out, what comes into view is a struggle over how Africa is imagined within this machine age, and what kinds of futures that imagination makes thinkable.


These frames are not simply different ways of describing a new technology. They are competing scripts for what Africa is, what AI is for, and who ought to shape its future. Some cast the continent as a site of leapfrogging and renewal; others as a zone of exposure, extraction, sovereignty, moral repair, or improvised adaptation. Each brings some actors and possibilities into focus while pushing others to the margins. That is why the issue is not only what AI means for Africa, but what pictures of Africa are being called into view through AI discourse.


The first terrain is shaped by promise and protection. One of the most pervasive registers is promissory. In the African renaissance 2.0 frame, visible in the

AU Continental AI Strategy

, AI appears as a

leapfrogging

 device through which Africa can bypass the chokepoint of traditional industrialization and enter prosperity through technical modernization. Here, the ethical subject is the developmental state or planner charged with delivering growth, inclusion, and renewal. What comes into view is capacity, competitiveness, and beneficial transformation. What recedes from view are the historical and political-economic conditions that make acceleration so attractive in the first place: debt, infrastructural dependence, uneven ownership, and the possibility that AI may deepen rather than overcome inherited asymmetries.


Running alongside this is a protective register. In this vulnerability frame, Africa is not late but exposed to surveillance, bias, exclusion, and systems introduced into settings where safeguards are weak and redress is limited. As the

CIVICUS report on AI surveillance in Africa

 suggests, the issue is not only future risk but already existing forms of technologically mediated harm. The ethical subject here is the harm-bearing population—the data subject, precarious worker, surveilled citizen, and linguistically marginal user most likely to absorb the costs of badly governed AI. This frame is ethically indispensable because it foregrounds rights, harm, and institutional fragility, including the uneven but growing architecture of data protection on the continent. Its limit, however, is that it can cast Africa chiefly as a site to be protected rather than one from which technological futures are actively contested and shaped.


A second terrain is shaped by structure and sovereignty. Alongside these promissory and protective registers sits a more structural critique. In the

anti-colonial frame

, AI appears as a socio-technical order built through unequal material relations: not only data extraction, but also mineral supply chains, outsourced labor, environmental degradation, foreign-owned infrastructures, and asymmetrical control over the institutions that govern digital life. From this perspective, Africa is not outside the AI order looking in; it is already deeply inserted into it, though often on subordinated terms. The ethical subject is the dispossessed worker, community, or polity whose labor, resources, and data are drawn into AI systems while ownership and value are captured elsewhere. What becomes visible is the political economy of AI—an approach that makes it harder to sustain the comforting idea that Africa’s main problem is simply one of readiness or delayed entry. But the frame has limits. In foregrounding dispossession, it can flatten internal differentiation, externalize agency too completely, and become so totalizing that the uneven realities of negotiation and strategic inhabitation recede from view.


The sovereignty frame shifts the question from extraction to control: AI is cast as a problem of authority over infrastructure, procurement, standards, and rulemaking, a concern visible in South Africa’s

National …

author: Dinah Gardner
title: The Other China We Need to Talk About
content:
WHAT IF I told you that there was a chance—not a very high chance, but a real chance nonetheless—that if you visited the People’s Republic of China today you might be kidnapped, blindfolded, driven to a specialized facility and subjected to six months of psychological torture. All on the orders of the state.

It sounds unbelievable, doesn’t it?

But this is what happened to at least several dozen foreign citizens in recent years. It is what happened to American scholar Min Zin this past June, when he landed in Yunnan province on the invitation of a Chinese academic institution to attend a conference. And it is also what happened to half a dozen people who appear in the latest edition of the book The People’s Republic of the Disappeared, which we just published on 28 October.

This important book is a collection of mostly first-person stories that expose the psychological horrors of being held in the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) feared secret detention system called Residential Surveillance at a Designated Location (RSDL). The system permits police to hold an individual in complete isolation, no contact with family or lawyers, to be interrogated for hours at will.

The individual is under 24-hour guard: this includes being watched all day every day, all night every night, whether you are asleep, sitting quietly in your cell or even on the toilet. The CCP intentionally uses RSDL to strip away every last shred of human dignity. RSDL is designed to break a person’s will to extract a confession for crimes imagined by the state

For more than a decade, the CCP has used RSDL against its own people, in particular human rights defenders. It is now increasingly using it against foreign citizens to exert its will across borders and as a kind of hostage diplomacy. Michael Kovrig, a former Canadian diplomat who wrote the foreword to this edition, is one of its most well-known examples.

In editing the stories for this book, I was struck again and again by how similar everyone’s experience was. This speaks to the uniformity of the RSDL system:

The removal of the temporal world. “There are no clocks in RSDL” is the title of Australian TV anchor Cheng Lei’s chapter. She would guess and count breaths to keep track of time.

The removal of the physical world. There are no windows in RSDL or they are covered in thick blackout curtains. Japanese scholar Hideji Suzuki cried when he was granted 15 minutes of sunlight, the only time in his seven months’ incarceration when he was allowed to see the sky.

The removal of yourself. Michael Kovrig noted: “There are no mirrors—not even the reassurance of seeing your own face.” Chinese activist Li Qiaochu writes how she was simply called “target”.

Filling the space left by these absences was a current of fear. Endless rules, the lack of privacy yet total isolation (guards were forbidden from talking to prisoners), reduced nutrition, sleep deprivation, lack of fresh air, and the padded suicide-proofed walls. Several of the detainees wrote while they could never see outside their RSDL facility, at nighttime they would often hear gunfire or the barking of dogs.

“In my mentally exhausted state, the sounds of gunfire would constantly startle me and even cause me to imagine that I was about to be executed,” wrote Taiwanese human rights activist Lee Ming-che.

But something else struck me as I read through their testimonies. However harrowing these stories of suffering are, they are also evidence of human resilience in the face of horror.

Cheng Lei writes about how she would escape into her mind, translating poems, reliving her former TV interviews and making up stories in her head. Similarly, Michael Kovrig meditated, sang songs to himself, and remembered past moments in his life, as if it was a recording playing in his mind.

“I learned to meditate on the movies I had watched and the poems and novels I had read,” wrote Li Qiaochu. “Those precious memories allowed me to gradually filter out the brainwashing, to preserve my vitality and to keep myself from being transformed into their machine.”

Feedback from earlier editions informed us that rights activists use the Chinese editions of The People’s Republic of the Disappeared to prepare for and strengthen their mental resolve and courage in case one day they too are taken into RSDL. Knowing that others have gone through this and come out the other side can be an immense help. It’s for this reason that the Chinese edition of this book will be …

title: Deep Dive: Minnesota 15 Case Reveals Range of Pervasive Surveillance
content:
St. Paul, MN – Looking closely at court filings around the “Minnesota 15” prosecution has revealed vast patterns of surveillance by federal agents, in Minnesota and beyond. We took a closer look at the summer’s largest set of filings, 30 main exhibits and several subsequent ones, to map out just how undercover operations,

facial recognition

, pole cameras, and other tactics played out. The project gives a sharp illustration of the cutting edge of America’s modern, lavishly funded surveillance state.


We did an in-depth

webinar-style recording

 going through all of

these defense exhibits

. Covering hundreds of pages of evidence, it’s around 100 minutes long. While it is an almost overwhelming level of detail, it is worth checking out to get a glimpse at both the breadth and the depth of how this campaign worked.


Watch the full report on

Vimeo

 or

YouTube

.


The prosecution of the Minnesota 15

(United States v. Sant, et al)

 has been playing out through the summer — one of the more high-profile politicized court cases Minnesota has seen in years. Unicorn Riot has

interviewed many defendants

 about their experiences getting raided.


ICE in Minnesota: 2025-2026


Minnesota 15 Coverage


Federal prosecutor Brian W. Lynch, who

marched masked at the January 6 riot in Washington, DC,

 was integral to the Minnesota grand jury presentation of “The Conspiracy,” a foundational component of the Minnesota 15 prosecution.


Kieran F. Knutson, the president of Communication Workers of America Local 7250, told Unicorn Riot that the surveillance which targeted his union’s finances was part of an effort to “map out the resistance to ICE”:


“In my opinion the federal investigations should be seen as both an attack on and an effort to map out the resistance to ICE in Minnesota including the trade unions.


The Feds have a broad understanding of the different facets of the resistance and they have used these investigations as a means to map out the specific organizations, influential organizers, and networks of solidarity and collaborative activity.


The release of documents shows that this is not limited to investigating incidents involving ICE agents and protesters but is expansive to include unions and community groups that sponsored and organized the January 23rd Day of Truth & Freedom with No Work, No School, and No Shopping, including their finances.


This investigation started concurrent with the launching of Operation Metro Surge revealing its purpose as a counter-insurgency operation to, in the words of Commander Greg Bovino, ‘pacify this place’.


The unions – as a part of the active resistance to the illegal and deadly ICE operation – are an important target for the Federal government.”


Kieran F. Knutson, President CWA Local 7250


Federal Reserve wire transfer systems searched for CWA union, Sunrise Movement, and other data between January 1, 2023 and March 29, 2026.


Anti-Left Campaign Centered on Minnesota


Ali Winston in Wired pointed out that

ICE is running one of the largest anti-left surveillance campaigns in U.S. history

, and Minnesota is at the heart of it. By his count, 115 ICE-HSI agents were involved in the Minnesota 15 case, including several high-profile agents from other states. He also found a

spinoff surveillance campaign in Chicago

 in April 2026.


As Winston noted, Unicorn Riot’s previous

exposure of the confidential ICE-HSI Undercover Operations Handbook

 helps decode the concepts around their operation.


Attorneys for the Minnesota 15 filed documents showing that Operation Keyhole was a “certified undercover” (CUC) operation. On September 9, this forced

Minnesota U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen to disclose Keyhole has been in effect since late 2008

. “77 separate criminal investigations” were approved under Keyhole.


As of June 2026, five investigations including Whipple Shield were being supplied under Keyhole, according to Rosen. The point of including Operation Whipple Shield and Puppet Master in Keyhole was to enable “the use of CUC Keyhole funds to provide investigative support, such as funding the deployment of personnel and the acquisition of necessary equipment,” according to Rosen.
