title: İklimi yok edenler iklimi konuşuyor
content:
Özlem Songül Abayoğlu [email protected]

Türkiye’nin ev sahipliğinde Antalya’da düzenlenecek Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) İklim Değişikliği Çerçeve Sözleşmesi’nin 31. Taraflar Konferansı COP31, bugün devlet başkanları ve holding patronlarının katılımıyla başlayacak.

Bugün (9 Kasım) başlayan zirvenin ilk gününün teması ‘gıda, tarım ve sağlık’ olacak. İklim destekçilerinde ormanları kesip maden açan Cengiz Holdingin, Akbelen Ormanı’na kömür madeni kuran Limak ve IC Holdingin, Petrol rafineleri kuran Koç Holdingin bulunduğu zirvenin ilk gününde “gıda, tarım ve sağlık” başlığı tartışılacak.

10 Kasım’da meralara ve tarım arazilerine enerji santralleri kuran Sabancı ve Kalyon Holdingin de ortaklar listesinde bulunduğu zirvenin ikinci gününün konusu da enerji güvenliği, şebeke altyapısı ve elektrifikasyon süreçlerini kapsayan “enerji ve ulaşım” olacak. Bu kapsamda, Eylem Gündemi’nde yer alan ve ‘35’e 35’ olarak da adlandırılan küresel elektrifikasyon taahhüdü duyurulacak. Buna göre Sabancı ve Kalyon; ulaşım, bina, sanayi ve tarım gibi sektörlerde elektriğe geçişin hızlandırılması, yüzde 23-24 seviyesinde bulunan elektrifikasyon oranının 2035’te yüzde 35’e çıkarılmasını hedefleyen başlığa katılacak.

11 Kasım’da ise öncelik alanı olarak belirlenen sıfır atık teması ele alınacak, sıfır atık yaklaşımını destekleyen iki girişim, liderler düzeyinde tanıtılacak. Eurostat ve Greenpeace verilerine göre; 2025 yılında Avrupa Birliği (AB) üyesi ülkelerden toplam 503 bin ton plastik atık ithal eden Türkiye’nin gündeminde ise sıfır atık girişimi olması bekleniyor.

12 Kasım’da ise liderler zirvesinin ikinci ve son günü yapılacak ve ‘dirençli şehirler ve yapılı çevre’ teması üzerinde yoğunlaşılacak. İklime dirençli altyapı, binalar ve kentsel planlama gibi başlıklar ele alınacak ve binalarda enerji kullanım yoğunluğunun en az yüzde 25 azaltılması hedefi gündeme getirilecek. Kentsel dönüşümün Türkiye’de dönüşümün ada bazlı kamusal planlamalar yerine, çoğunlukla parsel bazlı ve müteakip kazancına göre ilerlediği ve eski mahalle sakinlerinin yerine lüks konut ve rezidansların üretildiği bilinirken “dirençli kentlerin” toplantıda nasıl ele alınacağı da merak konusu.

13 Kasım’daki etkinliklerin teması ise “finans ve ticaret” olarak belirlendi. Toplantıda İklim Uygulama Köprüsü (BRIDGE) gündeme gelecek. Mekanizma, ülkelerin iklim ve kalkınma önceliklerini finansmana hazır proje portföylerine dönüştürerek hedefler ile uygulama arasındaki açığı kapatmayı amaçlıyor. Ancak Vakfının açıklamasına göre İlk COP’un gerçekleştirildiği 1995’te atmosferdeki karbondioksit yoğunluğu 360.82 ppm’di. Kyoto Protokolü’nün kabul edildiği 1997’de miktar 363.73 ppm’e, Paris Anlaşması’nın kabul edildiği 2015’te 400.83 ppm’e çıktı. 2025 yılında ise 427.35 ppm’e ulaştı. İlk COP toplantısından bugüne 30 yılda atmosferdeki karbondioksit yoğunluğu yaklaşık yüzde 18 arttı.

14 Kasım’da; 66 çocuğun 2026’nın ilk 9 ayında çalışırken öldüğü, 2025-2026 yıllarında 37 çocuğun MESEM’de çalışırken öldüğü, 10 bin çocuğun ise MESEM’de çalışırken yaralandığı Türkiye’de COP31 kapsamında “çocuk, gençlik, eğitim ve beceriler” teması kapsamında etkinlikler düzenlenecek.

15 Kasım’da COP31 toplantılarına ara verilecek. 16 Kasım’da ‘bilim, sanayi ve teknoloji’ teması, 17 Kasım’da ‘okyanus, denizler, doğa ve arazi kullanımı (Rio sinerjisi)’ teması, 18 Kasım’da ‘insani ve sosyal kalkınma’ başlığı, 19 Kasım’da ise ‘İmece: Uygulamanın güçlendirilmesi’ teması kapsamında etkinlikler düzenlenecek.

14-18 Kasım’da Antalya’da COP31 ile aynı dönemde Halkların İklim Zirvesi düzenlenecek. Glasgow ve Belém’deki “People’s COP” buluşmalarının devamı olan zirvede, kadınlar, işçiler, köylüler ve yaşam alanlarını savunucuları bir araya gelecek. Destekçiler arasında ise Türk Tabipleri Birliği, Uluslararası Af Örgütü, DİSK’e bağlı sendikalar ve Greenpeace Türkiye bulunuyor. 14 Kasım’da planlanan yürüyüş ve mitingle başlayacak zirvede, 15 Kasım doğanın hakları, 16 Kasım fosilden çıkış ve enerji demokrasisi, 17 Kasım demokrasi ve barış, 18 Kasım’da ise gıda egemenliği ve agroekoloji konuşulacak. Programda yerel çevre mücadeleleri, sağlık ve insan hakları gibi konular yer alırken, Ege Çevre ve Kültür Platformu (EGEÇEP) 15 Kasım’da Aliağa’daki ekolojik yıkımı, Peace Boat 17 Kasım’da savaşların çevresel bedelini değerlendirecek. 18 Kasım’da ise Türk Tabipleri Birliği iklim krizinin sağlık etkilerini, Uluslararası Af Örgütü çevre savunucularının adil geçişteki rolünü tartışacak.

author: Unknown
title: A border built with water: Six dams in succession
content:
There are six dams along a stretch of just 45–50 kilometers on the Ortasu (Rubozik) Stream, located on the border between Northern Kurdistan (Bakur) and Southern Kurdistan (Başur). Under normal circumstances, dams should either not be built because of the damage they cause to the ecological balance, or should only be constructed following an Environmental Impact Assessment for irrigation, flood prevention and electricity generation. However, these six dams serve a somewhat different purpose. The 2007 activity report of the State Hydraulic Works (DSI) states that their function is entirely security-related. This represents an unprecedented category worldwide, a new type of dam.


A look at the map reveals that all six dams have been built along a single stream. Each has its own tender, dam structure and reservoir. Yet for those living in the valley, they are all part of the same story: villages whose roads have been cut off, whose pastures and farmland have been lost, and whose residents face the winter fearing landslides and floods.


The fundamental question that needs to be asked is: Why does the Turkish state use dams so extensively as a security instrument in Kurdistan?


'Security dams': A new category


A report published in the newspaper Hürriyet on 26 October 2011 clearly revealed why these six dams were being constructed. The report emphasized that the dams were intended to "solve the problem" by flooding caves used by guerrillas and people engaged in cross-border trade. The deep valleys of Aynatepe, Gürbül Mountain, Bezenik Mountain and Düğün Mountain, which form the border stretching from the Qilaban (Uludere) district of Şırnak (Şirnex) to the Çelê (Çukurca) district of Hakkari (Colemêrg), contained strategic locations. Guerrilla transit routes also passed through these valleys.


A project tendered in 2008 and prepared by the DSI for "energy storage" along the borders with Iraq and Iran included a total of 11 dams. Seven were located in Şırnak (Silopi, Şırnak, Uludere, Ballı, Kavşaktepe, Musatepe and Çetintepe), while four were in Hakkari (Gölgeliyamaç, Çocuktepe, Beyyurdu and Aslandağ).


Reports based on a DSI map obtained by the press in July 2009 stated that the reservoirs would flood hundreds of caves and crossing points used by the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), cut off logistical support and prevent infiltration and smuggling.


The military and strategic function of the dams


The primary rationale behind the construction of these dams was a strategy of territorial control. The deep valleys along the border formed natural corridors for the PKK's logistical and shelter networks. By filling these valleys, the reservoirs physically block transit routes while also restricting military movement in the region.


This represents a concrete shift from the tactics of the 1990s, characterized by "burn the villages, dry up the water," toward an approach based on "transforming the terrain to prevent operations." The dams reinforce the border with a natural barrier while simultaneously reshaping the region's socioeconomic structure. However, the long-term ecological and social costs of this strategy have not been adequately discussed in public.


Reshaping geography in the name of 'securitization'


Rather than resolving the Kurdish question through peaceful means, the state sees no problem with reshaping the region's geography and ecosystem and displacing its inhabitants through securitization policies. Dams built in succession are turning artificial borders into natural barriers.


The term "security dam" appeared in the DSI's 2007 report, although officials later stated that these dams were being constructed for irrigation and energy production. While official discourse presents them as "energy and irrigation investments," the experiences of villagers in the region do not correspond to this narrative.


It has been reported that the canals and distribution networks required for irrigation have largely not been constructed, while electricity generation remains limited to a total installed capacity of 15 megawatts. This capacity reportedly represents just 0.044 percent of the total installed capacity of hydroelectric power plants in Turkey.


Meanwhile, the risks of landslides, water leakage and flooding caused by the dams pose serious dangers to local communities. This situation reinforces criticism that the dams' primary function is not "development" but "keeping the region under control."

author: Matt Simon
title: Extreme Flooding in US Southwest May Foreshadow a Disastrous El Niño Winter
content:
Historically, the phenomenon boosts precipitation in the southern US. This may be a glimpse at the pain to come.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Southwest just got way too much of a good thing. Last weekend, a ferocious storm inundated communities and killed at least four people. Though precipitation is an essential component of Arizona’s desert climate, the state got two or three months’ worth of it in just a few days — far more than human infrastructure could handle all at once. Since September 20, an astonishing 28.84 inches of rain has fallen on Clovis, New Mexico, compared to its historical average of just 3.3 inches.

“This weekend was just adding more on the rough times that those communities in Southwest Colorado and Arizona and Utah and New Mexico have been having recently,” said Russ Schumacher, director of the Colorado Climate Center at Colorado State University, who’s also the state climatologist. “I think the El Niño connection is pretty clear.”

Indeed, that band of warm water in the Pacific could be priming much of the southern United States for a winter of increased precipitation, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s seasonal outlook. “Could an event like this have happened in a non-El Niño year?” asked Michael A. Crimmins, a climatologist at the University of Arizona. “It could have, but it would have been a lot harder to pull all of the ingredients together at the same time, and would have been a lot less likely.”

The looming problem this winter is heat, oddly enough. The unfolding El Niño is already the strongest on record, and it could get stronger still in the next few months. Although that amounts to just a handful of extra degrees in the Pacific, it injects a tremendous amount of energy into the atmosphere, scrambling weather the world over. The phenomenon is so influential, in fact, that it has helped cancel hurricanes over in the Atlantic, by messing with winds high up in the atmosphere. Accordingly, this year shattered the record for the latest first hurricane in a season by nearly a month. Normally by this time of year we’d have seen six of these cyclones, but 2026 has still only produced one.

The Southwest, though, gets no such relief from inclement weather. In addition to adding heat to the sky, the warmer waters of El Niño also increase atmospheric moisture. Even beyond the El Niño, temperatures in the Pacific have been running extra hot, which explains why the western part of the ocean has produced 10 hurricanes this season even as the Atlantic has remained quiet. (Overall, more than 90 percent of the excess heat that humans have pumped into the atmosphere has been absorbed by the oceans.)

All this warm water means more moisture for the weather patterns that have been moving into the Southwest over the last month. A separate system in late October, for instance, became one of the most extreme storms in Colorado’s history, pelting higher elevations with up to 8 inches of rain in four days, causing widespread destruction. “It’s just really extreme amounts of water vapor in the atmosphere that have been aimed into the Southwest in each of those storms,” Schumacher said.

This autumn precipitation primed Arizona, Colorado, and other Southwestern states for yet more destruction this past week. For one, rivers were already running high, then ran all the higher. And two, if soils are soaked, a follow-up bout of rain will run off and cause flooding. “We get the second storm, just a little bit after the first one, then everything was primed for even worse flooding this time around,” Schumacher said.

In mountainous terrain, this gets especially dangerous, as the topography funnels rainwater into raging torrents. “If you hike around the Southwest, you’re going to see out-of-place boulders all over the place,” Crimmins said. “Water put it there. Maybe it was 5,000 years ago or something like that, but water moves. We can have really epic flash flooding.”

The one silver lining here is that any increased precipitation from this El Niño could bring drought relief to much of the southern U.S., according to NOAA’s projections. Climate change is not only exacerbating these ongoing dry spells — hotter temperatures also increase evaporation from reservoirs. At the same time, populations are growing in the Southwest, meaning more people demanding more water.

With these factors …

author: Solarpunk Magazine
title: Solarpunk Horror, Lunarpunk Submissions, and 2027 Magazine Submissions
content:
We’ve got some exciting announcements to share! There’s a brand-new lunarpunk anthology seeking submissions, our special horror-themed issue of Solarpunk Magazine is available for preorder, we’re going to start publishing solarpunk novellas and novels, and our complete 2027 submissions schedule is now up on our website’s submissions page.

So whether you’re a reader looking for your next great story or a writer dreaming up better futures, here’s what’s coming.

Submission Window: November 1 – December 31, 2026

Android Press is preparing to venture into the shadows with What Blooms in Darkness: A Lunarpunk Anthology, edited by our co-editor-in-chief, Justine Norton-Kertson, and scheduled for publication in autumn 2027.

Lunarpunk shares solarpunk’s commitment to ecological regeneration, social justice, community, and liberatory futures, while exploring the possibilities that emerge in darkness, mystery, privacy, dreams, and the hidden corners of our world.

What Blooms in Darkness asks some fascinating questions: What kinds of communities thrive beyond the reach of surveillance? What knowledge survives underground? What forms of liberation become possible when people are free to remain unseen?

Android Press is seeking stories about everything from nocturnal ecosystems and underground communities to secret mutual-aid networks, hidden cultures, rituals, and resistance movements. The anthology welcomes imaginative interpretations of lunarpunk, especially stories that challenge the assumption that darkness is inherently dangerous or frightening.

Genre: Lunarpunk, climate fiction, and related speculative fiction

Eligibility: Original, unpublished fiction by human authors worldwide

Expected publication: Autumn 2027

Whether you’re a writer or a reader, you can easily sign up to get a notification when the anthology’s crowdfunder launches in March 2027!

We’ve spent years exploring what better futures might look like. Now we’re inviting some monsters into the garden. We’re thrilled to reveal the cover and complete table of contents for Solarpunk Magazine Issue #30, our special Solarpunk Horror issue, arriving November 10, 2026!

Horror and solarpunk might seem like an unusual combination, but we think they have a lot to say to each other. What happens when the ghosts of ecological destruction refuse to stay buried? What kinds of monsters might haunt societies struggling to heal centuries of exploitation? And how do things like fear, grief, survival, and resistance fit into our visions of better futures?

This extra large special issue brings together fiction, poetry, essays, and artwork that explore the darker edges of solarpunk imagination. We’re especially excited about the lineup of writers and artists contributing to this issue.

“The Unrooted Sea” by Seiba Rosario

“Bottles, Bones, Skein” by Marisca Pichette

author: David Greene
title: EFF Submission to OHCHR Consultation on Child Rights and Safety in the Digital Environment
content:
“

The safety of young people in the digital environment cannot be assessed without also considering the safety of young people in offline environments. For millions of young people around the world, the digital environment is their safe place, their haven from an unsafe physical environment, community, or family situation. The digital environment may be the best, perhaps only, place for them to find critical safety information and community, to explore ideas that are controversial in their families and larger physical environments, and to otherwise nourish their personal autonomy.


“For these young people, regulatory efforts that limit their access to online services or to certain features they find valuable, make their lives, in total, less safe, even if there has been some marginal safety benefit to their digital environment.


“The OHCHR must thus consider the whole of young persons' lives in any recommendations that come out of this process and not treat ‘safety, physical or mental health, and rights in the digital environment’ as disconnected from safety, physical or mental health, and rights elsewhere.”


So begins

EFF’s submission

 to the global Call for Inputs on

Child Rights and Safety in the Digital Environment

 conducted by the United Nations Office of the High Commissioner on Human Rights. The OHCHR is preparing a report on the issue to be presented to the UN Human Rights Council at its 64th session in the first quarter of 2027. The Human Rights Council requested the OHCHR to solicit input from a wide range of stakeholders, including child and youth perspectives, and convene five regional consultations to assess the risks to the safety of the child in the digital environment and best practices to address these risks in different geographical areas, bearing in mind current and emerging business models. 


The OHCHR acknowledges that young people today navigate a digital environment with both “unprecedented opportunities” and “serious and evolving risks,” and sets out a rights-based framing whereby “Children's 'safety' is therefore addressed through the full framework of their rights — with freedom from violence (Art. 19) and protection from exploitation and abuse (Arts. 34–36) as clearly defined obligations, situated alongside privacy (Art. 16), access to information (Arts. 13 and 17), expression (Art. 13), participation (Art. 12), and development (Art. 6). Protection and the full range of children's rights are understood as reinforcing rather than competing imperatives, and measures taken in the name of safety must not be used to restrict the enjoyment of other rights, such as the right to privacy and the right to participate.”


In light of this, EFF’s

submission

 focused on the current general disregard for young people's speech and privacy rights by regulators around the world, all of whom seem far more interested in empowering parents rather than young people themselves, or meaningfully involving young people in the regulatory process. 

We emphasized the human rights-centered uses young people make of social media that were not specifically set out in the concept note. 

We also explained that too often, policy proposals aiming to remedy the issues of online safety for young people introduce limitations on access to online services and content rather than tackling the specific problems that people experience. 


More specifically, our submission looks at:


the most significant risks to young people’s safety in the digital environment


how digital product design and business models drive risks to children's rights online, including in AI-mediated services


the inclusion of young people’s views in the design, governance, and regulation of digital environments 


how equality and non-discrimination in access and protection can be ensured


the promotion of digital literacy, skills, and empowerment for young people 


the impact of legislative and regulatory measures from the United States to Indonesia and Australia 


importance of broader, more systemic interventions that can address address online harms


how global instruments and processes can protect young people online. 


The internet is where young people learn, find community, explore their identities, access important information, and express themselves. Curtailing these opportunities doesn't make them safer. And requiring everyone to hand over sensitive personal information just to access online spaces creates privacy risks for …

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Hennepin County Surveilled Anti-HERC Activists Since 2023
content:
Minneapolis, MN — A report released by the Zero Burn Coalition documents years of surveillance conducted against activists pushing for clean air in Minneapolis. The revelations came from documents that the organization obtained through public information requests.


At the center of this is the Hennepin Energy Recovery Center (HERC), a nearly 40-year-old trash incinerator neighboring Target Field in Minneapolis permitted to burn 365,000 tons of garbage annually. Activists, including those with the Zero Burn Coalition, have advocated for its closure for years, citing the amount of pollution it produces and the disproportionate effect on marginalized communities.


A short walk to the west of the facility is historically Black and working-class neighborhoods of North Minneapolis, which bear the brunt of the plant’s pollution. 


Coinciding with the release of the report on Oct. 22, community members and Minnesota Environmental Justice Table (MNEJT) activists and leaders convened along Olson Memorial Highway in the Heritage Park neighborhood for a press conference, in full view of HERC’s foreboding smoke stacks on the other side of Interstate 94.


“Instead of addressing the concerns raised by residents, the county has devoted staff time and resources to tracking the people organizing for change,” MNEJT Associate Director Adina Black said. “This raises serious questions about accountability, transparency, and the county’s treatment of the communities it has a responsibility to serve.”


The

eight-page report

 details seven separate instances of the county surveilling activists and the role former environmental justice leader Joe Vital played in that. 


Hennepin-Co-Surveillance-Report-Zero-Burn-Coalition


Vital was a part of

the East Phillips Neighborhood Institute’s successful push

 to acquire the former Roof Depot site from the city of Minneapolis in 2023. Since then, he has become Hennepin County’s Environmental Engagement Coordinator and would attend activist meetings to feed his notes to other Hennepin County employees, such as the county’s Department of Environment and Energy Assistant Director David McNary.


The report alleges that Vital also attempted to learn the identity of a county whistleblower through conversation with Minnesota Environmental Justice Table’s co-founder Nazir Khan.


In emails acquired by the Zero Burn Coalition, McNary would forward alerts from the activists to Tim Steinbeck, the president of Great River Energy, the company operating HERC. McNary and Steinbeck both served simultaneously as the treasurer-secretary of Minnesota Resource Recovery Association, a group formed by leaders of the incinerator industry.


000124-000140


In March 2024, an amortization bill was introduced in the state legislature that would allow cities to phase out sources of pollution in vulnerable neighborhoods without requiring them to do so. The House committee considering the bill narrowed it to only the state’s largest cities.


Under Minnesota law at the time, amortization could only be used against adult-only stores and criminal nuisances.


While advocates rallied around the bill, McNary forwarded the private emails of activists to Steinbeck and other industry representatives, urging them to oppose it.


“They start with the big cities and before long it will be the entire state,” McNary wrote in the email thread while pushing the idea that the amortization process would come to affect other industries.


Read

all of the documents published to the public by the Zero Burn Coalition

.


HERC, which began operation in 1989, is a “waste-to-energy” facility, meaning it produces energy for the power grid by incinerating garbage. Since its construction, the population within five kilometers of the plant has grown to nearly 250,000.


Despite politicians and others

framing “waste-to-energy” as environmentally friendly

,

a peer-reviewed study published in 2023

 found that “incinerators emit more greenhouse gas emissions per unit of electricity produced … than any other power source.” The study also added that the inclusion of incinerators in “‘renewable’ or ‘clean’ energy standards is thus counterproductive, as they also divert more than $40 million in subsidies annually from cleaner energy sources.”


HERC, which has been operated by Great River Energy since 2018, annually produces roughly 350,000 million tons of carbon dioxide and 72,000 million tons of incinerator ashes, according to a report …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Las Tres Ecologías y la disputa por el espacio público en Rosario
content:
Por Laura Hintze


En la oferta gastronómica-cultural y del paisaje ribereño —por ahora accesible para todas y todos— en la costa de Rosario falta el Almacén de Las Tres Ecologías. Es un emprendimiento autogestivo donde, por más de una década, cooperativas, productores y organizaciones de la economía social de todo el país vendieron sus productos en un espacio público cedido a tal fin, en una zona codiciada por el negocio inmobiliario.

 Desde este año, por decisión unilateral de la Municipalidad, está cerrado.

 “El neoliberalismo es la práctica económica que, diciendo que está en contra del Estado, hace los mejores negocios con el Estado. Se apropia de sus recursos de infraestructura, de los recursos naturales o financieros para hacer negocios. Esto es lo que sucede. Es un proceso de profundización de la privatización”, reflexiona Roberto García, integrante de Las Tres Ecologías.


Durante años, quienes llegaban los fines de semana hasta el paseo ribereño podían encontrarse con un galpón de 25 metros por 10 donde había comidas, bebidas, artesanías, plantas, libros y textiles elaborados por cooperativas y organizaciones de distintas provincias

. Pero el Almacén no era solamente un lugar de venta. Aprovechaba su ubicación y el alcance a nuevos oídos y preguntas para abrir conversaciones a través de radios abiertas, presentaciones de libros, música en vivo, ferias y encuentros nacionales.

 Ese borde de la ciudad, a orillas del Paraná, se convertía en un lugar para producir, intercambiar y encontrarse.


El Almacén de las Tres Ecologías está cerrado desde enero. La Municipalidad de Rosario desocupó el galpón que había cedido once años antes a las organizaciones que lo gestionaban. Primero intentó hacerlo por la fuerza; después formalizó el cese del contrato por decreto. Desde entonces, quienes sostuvieron el proyecto se reorganizan fuera de ese espacio y buscan otro lugar en la ribera.

Detrás de esta disputa vuelve la pregunta que los rosarinos se hacen una y otra vez: ¿qué proyecto de ciudad se está construyendo frente al Paraná?


Foto: Las Tres Ecologías


El lujo es la organización comunitaria


El Almacén de las Tres Ecologías abrió sus puertas el 11 de febrero de 2015. “Ese día había muchísima alegría”, recuerda García. Habían trabajado todo ese verano para dejar el lugar a punto. El mobiliario, hecho con maderas recicladas, fue una de las marcas del espacio durante la década que funcionó: le daba un tono artesanal y luminoso que lo diferenciaba de lo que había alrededor. La inauguración reunió a amigos, organizaciones hermanas, ecologistas y autoridades municipales. “Fue el comienzo de una iniciativa única en todo el país”, resalta.


La apertura del comercio fue fruto de un acuerdo entre la Municipalidad de Rosario y tres redes de la economía social, solidaria y popular: la Red de Comercio Justo del Litoral, el Centro Ecuménico Poriajhú y la Cooperativa de Trabajo Encuentro Nacional. El Estado cedió a las organizaciones un espacio público sin cobrarles alquiler ni canon por su uso.


El galpón que recibió a las organizaciones cooperativas había pertenecido a empresas públicas vinculadas al puerto y al ferrocarril. Quedó abandonado después de las privatizaciones de los años 90. Según García,

mientras buena parte de esos espacios terminó destinada a proyectos inmobiliarios de lujo, otros quedaron en manos del Estado, municipal o provincial

. Ese fue el caso del galpón donde funcionó el Almacén, que quedó bajo la órbita de la secretaría de Economía Solidaria de la Municipalidad.


“La evaluación que hicimos hace 13 años fue que toda la costa se estaba privatizando y que solamente un galpón de 50 metros por 10 había quedado en manos de la Secretaría de Economía Solidaria. Entonces eso debía ser dedicado a prácticas relacionadas con la economía social y solidaria, una economía absolutamente emergente y débil frente a la economía de capital y del mercado. Nos pareció importante armar una propuesta en la que el municipio no hiciera algo estándar y llamara a licitación, que era lo que iba a hacer”, cuenta.


“Por eso no alcanza con decir que Las Tres Ecologías fue un proyecto cooperativo. Hubo una propuesta política muy fuerte: que estas organizaciones de la economía social, solidaria y popular pudieran gestionar un espacio del Estado de manera mancomunada, sin que el Estado aportara dinero ni les cobrara, sino que simplemente cediera el espacio.

Fue una experiencia de democracia participativa en el sentido más …

author: Danilo Arao
title: Peryodiko
content:
Photo from the Kilusang Magbubukid ng Pilipinas

Maganda ang teknolohiya kung mapapakinabangan ng karamihan.

May nagbabasa pa kaya ng peryodiko? Alam pa kaya ng kabataan ang mga katulad na salitang pahayagan at diyaryo?

Baka mas pundamental pa ang tanong: May nagbabasa pa kaya? Totoo bang wala nang masyadong kultura ng pagbuklat ng anumang nakaimprenta dahil mas gusto ng mga taong manood na lang ng bidyo?

Kung sabagay, higit pa sa peryodismo ang isyu. Analog o digital? Nobela o pelikula? Lumang midya o bagong midya? Pero saglit lang. Kailangan ba talagang mamili sa dalawa? Hindi ba puwedeng pagsabayin ang luma’t bago?

Kung gagamit ng ilang salita sa wikang Ingles, hindi ito usapin ng “conversion” kundi “convergence.” Posibleng gamitin ng lumang midya ang bagong teknolohiya para mapalakas ang mga katangian nito. At sa konteksto ng peryodismo, nagdesisyon ang maraming peryodikong gumawa ng mga website at account sa iba’t ibang social media platform.

Para sa mga peryodista, kailangang pumunta kung nasaan ang masa. Ito ang dahilan ng literal na pagbisita sa mga komunidad, lalo na sa mga liblib na lugar na tila napag-iwanan ng kabihasnan. Ito rin ang magpapaliwanag kung bakit pinapatulan pati ang TikTok sa paghuhubog ng opinyong pampubliko. Naglalaan din sila ng oras para makipagtalastasan sa social media kahit na hindi pinapansin ang mga personal na atake.

Dahil sa mabilis na pag-unlad ng teknolohiya, totoo namang lumang-luma na ang mga tinaguriang sinauna. Pero kapansin-pansin ang ebolusyon ng print para isama sa diseminasyon ng impormasyon ang teknolohiyang digital.

Gayundin ang kaso ng mga programa sa radyo dahil mayroon na silang kaakibat na teleradyo para marinig at makita ang balita, pati na ang nangyayari sa loob ng booth habang nagbobrodkast. At para naman sa mga programa sa telebisyon, uso na rin ang simultaneous live streaming.

Ngunit para sa mga lugar na mahina o walang internet signal, patuloy na namamayagpag ang lumang midya. Mas nakadepende sila sa radyo o telebisyon para sa pinakahuling balita. Nakakatulong din naman ang peryodiko para sa dagdag na pagsusuri kahit na hindi agad-agad na nakukuha ang kopya. Kaya hindi naman masyadong nahuhuli sa balita ang mga nasa liblib na lugar basta’t may mga matiyagang magsusubaybay at maghahanap ng paraan.

Maganda ang teknolohiya kung mapapakinabangan ng karamihan. Pero kung ang kalidad at bilis ng internet ay depende sa panggastos, parating mapipilitan ang mahihirap na pagtiyagaan ang mabagal na koneksiyon.

Para sa karamihang naka-prepaid na account lang sa kanilang mobile phone, mas gagamitin ang mga libreng opsiyon para ma-access ang social media accounts pero malamang na hindi maki-click ang link papunta sa buong teksto ng balitang nasa website ng mga organisasyong pang-midya. Kaya ang mangyayari, headline lang o maikling bahagi lang ng balita ang posibleng mabasa.

Anong klaseng opinyon ang mabubuo kung limitado lang ang impormasyon? Hindi ba’t mas mainam na gawing libre ang internet para sa lahat? Bakit kailangan pa kasing pagkakitaan ang teknolohiyang dapat na maging tulay para sa epektibong diseminasyon ng impormasyon?

Pero labas ng internet access, kailangan ding pangalagaan ang mga tinaguriang luma. Patuloy na kilalanin ang ambag ng print, radyo at telebisyon, lalo na ang kanilang paggamit ng teknolohiya sa gitna ng nagbabagong panahon. Hindi hiwalay ang pag-aaral ng bago sa pagkilala ng luma. Katulad ito sa pag-intindi ng kasalukuyan batay sa aral ng kasaysayan.

Uso pa ba ang peryodiko? Tandaang may mga nagbabasa pa naman. Hindi naman mawawala ang print media sa kabila ng pag-unlad ng teknolohiya. Mahalaga pa rin ang tuloy-tuloy na paglilimbag lalo na’t kinakailangan ang malalim na pagsasakonteksto.

Para makipag-ugnayan sa awtor, pumunta sa https://risingsun.dannyarao.com

author: groundxero
title: She Is Risen: Jamia’s Student Union Claws Her Way Out Of The Grave
content:
On the 106th anniversary of her foundation, Jamia’s student union came back to life. 


 


Mouli Sharma


 


Mahawat

 falls cold and brutal in Delhi’s October, announcing the coming winter and daring you to test her like only nature can.


 


In South East Delhi, rain is sickness, mosquitoes, and waterlogging; the roads in and around Jamia Nagar (Haji Colony, Gaffar Manzil, Batla House, Okhla Vihar, Sarai Jullena, etc.) are ill-tempered and poorly maintained—everything floods (except the posh New Friends Colony, home to a covert ‘counter-intelligence unit’ of the Delhi Police’s ‘Special Cell’).


 


Sometimes, of course, rain is rebirth. Autumn washing away the sins of the season past.


 


Since 12 October 2026, Jamia Millia Islamia’s banned Student Union had been clawing its way out from six feet under. Between an indefinite hunger strike, a multi-departmental occupation, a campus lockdown and five arrests, the University’s ‘sanghi’ administration and collective student body had been in the midst of a political showdown. Unbeknownst to both, judgment day was going to come as the protests (described as the biggest in Jamia since Shaheen Bagh) entered their 18th day, on the 106th anniversary of the University’s own radical birth.


On the 106th anniversary of her foundation, Jamia’s student union came back to life.


In the early 1900s, policies of the British Raj that prompted a mass exit of students and faculty from the Aligarh Muslim University—primarily due to pro-establishment policies aimed at preventing, discouraging, and penalising participation in the Freedom Movement, i.e. suppressing academic dissent—paved the way for collective desire for a “National Muslim University” free from authoritarian intervention.


 


“Many students of Aligarh too were disappointed with the administration’s pro-British policies which prevented teachers and students from taking part in the freedom movement,” says a memorial piece on Shaikhul-Hind Mahmood Hasan, one of Jamia’s most prominent founders, in the Milli Gazette from a decade ago, halfway between the perceived bookends of this story. “In 1920, some students suddenly left the Aligarh Muslim University. A free and private “National Muslim University” was planned to accommodate these students. Despite his bad health and frail body, Maulana Mahmood travelled to Aligarh and laid the foundation-stone of this institution on 29 October 1920. It later came to be known as Jamia Millia Islamia.”


 


As the piece goes on, Mahmood is remembered as being advised against going to Aligarh, to lay Jamia’s founding stone, on 29 October 1926. His response is one of the more telling anecdotes about this foundation:


 


“If this pains the British, I will do it.”


 


***


Sab Kuch Yaad Rakha Jayega?


 


Eight decades later, a different regime did to Jamia what the British had done to AMU in their time. Contrary to the understanding of ‘2006’ as the definitive year of the JMISU’s two decade stint under the ground, the body’s existence had been tenuous for long before that, having been banned once prior in 1996, after merely 15 years of existence since the first union elections in 1981. The 2006 ban followed what was merely eight months of resurfacing, with a union having been constituted for the first time in a decade in July 2005, only to be banned under the Manmohan Singh-led UPA government the following year, by the university administration itself, ostensibly due to concerns over ‘campus violence’, and an alleged attack on then Vice Chancellor, Late Prof. Mushirul Hasan.


 


The purpose of the ban, both in motivation and impact, is debated till date.


 


“Mushirul is the last VC Jamia had that did anything in the university’s interest,” a professor who would rather not be named tells me over tea and nostalgia in another university campus—JNU, where he feels freer to talk. “You see the road that passes through the campus today?” he asks with disgust. It is this, Okhla Road, splicing through the belly of Jamia’s largest continuous territories, where armed vehicles and central forces have remained since the anti-CAA-NRC-NPR protests of 2020, and where they stood through 18 days of protest that took place there through the second half of October.


 


“He planned to have it razed; combine both the campuses. The police would not be able to militarise the campus the way they’ve done and are doing if that had happened. This entire architecture lends itself to repression,” he …

title: Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional - Don’t Forsake Us!
content:
Author

: Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional

Title

: Don’t Forsake Us!

Subtitle

: Zapatista Women in ’94

Date

: 1994

Notes

: Originally published by Ediciones OnA, València-Chiapas: 1

st

 edition May 2018, 2

nd

 edition January 2019, 3

rd

 edition July 2019, 4

th

 edition January 2020.

 English translation by Ediciones Bloodfruit/Malvivientes, 2026.

Source

: Retrieved 10/30/26 from https://www.patreon.com/bloodfruit/posts/dont-forsake-us-173797846


 The money raised from the this first volume are going to the benefit of Compañera M. Mother,

 Social Warrior, Multiply Employed, Indigenous.


 The best way to understand the path of the women who struggle is through their own words. These brief texts, interviews and declarations of the women of the Zapatista Army for National Liberation in the first months of the armed uprising of 1994 showcase the situation of indigenous women in Mexican territory, and are a mirror of the dignity that has kept the Zapatista struggle alive despite male chauvinism, racism and capitalism.


 This edition was part of a mutual aid initiative to redistribute the

funds of the circulating texts and “Independent” editions among

the struggles’ female protagonists


Words From Comandanta Ramona and Major Ana María


Another concern that indigenous

women have is the free choice of partners.


“The dowry custom still exists,

the girl is never taken into account,

she is sold off (in this region,

the average price of nuptial dowry is

two thousand pesos). The idea of

having a boyfriend doesn’t exist; it is sin.”


 Ana María, Infantry Major: “Don’t Forsake Us!” is the desperate plea of the women of the Zapatista Army for National Liberation so that their hopes of being heard within and without their communities may not die. “We ask all women to fight alongside us” is what Comandanta Ramona and Major Ana María say in Tzotzil and Spanish. Their call to Mexican women is not one to take up arms, but rather so that, within their spaces, they may support the changes proposed by the Revolutionary Law of Women, as well as their extensive list over equality, justice, health, education and housing. That night, the penultimate they would spend at the Cathedral, they arrived through the back of the altar, accompanied by Subcomandante Marcos.


 He, dressed in his unmistakable military uniform. Some steps behind, the only two women of a group of the 19 delegates of the Indigenous Clandestine Revolutionary Committee. “I’ll leave them with you so that you can speak to them about anything you wish,” he said in a joking tone as he bid his farewell to the group of five female reporters and two photographers intent on interviewing the women of the Zapatista Army. Ramona’s wide and sharp eyes revealed weariness. The black wool skirt, the beautifully embroidered loom-woven blouse, and her short stature contrasted with Ana María’s gray

ruana

 and sturdy frame. Alongside them, Comandante Javier remained behind (to translate Ramona’s Tzotzil’s words into Spanish). The words of the Comandanta, even if in Tzotzil, flow smoothly from her indigenous heart.


 I left my community in search of work because of necessity itself, there was no longer anything to live off of. When I arrived someplace else I began to learn that it wasn’t the same situation as that of women in the countryside. I learned there to understand and gain conscience of the differences, that’s how I learned of the organization (EZLN), and that it was also necessary to organize women.


 Within EZLN women’s participation in key. Ramona belongs to the political group that works in the communities; Ana María is part of the approximately 30% of female combatants/insurgents who voluntarily refuse to form a family in order to engage in armed struggle.


 “I am an insurgent. I’ve dedicated my entire life and time to the cause,” affirms Ana María, a 26 year old Infantry Major who, when speaking of displacement and suffering endured, furrows her brows in sadness, the only sign of expression able to be seen beneath her balaclava. “It’s a long story,” she says,


 Ever since I was eight years old I took part in peaceful struggles, in marches, in meetings. My family was one that fought, that always organized in order to have a dignified life, but that never achieved it through that route. We were in an organization —won’t say which— with other persons, with other peoples. We would go there, the children too, and that’s how we went began …

author: Kay Pacha / Equipo Pueblos Originarios del SERPAJ
title: La UNSa y su trabajo con los Pueblos Originarios
content:
Recordando que el reciente 12 de octubre, el Día del respeto a la Diversidad Cultural, en todo el país hubo actividades llevadas a cabo por organizaciones y comunidades originarias.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Pastrana-david.-Pueblos.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Pastrana-david.-Pueblos.mp3


Descargar archivo


Y uno de esos lugares fue la Provincia de Salta, en donde la Universidad Nacional de Salta reunió a referentes de pueblos originarios, autoridades, realizadores audiovisuales y miembros de la comunidad en una jornada de diálogo, memoria y reconocimiento de las realidades territoriales.


Esa actividad se llamó “Voces del Territorio: Memoria, Identidad y Continuidad” en donde se proyectó la Película “Senda India”, con la presencia de la directora Daniela Seggiaro.


Esto dio lugar a espacios de intercambio y debate sobre la situación territorial de los pueblos originarios y la agenda legislativa vinculada a sus derechos.


Cabe destacar que la película se hizo tomando como base las filmaciones realizadas por el joven wichí Miguel Ángel Lorenzo, quien filmó con una cámara de video Hi8, con humor, sensibilidad y junto a sus paisanos, recorridos por el monte, por casas vecinas, en actos escolares, pericias arqueológicas y visitas de un juez, como parte de las pruebas para un juicio que llevaba adelante su comunidad desde 1986.


Esta jornada fue organizada de manera conjunta por la Universidad Nacional de Salta, a través de la Coordinación de Pueblos Originarios de la UNSa, el Instituto Provincial de Pueblos Indígenas de Salta (IPPIS), el C.I.P.I., el MinPPi y EIB Salta.


Por eso, contamos ahora con el testimonio de David Pastrana, Coordinador de Pueblos Originarios de la UNSa, quien comenta con más detalles acerca de las reflexiones que tuvieron lugar en esa oportunidad. Agradecemos al programa Protagonistas de la Mañana de la Radio Universidad de Salta por este material.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense

author: Stelinsky
title: Μπέικον και δουλεία
content:
Το σημερινό άρθρο είναι επετειακό. Πριν από 350 χρόνια διαδραματίστηκαν στην αγγλοκρατούμενη ακόμα Αμερική τα γεγονότα που επιτάχυναν την εδραίωση της δουλείας στην αμερικανική ήπειρο, και η αφορμή ήταν στην περιοχή της Βιρτζίνια, και συγκεκριμένα στην πόλη του Τζέιμς Τάουν, και αυτή θα παρουσιάσουμε σήμερα.

Ας τα πιάσουμε όμως από την αρχή. Υπάρχει μία εύλογη ερώτηση στην ατμόσφαιρα· πριν από το 1676 δεν υπήρχε δηλαδή δουλεία στην Αμερική; Υπήρχε, απλά αποτελούσε εκείνη την περίοδο τη μειοψηφία στις εργασιακές σχέσεις. Η πιο διαδεδομένη όμως εργασιακή σχέση ήταν κάπως διαφορετική. Για να μπορέσει η Βρετανική Αυτοκρατορία να αποικίσει την ανατολική ακτή των σημερινών Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών, πρόσφερε στους μεγαλοκαλλιεργητές κάποια κίνητρα για να προσελκύσουν Άγγλους υπηκόους. Μέσω μίας σύμβασης με έναν τσιφλικά μπορούσες να προσληφθείς για 3 με 7 χρόνια, και να εργαστείς στις αμέτρητες εκτάσεις καπνού που είχε στην προκειμένη περίπτωση η Βιρτζίνια, και μετά το πέρας του συμφωνημένου χρόνου δικαιούσουν μία μικρή έκταση για να γίνεις και εσύ από μεριάς σου ένας αγρότης με το δικό του χωράφι. Ο «εργοδότης» σου από την άλλη, για κάθε έναν νέο άποικο που ερχόταν για λογαριασμό του, έπαιρνε 50 εκτάρια γης, και μόνη του έγνοια ήταν να σου πληρώσει ένα εισιτήριο για να έρθεις μέχρι την Αμερική, και αρκετό φαΐ ώστε να επιβιώνεις. Αυτή η σύμβαση ήταν καλύτερη από την απόκτηση ενός δούλου για τον εξής λόγο: Εάν εσύ που είχες υπογράψει τη σύμβαση πέθαινες, είτε κατά τη διάρκεια του ταξιδιού, είτε εξαιτίας των ασθενειών ή των συνθηκών που επικρατούσαν στην άλλη μεριά του Ατλαντικού, τότε ο τσιφλικάς είχε αποκτήσει τα 50 εκτάρια, και για την αντικατάστασή σου απλά θα έβρισκε κάποιον άλλον φουκαρά που θα ήθελε να ξεφύγει από την ανέχεια. Αντιθέτως για τους τσιφλικάδες η αγορά από τα σκλαβοκάραβα, που έφερναν σωρηδόν κόσμο από την Αφρική, ήταν μια μπίζνα ριψοκίνδυνη καθώς αγόραζαν ανθρώπους σε μία εποχή που η θνησιμότητα βάραγε κόκκινο.

Η δεκαετία του 1670 όμως δεν είναι και τόσο καλή για τον κόσμο που έρχεται στην Αμερική από το Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο. Κυβερνήτης της Βιρτζίνια είναι ένας από τους αγαπημένους του στέμματος, ο ηλικιωμένος Μπέρκλεϊ, ο οποίος έχει δημιουργήσει μια σταθερή κατάσταση στην περιοχή. Οι εχθροπραξίες με τους ιθαγενείς είχαν περιοριστεί, αλλά ο Μπέρκλεϊ είχε και σοβαρές εμπορικές δραστηριότητες μαζί τους. Έτσι και έσοδα έρχονται και δεν είναι υποχρεωμένοι να πληρώνουν για σοβαρά έξοδα για τη φύλαξη της περιοχής. Το πρόβλημα πού βρίσκεται λοιπόν; Κόσμος έρχεται στην Βιρτζίνια, δουλεύει στα καπνά, αλλά δεν υπάρχει η απαραίτητη γη για να τους δοθεί ως αντάλλαγμα. Έτσι έχουμε στα περίχωρα του Τζέιμς Τάουν ένα μείγμα λευκών δυσαρεστημένων που θέλουν περισσότερα από αυτά που τους δίνει η εξουσία. Και για αυτή την κατάσταση φταίνε φυσικά από τη μία ο Μπέρκλεϊ και από την άλλη οι ιθαγενείς. Και εδώ εμφανίζεται ο ήρωας της σημερινής ιστορίας· το όνομα αυτού Ναθάνιαλ Μπέικον. Ο Μπέικον δεν είναι κάποιος τυχαίος. Τον έστειλε ο πατέρας του από την Αγγλία στη Βιρτζίνια, αγόρασε εκεί εκτάσεις και έγινε τσιφλικάς στα περίχωρα κοντά στα νοητά σύνορα με τους ιθαγενείς. Φαινομενικά στην όλη κατάσταση ο Μπέικον δεν είχε κανέναν λόγο να εμπλακεί. Ήταν ένας γενικά κλειστός άνθρωπος, χωρίς κάποιο ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον για τα κοινά. Όμως μία σειρά αντεγκλήσεων με ιθαγενείς στην περιοχή, οι οποίες δεν αφορούσαν καν τον ίδιο, τον έκαναν να αναλάβει δράση. Χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα είναι η σύλληψη από μέρους του κάποιων ιθαγενών οι οποίοι, σύμφωνα πάντα με τον Θάνο μας, έκλεψαν καλαμπόκι το οποίο δεν ήταν καν δικό του. Ταυτόχρονα η συμβιβαστική στάση του Μπέρκλεϊ τού δημιουργεί την εικόνα μίας διεφθαρμένης κλίκας στο Τζέιμς Τάουν που δεν νοιάζεται να αντιμετωπίσει τα προβλήματα των κατοίκων της.

Έτσι, λοιπόν, ο Μπέικον αποφασίζει να πάρει την κατάσταση στα χέρια του. Δημιουργεί μία πολιτοφυλακή με άλλους κατοίκους (λευκούς και Αφρικανούς) και μπαίνει σε εδάφη των ιθαγενών και ξεκληρίζει χωριά. Ο κυβερνήτης Μπέρκλεϊ κρατάει μία αρκετά συμβιβαστική στάση και προσπαθεί να ηρεμήσει τα πράγματα, αλλά ο Μπέικον είναι ανένδοτος, αναγκάζοντας τον πρώτο να τον κηρύξει στασιαστή. Έτσι τον Ιούλιο του 1676 ο Θάνος γράφει τη Διακήρυξη του Λαού· ένα δριμύ κατηγορώ απέναντι στον κυβερνήτη που του επιρρίπτει ευθύνες για τον κίνδυνο που διατρέχουν οι κάτοικοι της περιοχής, για τη βαριά φορολογία και τον αποκλεισμό του κόσμου από τα κέντρα λήψης αποφάσεων. Ένα μανιφέστο αρκετά ωραίο στα αυτιά, αλλά που επ’ ουδενί δεν επιδιώκει να δώσει κάποια πιο δημοκρατική …

title: La menace de l'auto-justice
content:
Au lendemain du 17 octobre, le garde des sceaux Gérald Darmanin, brandie le menace de milices d'auto-défense : « si la réponse pénale aux violences liées au 17 octobre n'est pas extrêmement ferme », alors « les commerçants et les habitants feront justice eux-mêmes ». Une semaine plus tard, le 24, des milices fascistes sous-couvert de défense des petits commerçants attaquent des manifestations dans plusieurs villes de France. De nombreuses vidéos diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux attestent d'une collusion voir d'une collaboration avec les forces de l'ordre. Pour tenter d'y voir plus clair dans cette intrication étonnante entre pouvoir politique, police, milices d'extrême droite et auto-défense populiste, nous avons invité Gilles Favarel-Garrigues et Laurent Gayer, chercheurs au CNRS qui ont travaillé sur l'histoire de l'auto-justice ainsi que Vanessa Codaccioni, politiologue dont les recherches portent sur la répression, la délation et la société de vigilance.

author: daniel
title: Ableistisches journalistisches Versagen
content: Dieser wurde aber weitgehend totgeschwiegen. Es gab kaum Presseberichte. Selbst über die Besetzung eines Bundesministeriums berichtete einzig die Frankfurter Rundschau. Journalist*innen schreiben lieber über Einzelschicksale. Mitleid-erweckende Berichte generieren online Klicks und gefallen Leser*innen. Die Berichte bleiben oberflächlich und die systemischen und politischen Hintergründe werden nicht beleuchtet. Betroffene als Objekte einer bequemen Berichtserstattung. Sobald Betroffene als Akteur*innen auftreten und das System, das sie behindert, anprangern, werden sie unsichtbar gemacht. Die Redaktionen stehen offenbar zu dieser ableistischen Linie. Der Lüneburger Behindertenbeirat kritisierte die Nicht-Berichtserstattung der Landeszeitung (LZ) über eine Kundgebung am europäischen Protesttag für die Gleichstellung von Menschen mit Behinderung. Die Redaktion antwortete am 22. Mai 2026 wie folgt: „Anm. d. Red.: Am Protesttag selbst hat die LZ tatsächlich nicht berichtet. Wir stellen hingegen regelmäßig Schicksale von Menschen mit Einschränkungen in den Mittelpunkt von Geschichten – unabhängig von Protest- oder Gedenktagen. So haben wir beispielsweise am 9. Mai von der 16-jährigen Lotti berichtet, die trotz Unterstützungsbedarf ihren Traumberuf lernen will.“ Selbst die verwendete Sprache ist hier ableistisch. Das Wort „Behinderung“ wird gemieden, obwohl dies kein Schimpfwort ist, sondern eine neutrale Eigenschaft. Das ist ein journalistisches Versagen. Die Graswurzelrevolution wird dagegen über die Proteste und ihre Hintergründe ausführlich in der GWR 514 berichten. Seid auf den Schwerpunkt der Dezemberausgabe gespannt!

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”

author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: Peter C. Gøtzsche, MD
title: Winning Norwegian Lawsuits about Forced Drugging with Antipsychotics
content:
I

t is very difficult to win lawsuits about psychiatric malpractice, particularly about forced drugging with antipsychotics.

1

 One reason is, as lawyer Jim Gottstein, has observed in Alaska,

2

 and which I have also seen on several occasions, that psychiatrists routinely misrepresent the evidence in court: About how ill their patients are; what wonders they can achieve with antipsychotics; and saying that the patients have tolerated them well, which the patients disagree with.

3


When I studied 30 consecutive cases from Denmark

3

 and 30 consecutive cases from Alaska,

4

 where the patients had appealed forced treatment orders, I found that the legal procedures were a sham where the patients were defenceless, and that the law had been violated in every single case.


Another reason why lawsuits are difficult to win is that judges have so much respect for authority that they didn’t care the least when I, other expert witnesses, and lawyers for the plaintiffs like Gottstein demonstrated in court that professors of psychiatry and other experts were lying.

1,2,5


A third reason why it is so difficult to obtain justice is that Ombudsman and Supreme Court decisions are consistently being ignored.

1

 In Norway, the Ombudsman concluded in 2018 that forced treatment with an antipsychotic in a concrete case had violated the law.

6

 The law stipulates that forced drugging can be used when, with “high probability, it can lead to recovery or significant improvement in the patient’s condition, or if the patient avoids a significant worsening of the disease.” Referring to science, the Ombudsman noted that the probability of achieving the intended improvement is very low.


Despite the Ombudsman’s ruling, the unethical practice just continued. It is therefore very significant, also in an international context, that four court cases in Norway—three of them related to antipsychotics—were recently won.


In 2024, I was an expert witness in a lawsuit against the Norwegian State at the Oslo District Court.

5

 It was lost because of an incompetent judge, but the Court of Appeal, which corresponds to the Superior Court in other countries, ruled in 2026 that the human rights were violated when Inger-Mari Eidsvik was subjected to forced treatment with antipsychotics and in a case of solitary confinement.


It had been very difficult to get there. Inger-Mari’s lawyers had been fighting

pro bono

 for over three years for the right to sue the state for multiple violations of the European Convention on Human Rights, the UN conventions, and the Norwegian Constitution. After having lost in two inferior courts, they won at the Supreme Court and were allowed to go ahead with the first case ever to challenge coercive treatment in psychiatry.


I describe here three other Norwegian cases. I met the three women involved at the Mad in Norway film festival in September 2026 where my filmmaker and I showed our documentary, “The Illusion of Psychiatry.”

7

 My account is based on court documents and personal information.


Helen Wesnes


Helen’s story is so gruesome that it is hard to believe that this could happen in a civilised country. She was sexually assaulted in her late teens and struggled with insomnia and nightmares. In the end, she agreed to a two-week stay at a psychiatric hospital, which a psychologist had suggested.


Two weeks turned into nine years. Helen spent nine years continuously in Reinsvoll Hospital from 2000 when she was only 20 years old. NINE YEARS!


Then, from 2009 to 2015, she stayed at an assisted living residence where she was subjected to forced medication. In total, she was under forced treatment for 15 years.


From day one, she was put on an antidepressant, and shortly thereafter she also received antipsychotics, benzodiazepines, an antiepileptic, a stimulant, and lithium. She was misdiagnosed with hebephrenic schizophrenia, but lithium doesn’t work for schizophrenia.

8,9

 It was also medical malpractice to treat Helen with Leponex (clozapine) and Abilify (aripiprazole) simultaneously. National

10

 and international guidelines recommend against using two antipsychotics at the same time and there are very good reasons for this. The benefit is not increased by increasing the dose

11

 but the risk of death from these highly toxic drugs is of course dose-related.

12


Leponex is a particularly toxic drug, which is not more effective than other antipsychotics,

8

content:
Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. C'est la première fois que la révolution s'apparente à la chorégraphie du Thriller de Michaël Jackson. Si le Gilet Jaune de 2018 s'est ajouté au k-way noir de 2016, désormais : c'est l'intégralité du multiverse qui se fait costume. Il n'est pas certain que, dans cette immense Battle d'aura avec le gouvernement, ce soient la police qui ait le meilleur déguisement. Joyeux Halloween.

author: Anne-Marie Cicala
title: How My Body Rejected Lithium After 25 Years
content:
I

t was two o’clock in the morning on our first night out of town in New Orleans, and I woke up suddenly in the dark hotel room feeling horribly sick and needing to run to the bathroom. What ensued was messy and lasted for two hours. I kept waking up with my head in the toilet to do it again. I used most of the towels in the bathroom to clean up both myself and the mess I had made on the floor. At 4am, exhausted and beyond tired, not knowing exactly how to handle the situation, I opened my hotel room door completely naked, threw the armful of soiled towels into the hallway and went back to bed.


The next morning, I woke up extremely nauseous. I was thankful we had packed a decent amount of THC gummies, as they proved to be a savior for the next few days. The gummies took the nausea down to a level where I was able to function throughout the day, but I was still not feeling right or well. I didn’t know if it was from the previous night’s events, but I felt subdued by a heavy brain fog.


The day progressed slowly, as I was not feeling 100%, but I made it through, enduring other would just get a good night’s sleep and be better in the morning. Yet, without fail, I once more woke up in the middle of the night, more prepared this time, and got sick several times.


I really had no idea what was going on. Once again, I woke up with severe nausea but thought maybe a good breakfast would set me straight.


At the hotel restaurant, I could not tolerate the smell of the food. I could barely drink my coffee. My husband, looking at me searchingly, kept asking if I was okay. I tried to assure him that I would be fine, although I wasn’t sure I believed that myself. He finally said, “I don’t know what to do when my wife looks like she’s about to vomit at any moment.” Remembering how much the gummies had helped me the day before, I decided it was going to have to be another day like that, so I asked him to go up to the room to retrieve one for me. He happily obliged. I ate the gummy and was feeling relief within about 40 minutes. I could finally breathe and begin to perform as a person on vacation.


At restaurants, I noticed that the menus would shake furiously in my hands, as well as my fork and my drinking glass. I brushed it off as my usual lithium tremor combined with low blood sugar. I also noticed that my thirst was unquenchable. At one restaurant, as soon as the waiter set the water on the table, I chugged the glass immediately and instructed him to keep them coming, that I was extra thirsty. My husband looked at me with concern and kept the gummies coming, which were still keeping the nausea at a manageable level. My additional stomach ailments continued, but I pushed through them and tried to make the best of it, still under the spell of a heavy brain fog.


After another night of vomiting and immediately popping gummies as soon as I woke up, my husband and I put our heads together. We ran through the list of symptoms I had been experiencing, coming up clueless. Next, we thought back on anything that had changed recently. Aha! Indeed, my psychiatrist had increased my lithium right before we left for vacation.


Only knowing that connection, we began to research my symptoms plus the keyword ‘lithium’. Immediately, tons of links popped up about lithium toxicity, something neither one of us knew anything about. It seemed serious, but some of the stories I read seemed a lot graver than mine, so I figured I wasn’t in need of emergency care. I simply discontinued the lithium, and we went home the next day. Not getting back until later in the evening, it was the following day before I could go in for an emergency blood draw to check my lithium levels, something that had been done frequently throughout my nearly 25-year history of being on the medication.


I had been put on lithium for my early bipolar (then later schizoaffective) diagnosis when I was 18 years old, after spending the previous year psychiatrically hospitalized seven times for depression, anxiety, psychosis and unstable mood. I was promised mood stability and less suicidal ideation. It was supposedly the leading option, my best line of defense. That is what I was told for the next 25 years, but I was never told about lithium toxicity.


From the start, the side effects were horrible. So much GI distress and unquenchable thirst, which I know now was my kidneys urgently trying to rid my body of the essential poison of the drug. I learned to deal with it. Every …

author: Robert Whitaker
title: Dangerous Gifts: Rethinking Madness, Healing, and Human Connection – A Conversation With Sascha DuBrul
content:
H

ello, my name is Robert Whitaker, and today I have the great pleasure of having as my guest on Mad in America Radio Sascha DuBrul. Sascha will be well-known to most Mad in America listeners. He’s been a leading activist in psychiatric circles for more than two decades now.


He co-founded The Icarus Project and worked closely with the Institute for the Development of Human Arts. His interests lie at the intersection of the public mental health system and the Mad Underground.


The transcript below has been edited for length and clarity. Listen to the audio of the interview here.


Robert Whitaker: Sascha, welcome to Mad in America Radio.


Sascha DuBrul

: I’m so happy to be here, Bob.


Whitaker: I’d like to tell a little story about how I first discovered you and the Icarus Project. I had come out with a book,

Mad in America

, in 2002, and at that time, I wrote about MindFreedom, David Oaks, and the psychiatric survivor movement. Then all of a sudden, the Icarus Project popped up on my screen, and I could see that it was different in its orientation from the psychiatric survivor movement, and yet it was user-led. Sascha, can you tell us what led you to co-found the Icarus Project?


DuBrul:

 First of all, it’s great to have this conversation with you after all these years, because one thing that just occurs to me is when you started the Mad in America website, I was one of the first people

blogging

 on it.


When we started the Icarus Project, there was the psychiatric survivor movement that you were talking about, and then there was biological psychiatry. There were the NAMI meetings that my mom had gone to when I had been hospitalized and diagnosed with bipolar disorder, but there was nothing really in between. There was no space to say, Hey, you know what? These things that we’re talking about, mental illness if we want to call it that, or the extreme states that we’re experiencing, or these hard times that we’re going through, we don’t have language to talk about it.


The psychiatric survivor language never really resonated with me or with the other people that were originally part of Icarus, and part of that was a generational thing. The psychiatric survivor movement came of age in a time when people were getting locked up in institutions for long periods of time. We were the biomedical generation, where we were getting diagnosed and put on drugs, but not having these long, extended stays in the hospital.


Icarus started because I wrote an article in the

San Francisco Bay Guardian

. I was 27 years old, and I was asking questions like, I don’t trust the pharmaceutical industry, but the drugs that they’re giving me seem to actually be helping me. I’m looking for other people out there that are just trying to figure this stuff out. That’s the context in which Icarus started.


Whitaker: The Icarus Project is often referred to as a radical group. Yet on the one hand, you’re finding the drugs helpful; many members did. I presume you were in a position of choice, right? People like the drugs, that’s great. If they don’t like the drugs, that’s good too.


DuBrul:

 When we started, we said very clearly, if you take the psychiatric drugs or you think they’re poison, you’re welcome to be a part of the Icarus Project. If you use diagnostic categories, like bipolar disorder or schizophrenia, or you think all those categories are ridiculous, you’re welcome to be a part of the Icarus Project. We opened up a lot of space for people who wouldn’t necessarily agree with each other to be in the same room.


Whitaker: But you shared the experience of having been diagnosed, of having some exposure to the psychiatric system, and in some ways finding it unhelpful. Isn’t that correct?


DuBrul:

 For sure, but I think what that actually means is for people to say, yeah, that was really horrible the way those doctors treated me. They treated me like I couldn’t even make decisions for myself. But what is that language they use? The language of harm to self or harm to others. Maybe I actually was going to hurt myself if they didn’t put me in the hospital. Maybe I was actually going to hurt somebody else if I wasn’t put in the hospital.


We opened up space for all kinds of questions like that, that I think the traditional psychiatric survivor movement really didn’t have language or space for in the way they were thinking.
