author: Aallyah Wright
title: Mississippi Ballot Monitors Say They’re Being Shut Out of Vote Counting
content:
Volunteers say they are navigating confusion and obstacles while trying to ensure a transparent counting process.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

It took Natt Offiah an hour to realize he had arrived at the wrong location to monitor the provisional and absentee ballots in the Mississippi U.S. Senate race. He drove to Madison County Circuit Clerk’s Office on Wednesday, but the building was under construction.

After a phone call, Offiah, director of organizing for the People’s Advocacy Institute, and his colleague finally reached the temporary clerk’s office. They were redirected again, shared Offiah, still unable to locate officials.

At the next building, one woman said, “I haven’t seen them in an hour or so,” before directing the organizers down a hallway.

Offiah said he banged on the door, to no avail. The duo sat outside the room for 45 minutes before heading back to the front desk. A receptionist then told Offiah about two dozen staffers had left 15 minutes before his initial arrival.

No one could provide him any information on when they would return to continue counting votes.

“There is no standardized process for counting. Each county can pick and choose when they want to start counting. So, we’re running into this runaround issue,” Offiah said.

His experience mirrors the dozens of other volunteers who say they didn’t sign up for chaos and confusion, but to protect the democratic process. Some — who reported their concerns in group chats shared with Capital B — say they’ve been denied a seat to observe the process, while others struggle to find information.

With the nation’s close eye on Mississippi, advocates say it’s even more critical to ensure election officials “do the right thing.” Voters have been on edge since Election Day, waiting to see who will become the state’s next U.S. senator.

Despite no early voting or online registration, turnout and absentee ballots have surged. As of Nov. 6, Democrat Scott Colom leads Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith by over 2,500 votes.

Yet, there are still thousands of mail-in and affidavit ballots outstanding.

Issues like voter ID laws and inoperable machines have fueled delays, said Lydia Grizzell, policy and advocacy manager of ACLU of Mississippi.

“It is appalling the number of issues that we’ve seen and we had on Election Day, and now we’re seeing the extension of that post-Election Day in a way that is not great,” she said.

The Mississippi secretary of state’s office did not address the monitors’ allegations of being shut out of the vote counting process, but told Capital B the public is entitled to be present for the counting of ballots, the process where election commissioners announce which affidavit ballots are accepted or rejected, according to state statute. This does not include the preliminary work commissioners do to determine a voter’s eligibility.

There is no uniform process on how officials conduct affidavit ballot counting. In some counties, where ACLU dispatched attorneys, election officials had a closed door process, Grizell added.

“The best thing that we can do is have people watching, witnessing, and doing their best to gather as much information as possible as to what is happening,” she said.

Volunteers across the state are being deployed in a widespread effort prompted by several grassroots organizations. The NAACP has also deployed national legal, policy, and field staff to the state to make sure every vote is counted.

Both candidates sent their own groups to monitor the process and assembled a group of lawyers who are prepared to take legal action if necessary. Lawyers for Hyde-Smith sent a letter to election commissioners requesting “immediate separation, secure custody and preservation of all affidavit ballots.” Following Hyde-Smith’s legal team’s response, Colom’s legal counsel sent a letter to all 82 counties, calling the GOP senator’s demand unlawful.

Ahead of the election, thousands of Mississippians were moved to inactive status because the secretary of state’s office paid $50,000 to use unverified data from credit bureau Experian to clean out voter rolls. Secretary of State Michael Watson told Mississippi Today that the rollout of the commercial data was “wildly successful.”

This unprecedented number of inactive voters led to more affidavit ballots, prolonging the count, Tarekegn said. These ballots must be …

author: Unknown
title: Constitutional Court orders retrial of Mazlum İçli after ten years in prison
content:
Mazlum İçli has already spent more than ten years of his life in prison. He was accused of involvement, at the age of 14, in the killing of four people during the Kobanê protests in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) in October 2014. He was sentenced to a total of 124 years and eight months in prison. However, evidence that could exonerate him was not adequately considered during the trial. Turkey’s Constitutional Court has now confirmed serious deficiencies in the reasoning behind the verdict and ordered a retrial. İçli’s defense team intends to seek his immediate release.


The ruling, issued on September 16, 2026, could mark a decisive turning point in a case that has been fraught with contradictions for years. At the heart of the case is the question of why İçli was convicted despite several witnesses confirming that he was attending a wedding in the district of Kulp, approximately 140 kilometers away, at the time of the alleged crime. Video footage and an expert report also support his alibi.


The Constitutional Court particularly criticized the criminal court’s failure to provide a reasoned assessment of conflicting expert reports. While one examination suggested that İçli might be identifiable in footage from the crime scene, another report by the same expert confirmed with a high degree of probability that he was present at the wedding. It remained unclear why the court had relied on the incriminating report while failing to give appropriate consideration to the exculpatory evidence.

author: Unknown
title: Women organize symposium on social memory and trauma in Amed
content:
A symposium titled “Speaking Out: Social Memory, Testimony and Trauma” began at the Ali Emiri Conference Hall in cooperation with Amed Metropolitan Municipality, the Trauma Studies Association, and the Forum for Social Peace and Freedom.


Speaking during a session titled “Waiting at Ground Zero: Trauma, Unresolved Grief and the Power of Testimony in Enforced Disappearances,” moderated by social worker İrfan Ekinci, Sebla Arcan, a member of the Human Rights Association’s (İHD) Commission on Disappearances in Custody, said, “A person experiencing trauma due to the disappearance of a loved one can neither move forward nor go back. They remain trapped in that moment.”


Highlighting the trauma caused by enforced disappearances, Arcan said, “The effects continue for two or three generations after an enforced disappearance. But other things are also passed down through generations in connection with enforced disappearances. A sense of justice, the determination to struggle, and the spirit of resistance are also transmitted. What is passed down from generation to generation is not only trauma and grief but also political consciousness.”


Emphasizing the importance of testimony, Sebla Arcan said, “Your account of what happened is denied. Some people come and take your child into custody, but when you go to inquire about their detention, the authorities deny it ever happened. Denial is the most severe form of state violence and the most profound form of trauma.”


İHD Women’s Secretary Handan Çoşkun spoke in a session titled “The Perception of Space and the Body in the Intergenerational Transmission of Grief: Sur.” Çoşkun said they had been conducting research since the 1990s into issues including the forced evacuation of villages, enforced disappearances, suicide, and numerous other subjects.


Speaking on the topic “Disenfranchised Grief: Unrecognized Suffering,” neuropsychologist Masum Aydın said, “Witnessing is fundamental to existence. We cannot become ‘us’ without the other.”


Participants then shared their testimonies and asked questions of the panelists.


The third session of the symposium was moderated by sociologist Didem Aydemir. TJA (Free Women’s Movement) activist and psychological counselor Esra Kahraman spoke on “Geography, Body and Mother Tongue: The Transmission of Memory and Healing Mechanisms among Displaced Kurdish Women in the Middle East,” while TJA activist Rojda Bedia Akkaya addressed “From Oppressed Lives to Collective Healing: The Historical Legacy of Resistance, Communal Life and Distinctive Coping Mechanisms of the Kurdish Women’s Movement.”


Referring to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Esra Kahraman emphasized the importance they attached to the process and stated that confronting the past and ensuring justice were essential to building lasting peace.


Discussing their work with women who came to Amed following the attacks on Rojava, Kahraman said they had observed how women collectively resisted suffering and hardship.


Rojda Bedia Akkaya highlighted the struggle of Kurdish women and the methods they have developed.


The symposium will continue with presentations titled “What Remains in the Body: Rights Violations, Bodily Memory and the Conditions for Healing,” “Traumatic Silence and States of Subjecthood: From Perpetration to Involvement,” “Tracing the Unspoken: The Speaking Body,” and “Traces Left in Memory and Nature: Destruction and Possibilities for Healing.”

author: Jessica Kutz
title: The Navajo Nation Just Elected Its First Woman President
content:
The Navajo Nation isn’t alone. The Seneca Nation of Indians also elected its first woman president this week.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Crystalyne Curley is set to become the first woman president of the Navajo Nation, the largest reservation by land mass in the country.

Curley, who also held the distinction of being the first woman to serve as the Nation’s council speaker — the head of its legislative branch —when she was voted by council members to fill that role in 2023, has worked on issues related to water rights, uranium contamination and voter rights.

In another first for tribal governments, the Seneca Nation of Indians in New York also elected its first woman president, Tina Abrams. She previously served two terms on the Nation’s council.

While Native women made history for their tribes in this election, it is not uncommon for women to hold top positions in tribal nations. Activist Wilma Mankiller was appointed as principal chief of the Cherokee Nation in 1985, the largest tribe in the country by tribal enrollment numbers. Though there is no official data on women’s representation in tribal governments, the nonprofit RepresentWomen found that in 2020 at least 78 tribal nations had reached or exceeded gender parity in their legislatures.

Curley’s campaign website lays out her vision as president, including prioritizing behavioral health services, affordable housing programs, workforce development and protecting Diné culture and sovereignty, among other initiatives.

Leading up to the election, Curley told Indian Country Today, a nonprofit news outlet, that she brings her perspective as a mom to the position. “I want to make sure that our children have a safe future, a safe home where they feel they’re proud of who they are,” she said.

By Navajo Nation election law, the results are considered unofficial for ten days after November 3rd. With an 1115 vote count difference between them, Curley’s opponent Justin Jones has not conceded and says he’ll launch a legal challenge over the results, according to the Navajo-Hopi Observer.

The Nation, which has the second largest number of enrolled tribal members nationwide, spans northeastern Arizona and parts of New Mexico and Utah.

author: Novara Media
title: Inside China’s Biotech Revolution
content:
In the Mao era, ‘barefoot doctors’ received just a few months of training before being sent out to straighten broken bones and administer vaccines. Now China’s researchers make world-class cancer drugs, cheap surgical robots and cutting edge brain-computer interfaces. Its doctors make AI-powered avatars of themselves to deal with ever more patients.


But China is growing old before it grows rich. Cancer, diabetes, Alzheimer’s and cardiovascular problems are ballooning. And its aging crisis is coming on faster because of the legacy of its one-child policy. How will China adapt?


Ruby Wang worked on the NHS Covid frontline before becoming Head of Health at the British Embassy in Beijing. And now she’s written

The China Cure: The Rise of Biotech, AI Medicine and a Global Health Superpower

. She tells Richard Hames how China got from barefoot doctors to high-tech hospitals, what it learned from Covid, and what the NHS could learn from China.

author: Jon Queally
title: Petition Urging Dems to Reject Jeffries as House Speaker Passes 1M Signatures
content:
“The Speaker should represent the Democratic voters, not just the Democratic establishment,” reads the petition.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

An online petition that demanding that Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) not be the next Democratic Speaker of the House has hit one million signatories on Saturday as the clamor for a leadership change within the party explodes after historic midterm wins driven by populist demands.

As of this writing, the Change.org petition — titled “House Democrats: CHOOSE A NEW SPEAKER” — has 1,007,831 verified signatories, with the number rapidly rising.

While the final totals are not yet established, Democrats emerged from Tuesday’s elections with at least 254 seats in the next Congress, reclaiming the majority from the Republicans who currently can count on just 162 seats when new members are sworn in come January.

While Jeffries is clearly the presumptive choice for Democrats, and he formally put himself in the running on Wednesday with a letter to all members, outside progressives have voiced serious opposition given his failure to embrace many of the positions — including backing Medicare for All, taking on entrenched corporate power, and restricting military assistance to Israel over its genocide in Gaza — that have animated voters nationwide this election cycle.

We believe the Speaker should represent the Democratic voters, not just the Democratic establishment.

The Speaker has enormous influence over the direction of the House, including its legislative priorities and agenda. Before casting their votes, representatives should closely examine Jeffries’s public record, policy positions, campaign donor record and leadership … and listen to constituents who do not want him elevated to Speaker.

This is not a foregone conclusion. There is still time for other Democratic members of the House to step forward and seek the nomination for Speaker, someone whose priorities more closely reflect the voters who hope to elect the Democratic majority.

We are calling on every member of the incoming 120th Congress to vote against Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker in January 2027 and choose a different candidate.

Axios reported Friday that members of Congress have been “inundated” with calls urging them not to elect Jeffries and suggested that some of the hesitations are not just among progressives.

The outlet reporting interviewing “nearly a half-dozen incoming House Democrats in deeply red seats Thursday who declined to state a firm position one way or another on voting for him.”

Sign this petition if you want a new speaker of the house. https://t.co/G88VLySjsQ

As Corbin Trent, the former top aide to Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) who now runs a progressive organizing outfit called A Fight Worth Having, wrote in a column published at Common Dreams on Friday, “the Democratic leadership we have today is completely ill-suited for this moment. They do not have the vision for what it’s going to take to rebuild the trust the American people have lost in their government, their institutions, and the Democratic Party itself.”

“Democrats have spoken loudly and clearly that they want new leadership,” Trent said of the election. “Unfortunately, too many of the people in Washington aren’t listening.”

While the large Democratic majority in the House makes it easier for Jeffries to maneuver leading up to the leadership vote, and given that no challenger has stepped forward to take him on directly, the betting money is still safe that Jeffries will be the next Speaker of the House.

But the public push denouncing him as the wrong choice of leadership in a moment where Democratic voters are clearly demanding — and expecting — a much bolder agenda, the pressure may yet have an impact on his calculations.

title: Radical Hope From Gaza
content:

RADICAL HOPE FROM GAZA: A COLLECTION OF ESSAYS BY AYA AL-HATTAB

An Introduction from the Editors-in-Chief of Solarpunk Magazine

What does it mean to hold on to hope when the world around you is being destroyed? What does it mean to imagine a better future when even the possibility of an ordinary tomorrow feels uncertain at best?

In this powerful six-part series, Palestinian writer and journalist Aya Al-Hattab takes us into the lived realities of Gaza, offering an intimate and deeply human perspective on war, occupation, displacement, loss, and the struggle to preserve hope. Through personal reflections, historical examination, and stories of everyday compassion, Al-Hattab reveals the profound consequences of violence on people, communities, animals, and the places they call home.

Throughout these essays, a central truth emerges: hope requires the courage to imagine a future beyond the suffering of the present, even when that future feels impossibly distant. Sometimes that hope takes the form of caring for a beloved animal, remembering a familiar street, or simply dreaming of a home filled with books and loved ones.

At Solarpunk Magazine, we believe imagining better futures is inseparable from confronting the injustices that prevent them. Aya’s writing reminds us why those futures are so important, and why the right to peace, dignity, freedom, and an ordinary life is worth fighting for.

We are deeply honored to share her words. We invite you to read these essays with open hearts, to bear witness, and to consider what radical hope demands of all of us.

author: Randi Beers
title: News quiz Nov. 7 | Quitting, drifting, paving
content:
We’ve made it out of another week alive. Can you answer these questions five?


1.

 This week, MLA Brian Koonoo announced his resignation from cabinet. He estimated there were about “10,000 reasons” for his departure. Which of the following were not one of those reasons?


A.

 He misses hunting.


B.

 He misses being able to support his constituency.


C.

 He misses the beautiful mountain views from Pond Inlet.


2.

 According to a new study published in the journal Arctic Science, what is drifting from Iqaluit into surrounding lakes?


A.

 Cigarette smoke


B.

 Microplastics


C.

 Garbage


3.

 Nunavut Brewing Co. has stopped canning its beer after the Government of Nunavut’s Finance Department changed its markup structure. As a result, markups are now tied to the percentage of alcohol in a particular drink. NuBrew’s strongest beer, Frob Gold Strong Ale, is what per cent alcohol by volume?


A.

 6 per cent


B.

 6.4 per cent


C.

 6.8 per cent


4.

 Transportation and Infrastructure Minister George Hickes announced last week that the federal government is committing $3.5 million towards planning a runway paving project in Cambridge Bay. When does the actual paving work start, according to Hickes?


A.

 The sooner the better


B.

 Late 2027, if all goes well


C.

 Summer 2028


5.

 Players from which professional hockey team were in Iqaluit over the weekend to train young athletes?


A.

 The Toronto Blue Jays


B.

 The Toronto Sceptres


C.

 The Toronto Raptors


 


Nunavut Brewing Co.’s canning machine is idle after the Nunavut Liquor and Cannabis Commission changed the way it prices its retail products. (Photo by Daron Letts)


Answers:


1.

 C — Tununiq MLA Brian Koonoo might miss the breathtaking mountain views from his hamlet of Pond Inlet, but he didn’t specifically

cite that among his reasons

 for resigning from cabinet. The former environment minister misses his family, hunting, and being able to advocate for his constituents.


2.

 B — Scientists studied lake water upwind from Iqaluit and downwind from Iqaluit and

concluded

 that microplastics are likely drifting into the environment from the city.


3.

 C — Frob Gold Strong Ale is 6.8 per cent alcohol by volume. Under the

new markup structure

, the Finance Department applies a $2.50 markup to beers stronger than six per cent.


4.

 A — Transportation and Infrastructure Minister George Hickes

did not provide

 an estimate for when Cambridge Bay’s runway might be paved. But he’s hoping the federal government moves quickly. “The sooner the better,” he said.


5.

 B — Players and a coach from the

Toronto Sceptres

, a Professional Women’s Hockey League team, were in Iqaluit Oct. 30 to Nov. 2 to run drills, lead workouts and host scrimmage exercises.

title: Seriously ill prisoner Tuncer Sağlam dies in Ankara
content:
Seriously ill political prisoner Tuncer Sağlam died in Ankara on Saturday morning. Sağlam was arrested and imprisoned in 2024 in the province of Van on charges of “propaganda for a terrorist organization.” Due to his critical health condition, he had most recently been receiving treatment at Etlik Hospital in Ankara, where he died after 25 days of treatment.


Sağlam was initially held at Van High-Security Prison. After his health deteriorated significantly, he was transferred to Sincan Prison No. 2 in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on October 9. His condition continued to worsen during his subsequent hospitalization, and he eventually had to be intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation.


Following the completion of the autopsy, Tuncer Sağlam’s body is expected to be transferred to his hometown of Van, where he will be laid to rest.

author: Unknown
title: Mihemed: Women’s participation in decision making is a fundamental guarantee for future Syria
content:
Ruksen Mihemed, spokesperson for the Women’s Protection Units (YPJ), emphasized that guaranteeing the rights of Syrian women and enhancing their presence in decision-making positions constitute a fundamental pillar of any political process aimed at building a democratic, pluralistic Syria. She stressed the necessity of recognizing women’s roles and sacrifices, as well as ensuring their meaningful inclusion in shaping the country’s future.


​Ruksen Mihemed stated that over fifteen years of struggle and endeavor, the YPJ has played a historic role in transforming the reality of women and elevating their status in society. She noted that the units’ journey was not limited to military action and societal defense, but extended to empowering women in political, social, educational, and military fields, establishing their role as key partners in decision-making.


​

Women’s Protection Units: Fifteen years of struggle and empowerment


​ Ruksen Mihemed explained that the establishment of the Women’s Protection Units marked a pivotal turning point in women’s resistance, proving that women possess the ability to protect themselves, organize their ranks, and assume responsibilities across various walks of life.


​She added that the units evolved into a school of struggle and consciousness, helping women discover their identity, history, and rights. Meanwhile, the resistance and leadership of the female fighters became a symbol of courage, freedom, and resolve demonstrating women’s capacity to assert their presence and participate in all spheres of life.


​

Lack of genuine representation of women in the political process


​Regarding the political process in Syria, Ruksen Mihemed underscored the need to guarantee women’s participation in decision-making and administrative positions. She stressed that Syrian women possess vast expertise and potential gained through long years of struggle, practice, and experience, giving them the right to be essential partners in outlining the future of their country.


​She criticized the Syrian Interim Government for not taking sufficient steps thus far under the January 29 Agreement to guarantee women’s rights and enhance their presence in decision-making roles, noting that the status women have attained remains below their aspirations, role, and sacrifices.


She added that the YPJ sent fighters’ records and relevant documentation but has not received a clear response to date, while proposed measures and procedures are moving extremely slowly, hindering immediate and genuine female participation.


​

Formation of two women’s battalions amid talks with the Ministry of Interior


​Discussing participation in the security and military spheres, Ruksen Mihemed confirmed that Syrian women hold significant expertise and experience in defense and security. She noted that following a series of meetings and talks with the Ministry of Interior, the approval for forming two women’s battalions was ultimately proposed.


​She specified that the first battalion will fall under Aleppo Governorate—covering the areas of Kobani and Afrin—while the second battalion will fall under Hasakah Governorate.


​

Women’s participation is a non-negotiable right


​ Ruksen Mihemed concluded her statements by reaffirming that guaranteeing women’s rights and active presence across political, military, and administrative sectors represents a core demand rather than mere symbolic representation. She stressed that women must be true partners in decision-making, institution-building, and defining the contours of Syria’s upcoming phase.


​She emphasized that any political process seeking to build a stable and democratic future in Syria must be grounded in recognizing women’s will and rights, while ensuring their effective and equal participation in all facets of life.

title: Final declaration of the Conference on the Social Institutionalization of Women’s Policies
content:
Women’s policies in Kurdish municipalities are no longer to be limited to individual institutions or social services but are intended to shape every aspect of municipal self-governance. This was one of the key outcomes of the Conference on the Social Institutionalization of Women’s Policies, held on November 2 and 3 in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). In a final declaration published following the event, participants outlined a comprehensive program to rebuild municipal women’s structures, promote women’s economic self-determination, and ensure their organized participation in political decision-making.


Organized by the Women’s Council of Democratic Local Administrations and hosted by Amed Metropolitan Municipality, the conference was held under the slogan “Through Production and Organizing, We Embed Our Women’s Struggle in Society.” Through a total of 21 resolutions, the participating women’s organizations aim to establish a new organizational, financial, and social foundation for municipal women’s policies.


This approach is also shaped by years of state intervention in Kurdish municipal politics. The appointment of government trustees led to the closure of numerous women’s institutions, the abolition of independent municipal programs for women, and the dismantling of structures built up over many years. The conference therefore views the rebuilding of these institutions not merely as an administrative task but as part of the struggle for democratic self-governance and social transformation.


Rebuilding after years of state-imposed trusteeship


Over the decades, the Kurdish women’s movement has developed an approach to municipal governance that regards women’s liberation as a prerequisite for a democratic society. This includes autonomous women’s councils, solidarity-based economic models, institutions providing protection against violence, and women’s participation in political decision-making processes. With the removal of elected municipal administrations and the appointment of government trustees, these structures were systematically undermined in many cities across North Kurdistan. The final declaration describes the consequences as profound damage to both municipal institutions and their roots in society.


The participants therefore see themselves as facing a dual task: rights and institutions secured through years of struggle must be restored, while new structures must be so firmly rooted in society that women’s policies no longer depend solely on the political composition of a particular municipal administration.


“Overcoming the damage caused by state-imposed trusteeship, strengthening the achievements of women once again, and ensuring their permanent institutionalization are among our fundamental tasks for the period ahead,” the declaration stated.


The conference links this objective to a fundamental transformation of municipal decision-making processes. In the future, women’s policies are no longer to be the exclusive responsibility of dedicated women’s departments. Instead, all municipal departments are to be required to incorporate women’s needs, rights, and perspectives into their planning, budgets, and services.


Women’s policies to shape all municipal decisions


One of the most far-reaching resolutions concerns the institutional status of women’s policies. The conference called for principles of women’s liberation to be formally incorporated into the regulations, responsibilities, and working procedures of all municipal institutions.


This applies not only to social services and protection against violence but also to urban planning, economic development, education, culture, transportation, and the allocation of public funds.


Gender-responsive budgeting is particularly important in this regard. Municipal budgets are to be more closely aligned with the realities of women’s lives and their needs. At the same time, financial resources allocated to women’s policies are to be secured, and women’s organizations are to be involved in the preparation, implementation, and oversight of municipal budgets.


The conference also called for women’s departments to be strengthened in terms of staffing and technical resources. Existing shortcomings in premises, equipment, and organizational responsibilities are to be systematically identified and addressed through binding action plans.

author: Finley Williams
title: AI Companies Are Preying on Under-Resourced Schools, Students Say
content:
Poorer schools are being lured into spending their limited funds on AI tech in the face of chronic understaffing.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

When high school librarian Tara Donnelly talks to her classes about how AI has changed online search, she always starts with one question: “What is Google’s main goal?”

Students generally reply, “give you information,” or “tell you the answers to things” — until someone hits the nail on the head and ventures, “Make money.”

Donnelly, a member of the AI working group in the Chicago Teachers Union, says Google is one of many tech companies that are centrally motivated by profit, despite purporting to serve other aims. As AI developers like Microsoft and OpenAI push to integrate their products into U.S. schools and pupils’ lives more broadly, Donnelly said she believes that students are entitled to a clear understanding of the forces shaping their education.

“The ed tech industry is profiting off of running a race with school districts to see who’s going to adopt their chatbot or whatever their tech piece is, and it’s forced on students,” Donelly told Truthout. “Students should have the opportunity to refuse to use AI if they want to. They deserve to have the whole picture and not just to be the money-maker for these ed tech pieces.”

“Students should have the opportunity to refuse to use AI if they want to.”

Indeed, experts, education advocates, and students interviewed by Truthout portrayed a bleak reality in which desperation creates pressure for marginalized students to use AI, and for under-resourced schools to adopt it as a surface-level solution to structural problems like chronic underfunding and understaffing. Many education policy analysts say that in the absence of conclusive evidence that AI improves learning outcomes, companies’ pitch of AI tools as an educational cure-all distracts from more pressing needs: holistic, culturally responsive education that prioritizes human interaction and productive struggle.

Donnelly — an educator at Foreman College and Career Academy, a predominantly Latine school on Chicago’s Northwest Side — said she thinks about these concerns specifically in the context of racially equitable schooling.

“Whenever we’re talking about education, we’re talking about students of color. We always have to be very intentional about, how is this going to affect these students and what do we need to do differently?” Donnelly said.

Yeisbel Peña, a Latino high school senior in Boston who is interested in computer science, said it’s possible for young students to use AI to advance their thinking. But “raw education — just one-on-one, [the] old type of education — is the most appropriate way a person can actually engage and learn,” he said.

“When you have AI, it just says ‘yes,’ constantly. Any question you ask, it’ll probably just tell you yes,” Peña told Truthout. “It won’t give you complexity. And I believe that that complexity that you get from being in a classroom with a teacher … without it, you’re kind of just limiting yourself.”

Still, he said that in the absence of well-staffed after-school homework help, students at his charter school, which mostly serves students of color, often turn to chatbots instead. Peña described classrooms with only one teacher to assist 10 or 20 students.

“All of them trying to get one-on-one help, it definitely gets very diluted,” Peña said. “So you definitely don’t get the best quality of help.”

In Raleigh, North Carolina, Sacdiya Rashid, 17, said she sometimes chooses to turn to chatbots, which have helped her understand difficult math problems. Though she said that students can harm their learning by becoming over-reliant on the technology, she believes there are commercial influences at play beyond any individual student’s choices.

“I think these AI companies are trying to benefit off of students, like, struggling students,” she told Truthout.

“I don’t think we should really blame students for these AI companies and [the] narratives they’re trying to push. Because I think it just hurts the students,” Rashid said.

Indeed, students at Donnelly’s school in Chicago nominally have access to after-school tutoring, but the primarily immigrant, first-generation and high-poverty student body was hit hard by “Operation Midway Blitz,” President Donald Trump’s anti-immigration raids in the city …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: El filósofo Miguel Benasayag conversa acerca de la inteligencia artificial
content:
.


Argentina: El filósofo Miguel Benasayag conversa acerca de la inteligencia artificial y lo que distingue a los seres vivos de las máquinas


video:


https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=87WpAiOtiIE


Transcripción parcial de la entrevista:


4 noviembre 2026


…hoy tenemos una entrevista realmente increíble con Miguel Benasayag, es un filósofo, psicoanalista, investigador en epistemología y ex militante del PRT-ERP, donde pasó diez años. Nos pidió especialmente que lo presentemos como parte todavía de esa militancia porque sigue hasta el día de hoy siendo un investigador militante muy comprometido con la realidad social.


Nació en 1953, estuvo preso cuatro años durante la dictadura, mientras militaba, hasta que en el 78 se exilió y desde entonces vive en París. Dirige tres laboratorios donde toca de diversos temas relacionados algunos más a lo social, a la inteligencia artificial y a cuestiones también del cerebro, y editó una cantidad enorme de libros. Es coautor de más de 40 libros.


Entre los últimos y de los que más estuvimos leyendo para preparar esta entrevista tenemos La singularidad de lo vivo, (1:46) editado por Prometeo. La inteligencia artificial no piensa, el cerebro tampoco, que escribió con Ariel Penici, de Prometeo Editorial, y también su libro más reciente La época de la intranquilidad, (1:59) también de Prometeo Editorial.


…antes de arrancar, recordarles que Miguel está realizando un seminario llamado Hibridación en La Tribu… Ambos tienen modalidad virtual y presencial, así que pueden googlear «Hibridación Benasayag» y ahí les va a aparecer toda la información. Este es un podcast de La Izquierda Diario.


Bueno Miguel, cómo estás? Muchas gracias por estar acá.


-Estoy bien, estoy contento de estar acá. Gracias a ustedes por la invitación. La verdad que un gran placer de nuestra parte.


Bueno, queríamos arrancar para empezar por algún lado, porque la verdad que la diversidad de temas sobre la cual te queríamos preguntar es enorme, pero estuvo estas semanas mucho en discusión, en debate, si nosotros, las máquinas, la IA, pensamos, no piensan, que tienen conciencia, etc. ¿Qué es pensar? A mí en particular me llamó la atención que en algunas entrevistas vos hablabas como el proceso de pensar empieza como medio ajeno a uno o antes de que uno sea consciente. Transmitías una idea así.


¿Qué es pensar?


Bueno mira, yo diría que hay dos dimensiones del pensamiento. Los cuerpos piensan en el sentido que hay un pensamiento, más bien que se pasa como con formas. Elaboración de formas. ¿Esto qué quiere decir? Quiere decir que todos los cuerpos vivos, inclusive las plantas, no corresponden a una mecánica que responde mecánicamente al exterior, sino que lo que viene del exterior como perturbación tiene una reacción propia. O sea que lo vivo tiene una reacción propia orgánica.


Esa reacción se pasa por lo que diríamos formas, formas más o menos adecuadas que pueden adaptarse o no a lo que pasa. Bueno, eso es el modo de pensamiento de los cuerpos y mismo de los ecosistemas a veces. Hay un pensamiento que va a emerger mucho más tarde que es el pensamiento simbólico.


Pensamiento simbólico que corresponde a principios de la razón. O sea, los organismos funcionan con una coherencia orgánica que no es lógica. Es como una espiral, son regulaciones, ciclos, ritmos, ¿verdad? Que no corresponde a una lógica formal lineal.


El pensamiento formal es cuando de repente la humanidad encuentra a este otro de ella y se vuelve humanidad, que es esta mixidad que tenemos, ¿no? Que es un problema, ¿no? Que es que participamos de un pensamiento lógico formal siendo a la vez animales que funcionamos dentro de esta coherencia no lógica. El pensamiento lógico formal va a aparecer, inclusive para los que les guste Spinoza les digo que el pensamiento del cual habla Spinoza, que es coextensivo de lo extenso, es el pensamiento de las formas. Porque si no, no hubiera habido pensamiento hasta que no aparece el lenguaje, ¿se entiende? Bueno, es un pequeño paréntesis para los que conocen a Don Baruch, ¿no? El pensamiento formal va a emerger como una formación, ¿no? Una formación en un momento dado cuando la humanidad se humaniza, que es la lengua.


O sea, claro, aparece como la lengua directamente, donde hay una continuidad lógica, donde no todo es posible de decir, ¿viste? Como es muy complicado expresar un sentimiento, por ejemplo, ¿no? Por eso la poesía, la literatura, ¿no? Por eso vamos hacia gestos, ¿no? Porque el pensamiento …

author: CMI Argentina
title: El fiscal Pollicita descartó que Adorni se haya enriquecido: pidió que lo investiguen por posible evasión
content:
El fiscal, como argumentó la defensa del exvocero, aseguró que no se pudo probar que el incremento patrimonial se originó durante su paso por la función pública. Define el juez Ariel Lijo.


Foto: Antonio Becerra


Por Ariel Stemphelet @stempheletariel


Otro viernes de buenas noticias para el gobierno de Javier Milei y el ecosistema libertario. El fiscal federal Gerardo Pollicita determinó que por el momento no corresponde llamar a indagatoria al exjefe de Gabinete Manuel Adorni ni que se lo investigue por enriquecimiento ilícito. Para el representante del Ministerio Público, la causa debe pasar al Fuero en lo Penal Económico e investigarse como una “infracción” penal tributaria.


“Con la prueba aunada no se ha podido descartar que el capital principal se haya formado entre 2014 y 2018, como fuera alegado, varios años antes del 14 de diciembre de 2023 (NdR: cuando asumió como funcionario público)”, expuso el fiscal.


El eje central de la postura del fiscal es que no hay elementos para que siga la investigación por enriquecimiento ilícito sino que se trata de un caso de “posible evasión”.


En el mismo dictamen al que accedió

Tiempo

, Pollicita sentenció que no se encontró un vínculo directo entre su incremento patrimonial y un hecho previo que pueda tomarse como origen de ese crecimiento. “Tampoco pudo vincularse el monto por el que fue requerido con un acto funcional, una contraprestación o una fuente ilícita asociada a la función”, afirmó.


El ex jefe de Gabinete y ex vocero del gobierno libertario había esgrimido que el incremento patrimonial se explicaba debido a inversiones en Bitcoin que había hecho a partir de sus

ahorros familiares de toda la vida

. Después explicó que esas inversiones fueron entre 2014 y 2018, por medio de las que obtuvo u$s 591.544,61 que no declaró al asumir como funcionario público.


Recién expuso esas ganancias ante la Oficina Anticorrupción en junio de 2026, cuando ya estaba en desarrollo la causa judicial iniciada a partir de la denuncia de la diputada nacional Marcela Pagano.


Además, en septiembre la defensa de Adorni presentó la respuesta al requerimiento de justificación patrimonial de 20 preguntas que le había remitido Pollicita. Allí declaró ocho direcciones que usó para operar Bitcoin. Según el documento firmado este viernes por el fiscal, se detectó que “tuvieron efectivamente actividad entre 2014 y 2018”. Sin embargo, al someterlas a la investigación, no se pudo establecer “quién las controlaba, con quién se concertaron las ventas, a qué precio ni de qué modo se recibieron y conservaron los dólares billete”.


En el dictamen, el fiscal citó el resultado de un informe del Departamento de Cibercrimen de la Policía Federal. “Concluyó (…) que ninguna de las medidas actualmente disponibles permitiría establecer de manera concluyente que las direcciones fueron controladas por una persona distinta del requerido (por Adorni) por lo que nuevas diligencias orientadas a esa atribución difícilmente alterarían ese resultado”, agregó.


Posible evasión


Frente a ese panorama, el fiscal señaló que el comportamiento podría tomarse como una infracción al Régimen Penal Tributario. “La misma explicación introducida por la defensa da contenido a la hipótesis tributaria, porque la fuente anterior a la función que el requerido invoca se compone, según su propio relato, de recursos que no fueron informados al organismo recaudador”, marcó en el dictamen.


El cambio de figura resulta favorable para la estrategia defensiva de Adorni, a cargo del abogado Matías Ledesma. De hecho, al responder el requerimiento de justificación patrimonial, el propio letrado había mencionado la posibilidad de que lo investiguen por evasión, no por enriquecimiento. Si bien la posición del fiscal tiene que ser revisada por el juez federal Ariel Lijo, al ex funcionario se le abrió el escenario de posibilidades.


En principio, perdió fuerza la posibilidad de ser condenado por enriquecimiento ilícito, una figura que contempla pena de prisión de 2 a 6 años junto con la inhabilitación perpetua para ser funcionario público. Si lo investigan por evasión, se abre la posibilidad de que eventualmente tenga que afrontar como consecuencia el pago de la deuda tributaria para extinguir la acción penal.


Fuente:

author: Corey Larocque
title: Six months to fix foster care failures is a tall order
content:
Six months isn’t much time to fix a problem that has festered for 15 years.


But that’s the task ahead for the Government of Nunavut after the federal auditor general presented a scathing report on the state of foster care in Nunavut, pointing to “fundamental weaknesses” that have persisted for years.


Deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes presented the report titled

Foster Care in Nunavut

 on Tuesday. It’s the fifth time the office of the auditor general — responsible for probing the effectiveness of government programs — has looked into Nunavut’s foster care since 2011.


The Family Services Department can remove children from their family homes and place them in foster care when their parents aren’t able to meet their needs or provide a safe environment.


This week’s

report

 is a litany of failures — basic things the GN’s Family Services Department didn’t do well enough. It includes failing to do in-person checks on children once a month in 90 per cent of the files the auditor general looked at. In five cases, there was no documented contact with the child in more than a year.


Screening of foster caregivers was weak. In just 52 per cent of cases, the department completed the home studies to assess whether a new foster home was a safe environment to place a child in.


And the department didn’t provide the caregivers it relies on with adequate tools, information or financial support.


In March, there were approximately 400 children receiving protective services, including 260 who had been removed from their family home. But the government doesn’t actually know the precise number of children in care because the department relied on a manual list instead of one generated by a software package known as Matrix that was introduced three years ago.


Premier John Main and Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok held a press conference Wednesday to

respond

 to the report. But their explanations boiled down to “we’re working on it; we’re trying to do better.”


Main called the report “upsetting” and pledged a “whole government-wide effort” to make improvements. Time will tell. The “whole-of-government” line is one that politicians use to convey a sense of urgency or that something is a priority.


“Our sincere hope is that future audits will show real improvement,” Main said.


Does the GN really need a government-wide effort? What help can the Environment Department, for example, offer in terms of fixing the foster care system? Instead of a government-wide effort, why not just get Family Services’ house in order?


Healey Akearok said her department is making progress. Workers are getting trained on the Matrix system, 97 per cent of home studies have been done and 82 per cent of annual reviews have been completed.


“There’s still work to be done,” she said.


Hayes said Tuesday, the auditor general’s office will be back in the spring to release another report on the GN’s “quality assurance” work. Family Services pointed to the quality assurance framework it implemented to address at least four of the report’s recommendations, including calls to provide support payments to caregivers, determining if a child in care has special needs, and emphasizing to social services workers the importance of documenting care plans.


The report makes you wonder about Nunavut’s capacity to deliver bigger, more complex programs — like health care and education.


Foster care is a relatively small part of the GN’s operations. If there are so many “fundamental weaknesses” in foster care, imagine the weaknesses that must exist in other departments.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Trabajadores de las radios públicas porteñas rechazan la pre adjudicación ilegítima de sus medios
content:
Este miércoles se publicó en el boletín oficial de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires la preadjudicación de las radios públicas de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires por los próximos 5 años, a la Unión Transitoria que conforman las firmas Green Umbrella Producciones SAS y JR Comunicaciones SRL. Los trabajadores y las trabajadoras de La Once Diez (AM 1110) y La 2×4 (FM 92.7) rechazan este intento de privatización encubierta porque se trata de una acción plenamente inconstitucional e ilegal, y afirman que es urgente que la justicia se expida.


A través de un comunicado, los trabajadores y las trabajadoras afirman que el Jefe de Gobierno, Jorge Macri, incumple el mandato de la propia Constitución de la Ciudad, que en su artículo 47 garantiza la existencia de medios de comunicación propios, destinados a difundir la actividad oficial y a promover la cultura y la educación, bajo gestión estatal; y viola además el artículo 44 de la Ley de Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual, que establece el principio de indelegabilidad de la explotación de las frecuencias asignadas a dichos servicios de comunicación audiovisual.


Los trabajadores señalan que la preadjudicación de Radio de la Ciudad (AM 1110) y La 2×4 (FM 92.7) a la Unión Transitoria, integrada por Green Umbrella Producciones SAS y JR Comunicaciones SRL, abre una serie de interrogantes sobre su idoneidad para asumir la gestión de las radios públicas.


“Incluso si dejáramos de lado la plena ilegalidad de este proceso, según la información disponible estas empresas no cuentan con antecedentes suficientes en la administración integral de emisoras ni en la gestión de medios públicos. La incorporación de actividades radiofónicas en el objeto comercial de Green Umbrella no demuestra experiencia efectiva en la operación de una radio. La trayectoria de JR Comunicaciones, en tanto, se vincula principalmente con la actividad gráfica. No tendrían entonces expertise en la gestión de medios públicos, ni podrían ser calificados como profesionales del rubro, tal como reclaman los funcionarios porteños; incumpliendo con la expectativa de que ‘un privado puede hacerlo mejor’, tal como declaró Jorge Macri al anunciar la licitación de los medios públicos de la ciudad. También plantean dudas los contratos que mantienen o mantuvieron con el gobierno porteño. En el caso de Green Umbrella, llama la atención además que uno de sus fundadores, Rodrigo Matías Morán, ocupó una banca en la Legislatura porteña en 2021 dentro del espacio Vamos Juntos, vinculado directamente al Ejecutivo de la Ciudad”, detallan.


Además, recuerdan que en una primera licitación, el gobierno porteño ya adjudicó el Canal de la Ciudad al empresario Augusto Marini, que está al frente del Grupo Cale, dueño de los streamings Carajo y Blender: “Llamativamente ahora Marini no querría avanzar con la concesión hasta que el gobierno porteño le garantice que el traspaso sea ‘sin empleados en el Canal’. Demostrando el desprecio por quienes desde hace años sostenemos y le aseguramos valor y calidad a los medios públicos de la ciudad”, afirman.


Es por todo esto que los trabajadores reiteraron su reclamo a los jueces de la Sala III de la Cámara de Apelaciones, para que den lugar a la medida cautelar que ya cuenta con dictamen favorable de la Fiscalía General de dicha cámara, donde solicitan que “se frene este intento de ceder a un privado el patrimonio del público, que es el derecho a medios estatales, que cumplan el rol social de brindar comunicación de calidad, sin ataduras comerciales ni de otro tipo”.


“La causa que iniciamos contiene en su expediente con un informe favorable del ENaCom en el que los apoderados del organismo aseguraron que la licitación se encuentra ‘en colisión con expresas previsiones legales y reglamentarias, tendientes a precaver sobre la delegación de la explotación de los medios de comunicación autorizados en su favor’”, agregan.


“Los medios públicos cumplen una función esencial para la comunicación en una sociedad democrática: informar con criterios de interés general, dar lugar y promover todas las voces, fomentar la cultura y generar espacios de interacción para y con los vecinos de la Ciudad; funciones que difícilmente puedan sostenerse bajo la lógica exclusiva de la rentabilidad comercial.


Somos las y los profesionales que desde hace 99 años hacemos llegar el Teatro Colón a todo el país; quienes desde hace 26 años hacemos sonar el Tango en todo el mundo. Las radios de la ciudad no son un negocio. Son patrimonio …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Adiós a Patricia Walsh, esa compañera que siempre estuvo en el lado correcto de la historia de nuestro pueblo
content:
Por Carlos Aznárez, Resumen Latinoamericano


Patricia, la más pequeña pero no menos importante de esa familia de patriotas revolucionarios y revolucionarias que comandaba tu padre, el montonero, el periodista, el escritor, el imprescindible. Patricia hermana querida de Viki, caída en combate en la batalla de la calle Corro. Patricia, la que nunca dejó de estar en aquellos gloriosos años 70 en que los compañeros y compañeras peleábamos por la Revolución y el Socialismo. Patricia, la que masculló su rabia el nefasto día en que los marinos genocidas intentaron secuestrar a Rodolfo, después de dar a conocer su Carta abierta a la Junta Militar, y éste resistió hasta entregar su vida para impedirlo. La misma que, ahuyentando todos los peligros, fuiste hasta el domicilio de tu padre y de su compañera Lilia, preocupada porque no tenías ninguna señal de su paradero, y sin entrar en el lugar pudiste ver los destrozos que habían hecho los milicos. Patricia, la que años después aguantó como pudo la irreparable pérdida de su hija María Eva, y ni siquiera en tan terribles circunstancias dejaste de reivindicar la vida y la lucha que la habita en todos los momentos y en cada circunstancia.


Patricia, militante de HIJOS, junto a los que peleaste por la memoria fértil de tantas y tantos madres, padres, hermanos, a los que el sistema, el de ayer y el de hoy, trata otra vez de hacer desaparecer. Patricia, la que impulsaste, desde tu cargo de diputada, y con toda la fuerza de tus principios revolucionarios, el proyecto de

Nulidad de las Leyes de Punto Final y Obediencia Debida

, esos dos engendros que el sistema intentaba encajar con forceps en la democracia «controlada» y «dependiente».


Y por supuesto, que también fuiste periodista, psicóloga social, militante de izquierda, feminista, rebelde ante las injusticias, pero por sobre todo, digna reivindicadora de la trayectoria de tu viejo y de tu hermana, militantes montoneros, cuya memoria defendiste, no dejando que nadie se apropiara con oportunismo de la misma y del legado de sus hermosas vidas entregadas a la causa de los trabajadores y trabajadoras.


A partir de hoy no te tendremos más físicamente, pero nos acompañarán tu sonrisa compañera, tus enojos y rabietas cuando algo no salía como te lo habías imaginado, tu maravillosa pasión por darle para adelante a pesar de que -como siempre nos pasó- las derrotas parecían sumar más escalones que las victorias. Pero nunca consiguieron amilanarte todos aquellos que solo saben hablar con la voz de la violencia del poder, ni tampoco cooptarte con los cantos de sirena de falsos progresismos que tiempos después terminaban derrumbados por fuego cruzado.


Te despido compañera, y lo hago recordando ese enorme abrazo que nos dimos cuando en plena calle Arenales nos cruzamos de pura casualidad, o por esos encuentros que pacta el destino, aquel día del mes de octubre del 76. Ya había sucedido lo de la calle Corro, y por supuesto nos emocionamos hasta las lágrimas durante varios minutos, mientras repetíamos, recordando a Viki, y como una clave para seguir sobreviviendo: “LOMJE, LOMJE”. Libres o Muertos jamás esclavos.


Hasta la Victoria Siempre, compañera Patricia Walsh.


Fuente:

https://www.resumenlatinoamericano.org/2026/11/05/argentina-patricia-walsh-esa-companera-que-siempre-estuvo-en-el-lado-correcto-de-la-historia-de-nuestro-pueblo/

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.

author: Unknown
title: Candan Yüceer YENİ Parti'den istifa etti
content:
Tekirdağ Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Candan Yüceer, YENİ Parti üyeliğinden istifa ettiğini duyurdu.


Yüceer, bugün sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, hasta olduğu dönemde düzenlenen il kongresinde kurultay delegeliği üzerinden yaşanan tartışmalara ve kendisinin delege listesine alınmamasına tepki gösterdi. "Benim aradığım yol arkadaşlığı bu değil" dedi. Şunları kaydetti:


"Bugün itibarıyla üyesi olduğum YENİ Parti'den istifa ediyorum. Ben siyaseti koltuk hesabı yapmak için yapmadım. Benim mücadelem hiçbir zaman kişisel ikbal mücadelesi olmadı. Ancak üzülerek görüyorum ki bugün bazıları kendi kişisel ikbalinin, makamının ve koltuğunun hesabına düşmüş durumda.


Son olarak benim hasta yatağında olduğum bir dönemde il kongresinde gündemin kurultay delegeliği üzerinden tartışmaya dönüştürülmesini ve bu tartışmalar nedeniyle kongrenin başlatılmamasını, şahsımın kurultay delegesi olarak dahi yazılmamasını kabul edilebilir bulmuyorum. Burada mesele bir delege listesinde kimin olup olmaması değildir.


Mesele yıllarca birlikte mücadele etmiş insanlara gösterilmesi gereken saygıdır. Mesele yol arkadaşlığı hukukudur. Mesele seçilmiş bir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanına gösterilmesi gereken siyasi nezakettir. Mesele birlikte yürüdüğümüz insanların birbirine nasıl davrandığıdır.


Benim beklediğim vefa, benim aradığım yol arkadaşlığı bu değil. Yol arkadaşlığı hukukunun bu kadar kolay çiğnendiği, kişisel çıkarların ortak değerlerin önüne geçirildiği bir anlayışın içinde yokum. Benim önceliğim de sorumluluğum da çok açık: Tekirdağ.


Benim her sabah uyandığımda düşündüğüm şey Tekirdağ’ın hangi sorununu çözeceğimiz, hangi yatırımını tamamlayacağımız, hangi projemizi hayata geçireceğimiz.


11 ilçemizde yaşayan vatandaşlarımız bizden hizmet bekliyor. Altyapı bekliyor, yol bekliyor, su bekliyor, sosyal destek bekliyor. Tekirdağ’ın kaybedecek bir günü bile yok. Benim önceliğim siyasi hesaplaşmalar değil, Tekirdağ'a hizmettir, Tekirdağ'ın bekleyen sorunları, devam eden yatırımları ve halkımıza verdiğimiz sözlerdir.


Ben enerjimi kentin geleceğine harcamayı tercih ediyorum. Bizim mücadelemizde, yolumuzda, önceliğimizde Tekirdağ’ın daha güçlü, daha adil, daha yaşanabilir bir kent olmasıdır. Ben bu göreve Tekirdağ’a hizmet etmek için geldim. Biz başımız dik, alnımız açık, hemşerilerimize karşı sorumluluğumuzun bilinciyle yolumuza devam edeceğiz. Ve bütün gücümle Tekirdağ’ıma olan sevgim ve bu güzel şehre hizmet etme sorumluluğumla Tekirdağ için çalışmaya devam edeceğim."


(HA)

author: Randi Beers
title: Jimmy Bell – The ghost of Arctic Bay
content:
At Cape Dorset in 1949, Jimmy Bell, the large, fun-loving Hudson’s Bay Co. trader, took ill. His once rotund body began to waste away until he was but a shadow of his former self.


On arriving in Cape Dorset, his young clerk, Peter Murdoch, who had known Jimmy in Lake Harbour, barely recognized him. He described him as “a skinny-looking fellow wearing baggy clothes, his face lined and his eyes a sickly yellow.”  


Officials in Winnipeg knew in February that Jimmy’s health was “not up to its usual robust standard,” but Jimmy attributed it to “too much of his own cooking.”


In May he sent a message to Winnipeg that admitted he required medical attention. Another message followed, in which he said he would go out to Churchill on the supply ship for a check-up. But he kept the extent of his illness from his superiors. He surmised, correctly, that if they knew his true condition, they would evacuate him to the south. 


But Peter Murdoch knew that Jimmy needed attention, much more than he could provide using the post’s medical manual. He thought that Jimmy had stomach cancer. Without Jimmy’s knowledge, Murdoch sent a telegram by radio to Winnipeg informing them of Jimmy’s condition. Too late, Jimmy realized what Murdoch had done and mustered all his strength to roar at Murdoch and express his disapproval. 


Jimmy told Murdoch, “If I have cancer I want to die in the North. I want my spirit to stay in the North. When I die my spirit is going back to Arctic Bay. That’s the place I really love most – Arctic Bay.” 


But Winnipeg had got the message. Headquarters immediately dispatched their Canso aircraft, nicknamed Polar Bear, on the long flight to Cape Dorset.


Jimmy was evacuated to Winnipeg on July 2. He was operated on at Winnipeg General Hospital a few days later, but doctors concluded that there was nothing more they could do for him. His mother and a brother were sent for and reached his bedside on the last day of August. Jimmy Bell died on Sept. 12 and was buried in Brookside Cemetery, in Winnipeg. He was only 43.


The inscription on his pink granite headstone ends with: “Here we leave our loved one sleeping.” 


But Jimmy wasn’t sleeping. He was restless. And, as he had promised, his spirit returned to Arctic Bay — or so it appeared.


Jimmy had a dear friend there. Amarualik was a leader among the Inuit and had worked for the Hudson’s Bay Co. for many years. Jimmy and Amarualik were close, and Jimmy had had a child with Amarualik’s daughter, Kautaq. That girl, Tapisa (now Tapisa Hughes of Arctic Bay) was the youngest of three daughters that Jimmy had with Inuit women.


When he died, the Hudson’s Bay Co. manager’s residence in Arctic Bay became the scene of strange occurrences. Residents and visitors heard footsteps in the storeroom, but there was no one there. Cups rattled in the cupboards and dishes rattled in the sink. But no one present had disturbed them. Doors mysteriously opened. The building was haunted.


Jimmy had returned to Arctic Bay to be near his old friend, Amarualik.


It’s noteworthy that many of Jimmy’s manifestations happened in the kitchen of the residence, because Jimmy, in life, had apparently been obsessed with the neatness of his kitchen. Len Budgell, a lifelong Hudson’s Bay Co. employee, recalled that Jimmy was a bachelor and that “he liked things just so. If you did the dishes at night and hung the tea towel up, and it wasn’t the way Jimmy would have hung it up, in the morning you would find it neatly rearranged to Jimmy’s preference.” 


When the rattling of dishes became too loud, some company managers were known to shout, “Leave the bloody dishes alone, Jimmy.”


That would generally result in a short burst of fierce rattling — Jimmy was clearly displeased — before silence would settle in. 


Soon after Eric Mitchell arrived in Arctic Bay as manager, he experienced a number of “curious, though disturbing incidents.” Footsteps were heard on the creaky floorboards of the attic night after night until one night he shouted, “Quit it!”


One night he awoke to find all the doors of the house wide open. When he told Amarualik about these events, the old Inuk replied nonchalantly, “That’s just Jimmy Bell wandering around. Don’t worry about it; he’s just waiting for me to join him.” 


The disturbances in Arctic Bay were no secret. They became part of Baffin Island lore. Word of the haunted staff house reached Winnipeg where some officials laughed it off.


But one winter in the 1960s …

author: Unknown
title: İşte Meydan İşte Sahne Sergisi ziyarete açıldı
content:
Ankara – 1961 yılında kurulan, kurulduğu dönem Ankara’nın tek tiyatrosu olan Meydan Sahnesi’ni anlatan ve Sibel Durak’ın hazırladığı ‘İşte Meydan İşte Sahne Sergisi’ 22 Kasım’a kadar ziyarete açık olacak.

Açılışta konuşan Ankara Tabib Odası’ndan( diyelim çalışanı yerine) Sibel Durak, “Sergideki bütün materyal arşiv malzemesidir. Sahaf ve müzayedelerden, kendi çabam ve olanaklarım ile topladığım malzemelerden oluşuyor. Yaklaşık 3 yıldır topluyorum. Aynı zamanda sergide, Uğur Kavas’ın verdiği Aceleci Kalp, Köşe Kapmaca ve Karaların Memetleri oyunlarının fotoğrafları yer alıyor” dedi.

Meydan Sahnesi’nin, tiyatronun altın çağında kurulduğunu dile getiren Durak, ”Sahne, 1961 yılında kuruluyor ve başarılı işlere imza atıyor. O dönem biletler satışa çıktığı gibi bitiyor. Meydan Sahnesi, açılan tiyatro kursları ve oyunları sayesinde çok fazla oyuncunun tiyatroya başlamasına olanak sağlamıştır. 80’lere kadar 20’ye yakın yeni tiyatro kurulmuş ve tiyatroların yaygınlaşmasında önemli rolü olmuştur. Ayrıca bu dönem telif ücreti ödeyemedikleri için Adalet Ağaoğlu tiyatro oyunlarının çevirisini yaparak destek vermiştir” şeklinde konuştu.

Serginin kuruluş sürecinde yaşananlara değinen Durak, “Meydan Sahnesi ile ilgili çok fazla kişiye ulaşamadım. Sergiyi hazırladıktan sonra bazı insanlarla görüşme fırsatı buldum. Tiyatro, 1972-73 sezonunda kapanmış ve 50 yıldan fazla bir süre geçmiş. Sergide, çalışmamım devamı için kullanmamı istedikleri materyalleri paylaşan olursa sergide kullanmak isterim” ifadelerini kullandı.

Devlet Tiyatrosu’nun zamanında çok iyi seyirci yetiştirdiğini söyleyen Durak, ”Meydan Sahnesi gibi özel tiyatrolar da bunun üzerine koyarak kültürün devamını sağlamıştır. Ankara seyircisi başkadır denir, çünkü bir kültür yaratılmıştır” dedi.

Meydan Sahnesi’nde oynanan oyunların kendine has tarzı olduğunu dile getiren Durak, “Genelde komedi, polisiye oyunlar oynanmış. Bulabildiğim oyun isimlerini yazdım. Tiyatroyla ilgilenen bir kişi sergiyi gördükten sonra ‘bu oyun da vardı’ diyebilir. Bu da talep doğrultusunda oyunların yeniden sahnelenmesine olanak sağlayabilir. Bu sayede o dönem verilen emek, mücadele ve cesaret insanları harekete geçirebilir. Fakat ne yazık ki bu dönemde tiyatroların durumu iç açıcı değil. Yeterli destek görmüyorlar ve vergiler çok ağır. Bu da tiyatro kültürünü olumsuz etkiliyor” açıklamalarında bulundu. Açıklamalarında bulundu demeyelim dedi veya şeklinde konuştu diyelim

Ayrıca arşivlerin önemine vurgu yapan Durak, “1-2 istisna kitap dışında tiyatro tarihi ile ilgili tarih kitaplarında bile çok fazla bilgi yok. Yoklukların içinde önemli emekler verildiğini hatırlatmak istedim, amacım buydu. Aynı zamanda elinde arşivi olanlara da, ellerindeki arşivi nasıl kullanabilecekleri konusunda fikir vermeyi amaçladım. Rahmi M. Koç Müzesi’nin de sergi salonunu tahsis ettiği bir iş birliği oldu” dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.
