title: Martyrs of Kurdistan’s Freedom Struggle commemorated in Sine
content:
Following the HPG’s announcement of the identities of nine guerrillas from Rojhilatê Kurdistan who fell as martyrs in the freedom struggle in previous years, a memorial event was held in the city of Sanandaj (Sine).


During the commemoration, the Martyrs’ Families Committee and Peace Mothers carried photographs of the fallen guerrillas and repeatedly chanted the slogan “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs never die).


 


At the event, organised by the Martyrs’ Families Committee and the Peace Mothers, it was stated that the martyrs had become symbols of unity among all parts of Kurdistan.


It was also emphasised that the martyrs of the freedom struggle, from Kobanê, Shengal, Amed, Qamishlo and Hewraman to Sine, had set an example of defending humanity against ISIS.


At the end of the ceremony, the Martyrs’ Families Committee of Rojhilatê Kurdistan extended its condolences to the people of Sine and the patriotic people of Kurdistan. The committee also reiterated that the martyrs of Rojhilatê Kurdistan are martyrs of the entire Kurdish people.

author: Unknown
title: Laura Quagliuolo: Öcalan's freedom is key to lasting peace
content:
The Call for Peace and a Democratic Society issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025 brought discussions on a democratic solution to the Kurdish question into a new phase. International calls for Öcalan's freedom and the implementation of the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) ruling on the "right to hope" also continue. Demands for Turkey to fulfill its obligations under the supervision of the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers are increasingly coming to the fore.


Italian feminist activist, writer and member of the Rete Jin women's solidarity network Laura Quagliuolo spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the importance of Öcalan's freedom for a democratic solution, the failure to implement ECtHR rulings and the role of women in building peace.


Efforts to find a democratic solution to the Kurdish question have continued since the call issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025. How do you assess the process at its current stage? What do you think are the fundamental conditions that must be met to achieve lasting peace?


I think the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey has not yet been realized. We have not reached that point yet, primarily because Abdullah Öcalan is not free. I believe Öcalan's freedom is a very important condition for the Kurdish people to achieve freedom and for their existence to be recognized. The Kurdish people can no longer be ignored. As you know, Abdullah Öcalan's call was extremely clear and powerful. The guerrillas came down from the mountains and laid down their weapons. Their weapons were burned in a ceremony. This was an enormously significant step toward peace.


However, the Kurdish people must also be recognized. Their language, traditions, culture and way of life must be recognized. They can no longer be subjected to oppression, as the Turkish state has done in the past and continues to do today. Therefore, the most important issue, first and foremost, is the freedom of Abdullah Öcalan and the many other comrades who remain imprisoned under various circumstances.


Abdullah Öcalan's situation is particularly serious and troubling. Because after nearly 28 years of imprisonment, they must acknowledge that he has always been someone who has taken steps toward peace in the Middle East. Another condition is recognizing that the Kurdish people, and not only the Kurds but other peoples as well, are working and living according to the principles that emerge from Abdullah Öcalan's paradigm. This must be recognized because it represents hope not only for Turkey but for the entire Middle East and, if I may say so, for the whole world.


As you mentioned, despite the ongoing process, there has been no fundamental change in the legal status or prison conditions of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan. This remains one of the Kurdish side's most fundamental demands. Do you believe lasting peace can genuinely be built without securing the conditions necessary for Öcalan's freedom and participation in the process?


As I said before, Öcalan's freedom must be guaranteed. He must have the freedom to speak to the people, to his own people. It is not only a matter of allowing him to participate in meetings. Conditions must also be established in which he can express his views and be heard by everyone. Because, in my opinion, he is a man of peace. He is also someone who can help guide this peace process in the right direction. But they cannot continue to keep him imprisoned like this. They need to take steps, and serious ones at that.


The ECtHR ruled against Turkey in 2014 over the aggravated life sentence imposed on Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan without the possibility of release. However, more than 12 years later, the ruling has still not been fully implemented. How should this position be interpreted? What concrete steps do you expect from the Council of Europe's Committee of Ministers at its meeting in December?


You know, Europe constantly talks about peace and many other things. But in reality, Europe is not genuinely committed to achieving peace, whether in the Middle East, in the war between Russia and Ukraine, or anywhere else. They talk, but they have done nothing in the face of the genocide in Palestine. That is the situation in Europe. They speak and then fall silent. What remains after their speeches is silence. That is exactly what happened 12 years ago. You know, the court, all those rulings and everything else …

author: Unknown
title: KJK: The time for self-defence is now!
content:
The Coordination of the Kurdistan Women’s Community (KJK) issued a written statement ahead of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Emphasising the importance of strengthening women's organisation and unity against male-dominated violence, the KJK stated that the Peace and Democratic Society Process would create new opportunities for women's free participation and their struggle for freedom.


The statement said: "Violence against women has never before been carried out with such depth and systematic intensity. Male-dominated violence, which has reached horrific levels and permeates every month, every day and every moment of the year, has made it imperative to say ‘enough is enough’. In this regard, effective results can only be achieved if we, as women, unite in organised struggle against femicide, the destruction of life, society and nature perpetrated by capitalist modernity — the representative of our era's murderous system of domination — and its derivatives, which inject these forms of destruction into every cell of life.


Against a culture of violence embedded in every aspect of social life, we, as women, need plans and projects that establish a multidimensional perspective of struggle, ranging from transforming the organisation of everyday life and relationships to building alternative structures for a free life. At a time when violence has become a culture and a way of life, the process of democratic integration initiated by Rêber Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] brings all peoples and oppressed groups together within a framework of interconnectedness, while opening up new horizons of struggle for all the oppressed, particularly women."


The statement added: "With the development of the Peace and Democracy Process, our women's liberation perspective and the seeds of an alternative life will grow much stronger. One of the fundamental objectives of the Peace and Democratic Society Process is to pave the way for women's democratic and free participation. Through this process, the ground will also be created for a more comprehensive and profound struggle against violence targeting women, as well as all attitudes that marginalise and objectify women in every sphere of life. The Democracy and Peace Process will therefore also be a process through which women's freedom, their understanding of liberation and their fundamental human rights can be advanced in every sphere of life.


This year, we approach the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November with a new, comprehensive and profound perspective. We respond by strengthening women's unity in Kurdistan, the Middle East and across the world, and by advancing their collective struggle. Let us transform 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, into an even stronger expression of women's solidarity, unity and struggle than in previous years."


The statement continued: "The reality of 25 November places upon women's movements, above all, the duty and responsibility to organise through women's own collective wisdom and to democratise society under women's leadership. For this reason, everyone — particularly women comrades — must strengthen and expand their organisation with every step they take, successfully carrying this march towards freedom into cities, villages, streets, neighbourhoods, factories, schools, homes and the lives of individuals. The male-dominated system, which is the gravedigger of society and women, operates strategically and politically at global, regional and local levels. If it implements its agenda multidimensionally at every moment of life, then we, as women's movements, must also wage a multidimensional struggle everywhere and at all times, based on a strategy and politics of women's liberation.


We can develop our existence by expanding our world of meaning through struggle, organisation and the power of self-defence. On this basis, we can change and transform society and men, and create a world in which it is possible to breathe freely. In this way, the tradition of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, whose roots go back to the Mirabal sisters and extend to Sakine Cansız, will open the doors to a world free from violence.


Let us strengthen our organised, collective women's struggle under the slogan 'through women's organization against violence, the time for self-defence is now!' to …

author: Unknown
title: KNK warns of division in South Kurdistan and calls on KDP and PUK to engage in dialogue
content:
The Kurdistan National Congress (KNK) has warned of further divisions among Kurdish institutions amid the escalating government crisis in South Kurdistan. Following the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan’s (PUK) announcement that it would withdraw from the regional government and its threat to establish parallel administrative structures in Sulaymaniyah, the KNK called on the two dominant parties in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), the KDP and PUK, to resume negotiations without delay. It stressed that political power struggles must no longer be conducted at the expense of the population and the region’s constitutionally guaranteed autonomy.


The latest escalation was triggered by Wednesday’s election of a new parliamentary leadership in Hewlêr (Erbil). After nearly two years of political deadlock, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), together with smaller parties and minority representatives, pushed ahead with the parliamentary session. The PUK and several opposition parties boycotted the vote because no agreement had been reached on the future distribution of power. With 52 of the 100 members of parliament participating, the session barely secured the required majority. KDP politician Vala Fareed was elected speaker of parliament.


PUK leader Bafel Talabanî subsequently declared that his party would recognize neither the parliamentary session nor any government formed as a result of it. He announced the party’s withdrawal from the existing regional government and threatened to establish separate government and administrative offices in Sulaymaniyah if the KDP continued on its current course. As a result, the dispute now concerns not only the formation of a government, which has been deadlocked since the October 2024 elections, but also the unity of South Kurdistan’s political institutions.


KNK offers to mediate between the parties


In its statement, the KNK described the developments as a serious threat to regional stability. It warned that the ongoing disputes were already disrupting public life and jeopardizing the political achievements of the Kurdish population.


The organization recalled that it had repeatedly held talks with the parties involved since the parliamentary elections in October 2024 and urged them to form a government without delay. The KNK said it had also expressed its willingness to mediate between the KDP and PUK. According to the organization, the latest escalation made reaching a political agreement all the more urgent.


“The leaderships of the KDP and PUK, together with all political forces, must engage in comprehensive dialogue as soon as possible and with the necessary sense of responsibility to reach a national and patriotic understanding,” the statement said.


The KNK called on the parties to subordinate their interests in political power to a shared political responsibility. The priorities, it stressed, must be ensuring a functioning government, strengthening institutions, upholding the rule of law, and addressing the needs of the population. Civil society organizations and other social groups should also participate in efforts to find a solution, it added.


National unity as a prerequisite for stability


Through its offer of mediation, the KNK aims to prevent political divisions between Hewlêr and Sulaymaniyah from becoming further entrenched. The congress warned that the autonomous rights of the Kurdistan Region would be particularly at risk if the rival parties extended their dispute into state institutions.


Preserving these achievements, it emphasized, must take precedence over party-political interests. The KNK therefore reaffirmed its willingness to exhaust all possibilities for bringing the KDP and PUK closer together.


“The path to national unity is the only way to overcome the existing differences and ensure peace and stability for our people,” the statement concluded.

author: Unknown
title: Erdoğan'dan Aliyev'e ‘kardeşim’ mektubu: Ankara-Bakü geriliminin gölgesinde kutlama
content:
AKP’li Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Azerbaycan’ın 8 Kasım Zafer Günü’nün altıncı yıl dönümü dolayısıyla Azerbaycan Cumhurbaşkanı İlham Aliyev’e mektup gönderdi. Azerbaycan Cumhurbaşkanlığı’nın internet sitesinde 7 Kasım’da yayımlanan mektubun “Sayın Cumhurbaşkanı, aziz kardeşim” sözleriyle başlaması dikkat çekti.

Türkiye ile Azerbaycan arasındaki ilişkilere de değinen Erdoğan, Şuşa Beyannamesi ile en üst seviyeye taşınan “Bir millet, iki devlet” anlayışını vurguladı.

Erdoğan, iki ülkenin hem ikili ilişkilerde hem de uluslararası alanda yakın iş birliği ve dayanışma içinde çalışmayı sürdüreceğine inandığını belirtti.

Erdoğan’ın mektubu, Azerbaycan’da yaşanan başörtüsü tartışmasının ardından Ankara ile Bakü arasında ortaya çıkan gerilimin gölgesinde geldi.

Tartışmanın ardından başta eski Cumhurbaşkanı Danışmanı Oktay Saral olmak üzere AKP’li isimler Azerbaycan yönetimine yönelik sert açıklamalarda bulunmuştu. Azerbaycan yönetimi bazı isimlere ülkeye giriş yasağı getirirken, Saral tepkilerin ardından görevinden alınmıştı.

Gerilimin sürdüğü dönemde Azerbaycan Cumhurbaşkanı Aliyev, Ankara’da düzenlenen Türk Devletleri Teşkilatı Zirvesi’ne katılmamıştı. Aliyev’e yakınlığıyla bilinen APA haber ajansında yayımlanan bir yazıda da AKP iktidarına yönelik ağır suçlamalara yer verilmişti.

Erdoğan, daha önce Güney Kore dönüşünde gazetecilere yaptığı açıklamada 8 Kasım’da Azerbaycan’ı ziyaret etmeyi planladığını söylemişti.

Aliyev’e gönderilen mektup, iki ülke arasındaki ilişkilerde yaşanan gerilimin ardından Ankara’nın yakın iş birliği ve dayanışma mesajını yeniden öne çıkardığı bir adım olarak değerlendirildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Barış Akademisyenlerinin 215 dosyası Danıştay’da bekliyor
content:
Barış Akademisyenleri, 2016–2018 yılları arasında olağanüstü hal (OHAL) döneminde çıkarılan kanun hükmünde kararnamelerle (KHK) kamu görevinden ihraç edilen akademisyenlerin açtığı davalardaki güncel durumu paylaştı.


İhraçların üzerinden 10 yıl geçerken, akademisyenlerin açtığı davaların önemli bir bölümü halen bölge idare mahkemeleri, Danıştay, Danıştay İdari Dava Daireleri Kurulu (İDDK) ve Anayasa Mahkemesi (AYM) aşamalarında bulunuyor.


10 OHAL KHK’siyle 406 Barış Akademisyeni kamu görevinden ihraç edilmişti.


OHAL Komisyonu 385 başvuruyu reddetti


İhraçların ardından başvuruların ilk adresi, 2017’de kurulan OHAL İşlemleri İnceleme Komisyonu oldu.


Komisyon, Barış Akademisyenlerinin 385 başvurusunu reddetti. Komisyon ret kararlarını 2021’in sonunda açıkladı ve ancak bu tarihten sonra idare mahkemelerine başvuru yapılabildi.


Barış Akademisyenleri bu nedenle yargıya erişimin yaklaşık beş yıl boyunca engellendiğini belirtti.


İdare mahkemelerinde 190 ret, 173 kabul kararı


Komisyon kararlarının ardından idare mahkemelerinde toplam 384 dava açıldı.


Bunlardan 190’ında akademisyenlerin başvurusu reddedilirken, 173 davada kabul kararı verildi. Paylaşılan verilere göre 21 davaya ilişkin bilgi ise eksik.


İlk derece mahkemelerinin kararları daha sonra bölge idare mahkemelerine (BİM) taşındı.


BİM aşamasında 155 dosyada istinaf başvuruları davacı lehine kabul edildi ya da karar davacı lehine kaldırıldı. 130 dosyada ise süreç davacı aleyhine sonuçlandı.


78 dava hakkında henüz karar verilmedi.


23 akademisyenin göreve iadesi kesinleşti


Davaların Danıştay 5. Dairesi’ndeki aşamasında ise şimdiye kadar 23 dosyada akademisyenler lehine verilen kararlar onandı. Böylece bu davalarda göreve iadeler kesinleşti.


Beş davada akademisyenler aleyhine verilen kararlar onandı. Bu dosyalarda bir sonraki hukuki aşama Anayasa Mahkemesi’ne bireysel başvuru.


Danıştay ayrıca bir davada akademisyen aleyhine bozma kararı verdi. Bölge idare mahkemesinin kararından farklı olan dosya yeniden BİM’de görüşülüyor.


41 davada ise Danıştay akademisyenler lehine bozma kararı verdi. Bu dosyalar da bölge idare mahkemelerine geri gönderildi.


Bu 41 dosyanın dokuzunda BİM önceki, davacı aleyhine kararında ısrar etti. Bu davaların bir sonraki aşaması Danıştay İdari Dava Daireleri Kurulu olacak.


215 dosyada henüz karar yok


Danıştay 5. Dairesi önündeki 215 davada ise 6 Kasım itibarıyla henüz karar verilmedi.


Dokuz dava Danıştay İdari Dava Daireleri Kurulu aşamasında bulunurken, akademisyenler aleyhine kesinleşen kararlarla ilgili beş başvuru da Anayasa Mahkemesi aşamasında.


(HA)

title: Süper Lig'in 11. hafta maçı: Kocaelispor deplasmanda Eyüpspor'u 2-0 yendi
content:
Kocaelispor, deplasmanda Eyüpspor'u 2-0 yendi.

5. dakikada Kocaelispor öne geçti. Sissoho'nun ceza yayının sol çaprazından şutunda, kaleci Moldovan meşin yuvarlağı çeldi. Dönen topu altıpas çizgisinin gerisinde önünde bulan Agyei'nin vuruşunda, meşin yuvarlak ağlarla buluştu: 0-1.

12. dakikada Baku'nun pasında ceza yayının gerisinde topla buluşan Uğur Kaan Yıldız'ın vuruşunda meşin yuvarlak, Eyüpspor savunmasına çarpıp kaleye yöneldi. Kaleci Moldovan, meşin yuvarlağı önledi.

22. dakikada Massanga'nın pasında topla buluşan Boutobba, Kocaelisporlu Berkan Kutlu'dan sıyrıldıktan sonra ceza sahasının sağ çaprazından şutunu çekti. Kaleci Serhat Öztaşdelen, meşin yuvarlağı önledi.

28. dakikada Kocaelispor farkı 2'ye çıkardı. Tayfur Bingöl'ün uzun pasında sol kanatta topla buluşan Baku, ceza sahasının sol tarafındaki Rivas'a meşin yuvarlağı aktardı. Bu oyuncunun pasında ceza yayında topla buluşan Berkan Kutlu'nun bekletmeden vuruşunda, meşin yuvarlak kalecinin solundan ağlarla buluştu: 0-2.

Kocaelispor, karşılaşmanın ilk yarısını 2-0 üstün tamamladı.

55. dakikada Uğur Kaan Yıldız'ın sağ kanattan kullandığı serbest vuruşta ceza yayının içerisinde topla buluşan Sissoho'nun bekletmeden şutunda, meşin yuvarlak az farkla üstten auta gitti.

67. dakikada Raux Yao'nun pasında savunmanın arkasına sarkan Abdullahi, kaleci Serhat'tan sıyrıldıktan sonra ceza sahasının sağ çaprazından vuruşunu yaptı. Kocaelisporlu Emir Ortakaya, kaleci Serhat'ın müdahalesine rağmen kaleye yönelen topa müdahale ederek golü önledi.

90+1. dakikada paslaşılarak kullanılan kornerde sağ kanatta topla buluşan Sadia, arka direğe doğru ortasını açtı. Bu noktada bulunan Yusuf Barası'nın kafa vuruşunda, meşin yuvarlak üstten auta çıktı.

Kocaelispor, müsabakadan 2-0'lık galibiyetle ayrıldı.

content:
Fotoğraf: Tima Miroshnichenko/Pexels

Düzce'nin Gümüşova ilçesinde 16 yaşındaki Ahmet K., çıkan tartışmada av tüfeğiyle vurularak hayatını kaybetti.

Olay, Gümüşova ilçesine bağlı Yongalık köyünde meydana geldi. Edinilen bilgiye göre, Ahmet K. (16) ile A.İ.U. (17) arasında henüz belirlenemeyen bir nedenle tartışma çıktı.

Tartışmanın köy dışındaki orman yolunda kavgaya dönüşmesi üzerine A.İ.U., yanında bulunan av tüfeğiyle Ahmet K.'ye ateş ederek olay yerinden kaçtı.

İhbar üzerine bölgeye sevk edilen polis ekipleri, Ahmet K.'yi yerde hareketsiz halde buldu. Olay yerine gelen sağlık ekipleri, çocuğun yaşamını yitirdiğini belirledi.

Ahmet K.'nin cenazesi, otopsi işlemleri için Düzce Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi Eğitim Araştırma ve Uygulama Hastanesi morguna kaldırıldı.

Olayın ardından kaçan 17 yaşındaki A.İ.U. ise polis ekipleri tarafından gözaltına alındı.

title: She Is Risen: The Return of Jamia’s Student Union
content:
On the 106th anniversary of her foundation, Jamia’s student union came back to life.

By midnight, the chains around the iron bars of gate no. 7, the freshly cemented walls sealing the entrances in front of Ibn Sina and the Central Canteen, and the near 500 personnel of the central armed forces that had been occupying the road dividing the university campus for three weeks, the barricades announcing emergency ‘security measures’ under BNSS section 163, were dissolved. The JMISU is risen. The dirt on her grave has washed clean.


 


Mouli Sharma


 


Mahawat

 falls cold and brutal in Delhi’s October, announcing the coming winter and daring you to test her like only nature can.


 


In South East Delhi, rain is sickness, mosquitoes, and waterlogging; the roads in and around Jamia Nagar (Haji Colony, Gaffar Manzil, Batla House, Okhla Vihar, Sarai Jullena, etc.) are ill-tempered and poorly maintained—everything floods (except the posh New Friends Colony, home to a covert ‘counter-intelligence unit’ of the Delhi Police’s ‘Special Cell’).


 


Sometimes, of course, rain is rebirth. Autumn washing away the sins of the season past.


 


Since 12 October 2026, Jamia Millia Islamia’s banned Student Union had been clawing its way out from six feet under. Between an indefinite hunger strike, a multi-departmental occupation, a campus lockdown and five arrests, the University’s ‘sanghi’ administration and collective student body had been in the midst of a political showdown. Unbeknownst to both, judgment day was going to come as the protests (described as the biggest in Jamia since Shaheen Bagh) entered their 18th day, on the 106th anniversary of the University’s own radical birth.


On the 106th anniversary of her foundation, Jamia’s student union came back to life.


In the early 1900s, policies of the British Raj that prompted a mass exit of students and faculty from the Aligarh Muslim University—primarily due to pro-establishment policies aimed at preventing, discouraging, and penalising participation in the Freedom Movement, i.e. suppressing academic dissent—paved the way for collective desire for a “National Muslim University” free from authoritarian intervention.


 


“Many students of Aligarh too were disappointed with the administration’s pro-British policies which prevented teachers and students from taking part in the freedom movement,” says a memorial piece on Shaikhul-Hind Mahmood Hasan, one of Jamia’s most prominent founders, in the Milli Gazette from a decade ago, halfway between the perceived bookends of this story. “In 1920, some students suddenly left the Aligarh Muslim University. A free and private “National Muslim University” was planned to accommodate these students. Despite his bad health and frail body, Maulana Mahmood travelled to Aligarh and laid the foundation-stone of this institution on 29 October 1920. It later came to be known as Jamia Millia Islamia.”


 


As the piece goes on, Mahmood is remembered as being advised against going to Aligarh, to lay Jamia’s founding stone, on 29 October 1926. His response is one of the more telling anecdotes about this foundation:


 


“If this pains the British, I will do it.”


 


***


Sab Kuch Yaad Rakha Jayega?


 


Eight decades later, a different regime did to Jamia what the British had done to AMU in their time. Contrary to the understanding of ‘2006’ as the definitive year of the JMISU’s two decade stint under the ground, the body’s existence had been tenuous for long before that, having been banned once prior in 1996, after merely 15 years of existence since the first union elections in 1981. The 2006 ban followed what was merely eight months of resurfacing, with a union having been constituted for the first time in a decade in July 2005, only to be banned under the Manmohan Singh-led UPA government the following year, by the university administration itself, ostensibly due to concerns over ‘campus violence’, and an alleged attack on then Vice Chancellor, Late Prof. Mushirul Hasan.


 


The purpose of the ban, both in motivation and impact, is debated till date.


 


“Mushirul is the last VC Jamia had that did anything in the university’s interest,” a professor who would rather not be named tells me over tea and nostalgia in another university campus—JNU, where he feels freer to talk. “You see the road that passes through the campus today?” he asks with disgust. It is this, Okhla Road, splicing through the belly of Jamia’s largest continuous …

title: Anatoly Dubovik - Fire and Passion
content:
Author

: Anatoly Dubovik

Title

: Fire and Passion

Subtitle

: The Life of Ukrainian Anarchist Maria Nikiforova

Date

: 17 September 2024

Notes

: Originally

published in Russian on Akrateia

 in a slightly different version. Translated by Malcolm Archibald.

Source

: Retrieved on 7

th

 November 2026 from

freedompress.org.uk


 Maria Nikiforova is perhaps the most famous female anarchist who operated on the territory of the former Russian Empire and Ukraine. This is probably why many legends and outright fictions arose around the personality of this legendary anarchist, some of which we will try to dispel in this article.


 Maria Hryhorivna Nikiforova was born in 1888 (possibly 1885). Her precise place of birth is unknown. According to some sources, it was the town of Pechenikovo, Starodubskyi district, Chernihiv province; according to others, she was born in the village of Levshikovo, Oleksandrivskyi district, Katerynoslav province.


 There exists a romantic version of her origins that Nikiforova came from the nobility and that at the age of 16, she fell in love with an officer, ran away from home, was abandoned by her lover and was forced to earn a living on her own—as a nanny, a street vendor, and a bottle washer at a vodka factory. In reality, Nikiforova was the daughter of a peasant, and the only education she received, in her own words, was in the home. There is simply no other reliable information about her early youth.


 In the early 1900s, while working as a seamstress, Nikiforova joined the

Socialist Revolutionary Party (SRs)

, then switched to the anarch0- communists. This happened either in Oleksandrivsk city (now Zaporizhzhia) or Katerynoslav (now Dnipro). She was an agitator, then joined a fighting squad and participated in terrorist attacks against the local bourgeoisie and the police. By 1907, Nikiforova lived in Starodub, where she was one of the leaders of a revolutionary group that included young anarchists, SRs and

SR Maximalists

. They conducted propaganda among the city’s workers and the neighbouring settlement of Klintsy, as well as engaged in armed actions.


 In Starodub, Nikiforova was arrested for the first time in 1907 while trying to commit suicide—fortunately, unsuccessfully. Accusations of terror carried the threat of the death penalty, so Maria insisted to the investigators and the medical commission that she was born in 1889. This made her a minor and allowed her to hope for a lighter sentence. And so, it happened. On October 13, 1907, the Provisional Military Court in Chernihiv found Nikiforova guilty of belonging to the anarcho-communists, participating in the murder of a Starodub police officer, and robbing a priest. She was sentenced to hanging, but when the sentence was confirmed, the execution was commuted to 20 years of hard labour due to her falsified age.


 A year after the trial, Nikiforova was transferred to Moscow. The accompanying documents noted: “Prone to escape. In the common cell, she is a leader and agitator. It’s a good idea to keep her in solitary. Requires especially vigilant supervision as an important criminal.”


 Upon her arrival in Moscow in May 1909, Nikiforova was imprisoned in the Moscow Provincial Women’s Hard Labour Prison. She shared a cell with two other political radicals: Natalya Klimova, an SR Maximalist serving an indefinite term organizing an assassination attempt on Peter Stolypin, the Russian Minister of the Interior; and Ekaterina Nikitina, another Maximalist.


 Twenty years later, Nikitina claimed in her memoirs, among other things, that Nikiforova’s “real name” was not Maria but Vladimir and that she was neither a woman nor a man but a hermaphrodite. Nikitina’s salacious story about Nikiforova’s ambiguous gender has gained popularity since the 1990s and is still being retold despite any evidence. Nikiforova’s personal file from the Moscow Women’s Prison archives states: “Distinctive features: none”; “Marital status: unmarried.” The only detail given about the state of her health is anemia. Noticeably, the doctors of the prison department did not notice any “spicy” special features.


 Nikiforova spent less than two months in Moscow prison. By the time she arrived, an outside group composed of various revolutionary organizations was preparing an assault on the prison. This motley crew of jailbreakers included the young

Vladimir Mayakovsky

, soon to gain fame as the most important Russian futurist poet. The main goal of …

title: Dismissed by decree and imprisoned, Engin Cengiz returns to music at MKM
content:
More than 125,000 public employees were dismissed from their positions through emergency decrees issued under the state of emergency declared after the attempted coup on 15 July 2016. While the government defended these measures as actions targeting those involved in the coup attempt, the process also paved the way for the dismissal of public employees opposed to the government.


Ten years have passed since the emergency decrees were issued. Many of those dismissed were imprisoned, some were forced into exile, while others remained unemployed for long periods. Some were forced to work in construction to make a living, and some lost their lives in workplace accidents.


Engin Cengiz, who now works as a music teacher at the Mesopotamia Cultural Center (MKM), was among those affected during this period, when 125,678 public employees were dismissed according to official figures.


Cengiz was dismissed from his position as a music teacher by an emergency decree in 2016 and was subsequently imprisoned for a period. He spoke to ANF about his experiences during the emergency decree period, the difficulties he faced after his dismissal and how he became involved with the Mesopotamia Cultural Center.


 


‘The turning point came after a two-day strike during the Kobane protests’


Cengiz described the circumstances surrounding his dismissal under an emergency decree, explaining that he had been a music teacher for 15 years. 


Cengiz said: “By that time, I had approximately 15 years of teaching experience. I was a music teacher and had worked in Malatya for a long time. Before that, I was active in trade union organizing and the labor movement. Although the labor movement has a class dimension, we also took a stand on social issues in Turkey, the Middle East and around the world, on the problems faced by oppressed people and on our own existence as a community.


There was a civil war and a massive offensive in Rojava, Syria.


That was actually where the rupture occurred. There was a two-day strike in December over the events in Kobanê. Because we participated, many of us became direct targets. From the state's perspective, however, I was already a prominent figure in the area where I worked because of my activities. Subsequently, after the attempted coup, I was dismissed from my position through an emergency decree.”


Dismissed on the anniversary of the founding of the republic


Cengiz said that he was dismissed on the anniversary of the founding of the republic, stressing that losing his job on 29 October, at a time when they were demanding a democratic republic, held particular significance for him. 


Cengiz said: “The day I was dismissed was perhaps the day when all the coincidences and disasters I could experience in a lifetime came together. The fact that it was 29 October was significant in itself. Because experiencing something like this on the anniversary of the proclamation of the republic, while demanding a democratic republic, gave the whole situation an entirely different meaning.


My brother had been living in exile in Southern Kurdistan for nearly 10 years because of his sentence. He had met someone there, and they were planning to get married. The other family was from Hakkari (Colemêrg), and they came to visit us. We are originally from Oltu in Erzurum. The wedding took place, but neither the bride nor the groom was there. We finished the wedding ceremony with a sense of sadness, and just as everyone was about to return home, a message arrived informing me that I had been dismissed. It was actually something I had expected.


Interestingly, one of my former students from middle school was also at the wedding that day, and we were both dismissed on the same day. We experienced the tragicomic side of the process. I had prepared myself in my own way. Given everything that was happening in Turkey and the Middle East, it would not have been very ethical to question what had happened to me. I did not feel any particular sadness. I simply thought that we were experiencing another repetition of something terrible and that we would have to rebuild our lives from that point onward.”


Detained in Malatya and imprisoned for 10 months


Cengiz, who was arrested shortly after his dismissal under an emergency decree, said, “After I was dismissed on 29 October, I spent a few months exploring different possibilities. I even came to Istanbul for a few weeks. I wanted to travel a little, shake off the mindset of being a …

author: Unknown
title: Halide Türkoğlu: Concrete steps are essential for the process
content:
Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) Women's Council Spokesperson Halide Türkoğlu held a press conference at the party's headquarters ahead of the Women's Council meeting.


Türkoğlu began her speech by commemorating former Women's Council member Nesrin Aslan with respect and longing. She said that the women's conference would produce a powerful document for the success of the process. She stated: "Every gathering, action and event organized by women around the demand for a dignified peace as part of the Peace and Democratic Society Process has strengthened this spirit. Women have demonstrated with strong determination that they are present in resistance, in struggle and at the negotiating table, and that no process can be shaped without women."


Türkoğlu once again welcomed the "Women Stand Together, Discussing the Future" conference, held in Ankara on 31 October and 1 November, saying that it had been organized "in this spirit." She added: "We wholeheartedly believe that the outcomes of this conference will constitute a powerful document for the success of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Women already have their roadmap for peace and are ready to build their present and future."


Support for the Peace Mothers' demands


Türkoğlu also expressed support for the demands of the Peace Mothers, saying: "If peace requires courage, it is the Peace Mothers who have demonstrated this courage most clearly for years. Despite harsh winter conditions and all kinds of health problems, they raised their demands from the vigil they held in tents in the heart of Ankara, calling for the success of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, for other mothers to be spared the same suffering and for genuine peace."


'The way must be opened for Mr. Öcalan'


Türkoğlu continued: "They once again raised their voices in the strongest possible terms, demanding that Mr. Öcalan be allowed to continue his work under free and equal conditions and that political prisoners be released. On behalf of our DEM Party Women's Council, I once again salute the determination demonstrated by the Peace Mothers. Their demands are our demands."


Concrete steps must be taken


Halide Türkoğlu called for an end to further delays in establishing the conditions necessary for meetings with Abdullah Öcalan. She said: "The conditions of Mr. Öcalan, the chief negotiator of the process, must not be addressed solely in terms of relocation. The establishment of conditions that would allow journalists, academics, human rights organizations, women and all sections of society to meet with Mr. Öcalan must not be delayed any longer. Regulations must be introduced to complement the legislation referred to as the Framework Law. The Peace and Political Participation Council and all other councils must begin their work. The proposals for democratization contained in parliament's joint report must be enacted into law. These concrete steps are essential for the process to succeed. One of the most important areas requiring concrete action is the prisons. Enemy law must not be applied in prisons while peace is being discussed outside. Political prisoners and ill prisoners must be released."


Impunity is killing women


Türkoğlu also drew attention to violence against women, stating that at least 20 women had been killed in October alone. Türkoğlu said, "Policies of impunity protect men by covering up crimes committed against children. We will continue to pursue accountability for these crimes of sexual abuse against children." She added: "It is not only men who kill women. It is the policies of impunity that embolden these men. It is the protective measures that remain on paper, the restraining orders that are violated and the protection orders that are never implemented."


Türkoğlu then addressed the inheritance controversy surrounding Jülide Kural, saying that it could not be separated from patriarchal thinking. She said: "On behalf of our Women's Council, I express my solidarity with her and declare that Jülide Kural is not alone."


Everyone who enabled and financed the fund must face trial


Türkoğlu demanded that everyone who financed and facilitated the fund be brought to justice. She said: "The fact that such large-scale fraud can be carried out so easily demonstrates how this country is governed through criminal networks. Everyone who has supported and enabled this fund-related criminal network must face trial. We will not give up our struggle …

title: KCDP: 20 women murdered in October
content:
The We Will Stop Femicide Platform (KCDP) has published its October 2026 report on femicides, stating that at least 20 women were murdered, and 39 others lost their lives under suspicious circumstances.


Of the 20 women murdered, five were killed by their husbands, four by their current partners, one by someone they knew, one by their father, four by their former husbands and two by their former partners. The relationship between the perpetrators and the remaining three women could not be established. The report noted that 25 percent of the women were murdered by their husbands.


Nine women were murdered in their homes, three in the street, two in cars, two at their workplaces and one in a recreational area. The location of the murders of three women could not be determined. According to the report, 45 percent of the women murdered in October were killed in their homes.

title: Tuğba Hezer: Women must have a direct say in negotiations
content:
Kurdish politician Tuğba Hezer spoke about the social dimension of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the role of women in the process and the struggle for women's rights. Hezer drew attention to the exclusion of women from decision-making mechanisms in previous peace processes and Kurdish women's struggle for their identity and language. She said that women must have a direct say and decision-making power in negotiations.


Hezer highlighted the devastation caused by war and social inequalities in women's lives, the denial of women's identity and their exclusion from peace processes.


Hezer said: "Women bear the heaviest consequences of war, conflict and social inequalities. Yet throughout history, decisions in peace processes have largely been made without women. The denial of women's identity in Turkey, particularly Kurdish women's struggle to exist with their own mother tongue, identity and as women, cannot be separated from the devastation caused by war. Women experience the destruction of war while also facing patriarchal state violence. We struggle against these inequalities in every sphere, from politics and education to public and social life.


A different approach is needed in this process. We cannot accept women being treated merely as people whose demands are heard and on whose behalf decisions are made. If we are going to call it a negotiating table, then a table without women means that half of society is absent. Women must not simply have others speak or make decisions on their behalf. They must participate directly as active subjects.


Peace is not merely the silencing of weapons or the end of conflicts. Questions of identity, women's ability to live freely, equal citizenship, mother tongue, education, labor and public life are also part of peace. We cannot speak of genuine peace where women's right to life is not guaranteed, their identities are not recognized and they cannot live freely. Women's freedom must not be treated as an issue to be addressed after peace has been achieved. It must be one of the fundamental objectives of the process from the outset.


Turkey faces serious obstacles that must be overcome in democracy, rights and freedoms, the rule of law, freedom of expression and justice. We have a long struggle ahead of us, from guaranteeing mother tongue rights and equal citizenship to women's freedom and social freedoms. We must pursue this struggle together with all democratic sections of society, particularly women. A democratic solution to the Kurdish question, women's freedom and Turkey's democratization are inseparable."


'

The past two years have been marked by waiting'


Tuğba Hezer pointed to the differences between the state's approach and the expectations of women, Kurds and democratic circles over the two years of the process. She said that the perspective of a democratic society had not been sufficiently established throughout society.


Hezer assessed the work carried out during this period and the shortcomings that had emerged: "When we look at what we have done over the past two years, I see that we have experienced something of a period of waiting. This does not mean that nothing has been done. There have been tremendous efforts and valuable contributions. Very important conferences, meetings and gatherings have taken place. However, two years is a long time to build something, move it forward and reach broader sections of society.


Looking at the approach of the state and the government, we see that they view the process primarily in terms of disarmament and dissolution. The expectations of Kurds, women, leftist, socialist and democratic circles, however, concern a democratic solution to the Kurdish question, democratization and the construction of a democratic society. It is clear that the state and the government have demonstrated no political will for democratic transformation and have taken no concrete steps in that direction. No steps are being taken even to ensure that peace takes root in society. Problems concerning democracy, fundamental rights and freedoms, justice and freedom of expression continue in Turkey.


There are many steps that could be taken without waiting for the Framework Law to enter into force, yet the state continues to adopt a position of persistent inaction. The language of a century of denial policies is still being reproduced in the media and political discourse, and the Kurdish question continues to be defined as a matter of …

author: Unknown
title: Lawyer Newroz Uysal Aslan: Real change will come when Mr. Öcalan can engage with the outside world
content:
The relocation of Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan within Imrali F-Type High Security Prison has brought discussions about his status back into focus. Presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum's tendency to reduce the status of Abdullah Öcalan, the chief negotiator in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, solely to "disarmament" has drawn widespread criticism. The disagreement over Öcalan's status, one of the most important aspects of the process, came to the fore once again after Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP Ömer Öcalan, who recently visited his uncle on Imrali, reported that Öcalan opposed this restrictive approach and criticized attempts to address the process solely in terms of disarmament. DEM Party MP Newroz Uysal Aslan spoke to ANF and recalled that Abdullah Öcalan's status was that of chief negotiator. Uysal said: "The change in Mr. Öcalan's conditions must go beyond discussions about relocation and place him in a position where he can genuinely engage with society and guide the process."


'Relocation does not mean Mr. Öcalan's conditions are adequate'


Newroz Uysal Aslan said that Abdullah Öcalan's relocation within Imrali Prison was significant but insufficient to meet the needs of the process. Uysal stressed that the relocation should have taken place at the beginning of the process and had therefore been delayed. Uysal said: "We cannot say that defining the change solely in terms of relocation is sufficient either for his legal status or for the position of chief negotiator that would enable him to guide this process. Many individuals and groups have made statements on this issue. Some have approached it sensationally, while others have treated it as a matter of tabloid interest. However, beyond all this, Kurdish People's Leader Abdullah Öcalan holds the position of chief negotiator.


The conditions required for this position have not been fulfilled for more than two years. Relocation alone does not mean that these conditions have been made adequate. Therefore, what really matters is ensuring the means of communication with the outside world required by the Coordination for Peace and Political Participation, including communication with the movement, political actors, the press and academia. Because moving from one location to another within a prison does not create a fundamental or effective change in the process. The real change will become evident through the contacts Mr. Öcalan establishes with the outside world. Mr. Öcalan himself has approached the issue of relocation from the very beginning in terms of facilitating his relations with the outside world and the work of the coordinator. Otherwise, it is unethical to discuss his transfer to another location within the prison where he has been held for 27 years in such a sensationalist and tabloid manner.


The questions that need to be asked are these: Will his coordination role function alongside this relocation? Has the necessary legal status been established? Will the structures and cooperation required for this coordination be established with others who will work with Mr. Öcalan, including political institutions, different political movements outside the prison and representatives within the state? And when will we, as the public and as society, be able to see and discuss these developments? These are the real questions, and they have still not been fully answered. The relocation is important, but it does not, on its own, meet the needs of the process."


'The approach to Öcalan's status must be clarified'


Newroz Uysal Aslan criticized presidential adviser Mehmet Uçum for defining Abdullah Öcalan's status solely in terms of disarmament. Uysal said that Uçum had viewed the process from the outset through the lens of regional war, Turkey's growing power in the region and the concept of a "strong state," while attempting to confine the Kurdish people to a narrow and restricted political space. She stressed that Uçum's approach did not necessarily mean that the state or government would conduct the process accordingly, or that Öcalan, the Kurdish movement and Kurdish political actors would accept such an approach.


Uysal said: "Many groups have already repeatedly stated that such approaches, particularly the language being used, poison the process and are incompatible with its objectives. This approach is precisely one of the reasons why we want Mr. Öcalan's relocation to be assessed together with his working …

title: [Italien] Gefährliche Gespräche – Kurze Überlegungen zur Operation gegen Anarchist*innen vom 16. Juni
content:
Gefährliche Gespräche


Kurze Überlegungen zur Operation gegen Anarchist*innen vom 16. Juni


Oktober 2026


Teil I _Anatomie einer Ermittlung_


Die Ermittlung, die zu den Festnahmen vom 16. Juni führte, geht auf eine Untersuchung zurück, die mindestens seit September 2024 im Zusammenhang mit der Flucht des anarchistischen Genossen Salvatore Vespertino (genannt Ghespe) lief. Ghespe war seit Januar 2023 spurlos verschwunden und galt sechs Monate später, nach seiner rechtskräftigen Verurteilung zu acht Jahren Haft, offiziell als unauffindbar. Offenbar wurde eine breit angelegte Ermittlung gegen Personen und Kreise aus seinem Umfeld eingeleitet, um ihn aufzuspüren.


Aus den bislang verfügbaren Unterlagen der römischen Ermittlungen geht hervor, dass sich dieser Ermittlungsstrang, in dem zunächst der Verdacht auf Beihilfe zur Flucht und später auch auf Beihilfe zur Strafvereitelung (erschwert durch die §§ 270bis und 270-sexies des Strafgesetzbuchs1) bestand, sich zunächst auf die mutmaßlichen Einkommensquellen und das vermutete Versteck des Gesuchten konzentriert und dabei mehrfach auf „Geheimdienstquellen“ zurückgreift.


Um sein Versteck zu finden, ermitteln sie gegen eine Mitstreiterin, verfolgen deren Bewegungen anhand von Mobilfunk-Standortdaten und stufen ihre Aufenthalte im Gebiet Sambuci/Vicovaro als „auffällig“ ein – ein Gebiet, in dem sich ein Landhaus befindet, das bis vor zehn Jahren von Anarchist*innen unter dem Namen „Improbabile Squat“ bewohnt wurde. Nach einer Besichtigung vor Ort und der Befragung des Eigentümers kommt die Digos2 zu dem Schluss, dass das Anwesen zwar verlassen ist, jedoch Spuren einer kürzlichen Nutzung aufweist und potenziell bewohnbar ist. Daher lässt sie versteckte Kameras installieren, die auf den Eingang des Bauernhauses und einen möglichen Parkplatz in der Nähe gerichtet sind.


Anhand der Videoüberwachung stellen die Ermittler fest, dass das Landhaus sporadisch besucht wird – wenn auch nicht vom Gesuchten –, doch das reicht aus, um immer wieder Verlängerungen zu erwirken, und nachdem sie die Anwesenheit einer Anarchistin bemerkt haben, sogar die Installation von Raummikrofonen im Inneren. Am 15. Februar 2025 endet Ghespes Flucht leider mit seiner Festnahme in Spanien, doch die Ermittler geben nicht auf und erreichen immer wieder Verlängerungen der Überwachungsmaßnahmen für das Landhaus, mit dem Ziel, mithilfe dieser das Unterstützungsnetzwerk aufzudecken, auf das der flüchtige Mitstreiter zwei Jahre lang zurückgegriffen hatte. Auf diese Weise sehen und hören sie im Mai 2025 einen Mitstreiter im Haus, der davon spricht, „Wartungsarbeiten durchzuführen, um eine Veranstaltung zu organisieren“, woraufhin eine Videoüberwachung vor Ort eingerichtet wird.


Im Juli 2025 wird daher ein längerer Austausch zwischen Mitstreiter*innen aus verschiedenen Städten während zweier Tage auf dem Landhaus aufgezeichnet: 15 Stunden abgehörte und transkribierte Gespräche, in denen allgemeine Themen wie der Zustand der heutigen anarchistischen Bewegung, die Kommunikation mit der Gesellschaft, die Bedeutung der Forderungen der Aktionen, die Mobilisierungen für Palästina und der Umgang mit jüngeren Genoss*innen angesprochen werden, die Affinität und die Reproduzierbarkeit, die Wirksamkeit anarchistischen Handelns sowie die Frage, ob im Hinblick auf die Verlängerung der 41bis-Maßnahme3 gegen Alfredo Cospito erneut eine Mobilisierung gestartet werden soll oder nicht. Die Staatsanwaltschaft glaubt, alles im Griff zu haben, vergisst dabei jedoch die Flucht von Ghespe und leitet ein Ermittlungsverfahren gemäß § 270bis gegen die neun Mitstreiter*innen ein, die als Teilnehmer*innen des Treffens identifiziert wurden, wobei gleichzeitig Überwachungs- und Abhörmaßnahmen gegen sie in Gang gesetzt werden.


Nach dem, was bisher aus den Unterlagen hervorgeht, weisen die von der Digos eingesetzten technischen Überwachungsmethoden keine besonderen Neuerungen auf; sie bestehen aus „standardmäßigen“ Abhörmaßnahmen von Anrufen und SMS, der Erfassung von Telefonverbindungsnachweisen und Telematikdaten (d. h. Netzwerkdaten) der vergangenen Monate sowie der Geolokalisierung von Mobiltelefonen (Positionierung), GPS in Autos sowie Kameras, die den Hauseingang einiger Verdächtiger und des besetzten Bencivenga-Gebäudes aufzeichnen. title: Kreuzberg – going to the streets for Kyriakos Xymitiris
content:
On the evening of 31. October we gathered in front of the evicted bar collective Meuterei because the anarchist fighter Kyriakos was participating in this space. We did a wild and unregistered demonstration through the streets of Kreuzberg with a banner, shouting slogans, spraying the walls, barricaded the roads behind us with material from construction sides and trash bins and arrived at Mariannenplatz. We were prepared to defend us against the enemy, which attacked another demonstration in the context of european youth strikes some hours before. But the cops did not try to stop us, as they usually do with not registered marches. Freedom to Marianna and Dimitra!


Death to every state!


For a free Palestine within our lifetime!


Kyriakos Xymitiris always with us in the streets of fire!

author: Brian Hioe
title: The Country That Has Forgotten Joshua Wong
content:
THE SENTENCING of Hong Kong political activist Joshua Wong to an additional ten years in prison, on top of the time that he was already serving, should be a stark warning to Taiwan of the future that it faces if it acquiesces to Chinese political control. Still, one notes that many in Taiwan have forgotten the lessons of Hong Kong.

Wong’s extra ten years in jail were on the basis of alleged collusion with foreign forces. Wong has already spent six years in prison and recently celebrated his 30th birthday behind bars. The new charges mean that by the time Wong gets out of jail, he will be 40. Wong pled guilty to the charges, not because they are true, but as a means to lower his jail sentence.

This proves a tragic fate for Wong, who rose to fame as a youth activist as a teenager. In another future, as one of Hong Kong’s best and brightest, Wong would have taken up leadership in Hong Kong society. Instead, the society that Wong has sacrificed so much for has, because of Chinese political control, locked him away.

Clearly, through locking him away, China aims to hope that the world forgets about his plight, as well as that of many other Hongkongers who are not as internationally well-known as he. Nevertheless, many in Taiwan have already forgotten, or have come to see Hong Kong as a faraway place that offers few lessons for Taiwan.

It is this historical amnesia that members of the KMT, such as chair Cheng Li-wun, tap into in framing China’s actions as only because of the DPP provoking China. Wong’s fate and those of his cohort show that this is not the case. Advocates of One Country, Two Systems in Taiwan are counting on the Taiwanese public to not realize that One Country, Two Systems–first applied in Hong Kong, even if originally formulated to appeal to Taiwan–would have the same outcome.

If Taiwan acquiesced to Chinese rule, it would not be that one would be safe if one kept one’s head down politically. Rather, with the targeting of Wong and other pro-democracy figures for simply organizing a primary for pro-democracy candidates to run for office, one notes the criminalization of what was previously a legal activity. Under Chinese rule, the political red line would always be shifting.

Still, in Taiwan, one also sees that while promises were made to assist Hongkongers around the time of the 2019 protests, Hongkongers have increasingly come to be seen as potential Chinese spies. In this way, society has become increasingly unfriendly towards Hongkongers, as has strangely gone hand-in-hand with forgetting about Hong Kong’s political fate. This, too, has been observed in other contexts such as the US, with Hong Kong political exiles among those to face deportation by ICE. This evidences the hypocrisy of Taiwanese society, as well as the political leadership of countries such as the US, in promising to help Hongkongers only to throw them under the bus when convenient. Even when Taiwan remembers Hong Kong’s plight, Taiwanese should do better than simply see events in Hong Kong as at a remove and having little to do with them. Taiwan should do better.

author: Eduardo Scott
title: Branco duro, pingo de mel, maracotão ou solta caroço
content:
Meu avô amava frutas, em especial pêssegos. Nós morávamos em Jundiaí e ele pegava seu Fiat 147, a Fortunata, para passar fins de semana conosco. Naquela época, a Anhanguera era povoada de pequenas paradas e barracas à beira da estrada que vendiam a produção local, garapa e, às vezes, pamonha. Na safra, os pêssegos pareciam estar por toda parte. Depois vinham morangos de Atibaia, uvas Niágara de Jundiaí, daquelas de chupar e jogar fora a casca, figos de Valinhos, grandes, gordos e macios, como já não se encontram hoje. Às vezes havia também uvas Itália, de bagos gordos, que vinham — eu nem sabia de onde —, talvez do Vale do São Francisco. Mas a Fortunata quase sempre saía carregada com caixas de pêssegos aveludados e sumarentos.


Eu lembro também do pêssego em conserva, sobremesa de festa. Amarelos, macios, embebidos na calda, apareciam na mesa em dias mais nobres. Quase sempre o creme de leite de lata vinha ao lado. Eu me lembro da propaganda: “envolvi tudo”, falava uma voz de criança, com a câmera fechando na fruta e no creme espesso escorrendo sobre ela.


Os pêssegos em lata também apareciam no centro da mesa de Natal, cuidadosamente arrumados na forma de gelatina vermelha que tremia levemente sobre a toalha. Minha tia a preparava invariavelmente para as festas, perfumada com cravo e canela.


Quando via uma caixa de pêssegos, meu avô desembrulhava um deles, retirava o papel fino que o protegia, disfarçava, mas dava uma apertadinha para saber se a polpa cedia ou se ainda resistia na firmeza verdolenga.


Ele tinha uma tese. Conhecia todas as espécies e achava os branco duros melhores do que os solta caroço, os pingos de mel ou os maracotões. “Só têm tamanho, falta textura e sabor nesse aí.”


Acho que parte dessa paixão veio da época em que morou no Rio Grande do Sul. Mas ele também inventava causos para tornar as histórias mais interessantes.


Quando tive o Bistrô nos Jardins, quis fazer um Bellini seguindo a receita do Harry’s Bar. A receita de Cipriani leva purê de pêssego e espumante da região, o prosecco. Tentei reproduzir o purê usando maracotão, mas não funcionou. Coloquei um pouco de suco de maçã, pedaços em cubos descascados, um pouco mais de açúcar, tentei corrigir daqui e dali. Nada funcionava. Um ficava sem sabor, outro doce demais.


Fui pesquisar e descobri que na Itália existem variedades mais comuns — bianca, gialla e percoca — e que Cipriani usava, em sua receita, purê fresco de pêssego branco. Comprei mais pêssegos, tirei a casca, processei, cozinhei, tentei vídeos no YouTube, mas nada ficou igual ao que experimentei uma vez, num verão em Veneza. Desisti do drink.


Mas não dos pêssegos.


Meu marido é como meu avô: ama pêssegos. Mas não sabe diferenciá-los. Compra pela aparência. Às vezes acerta.


O pêssego sempre teve alguma coisa de desejo. A fruta suculenta, doce, perfumada, escorre pelo canto da boca, mela os dedos, ocupa o espaço inteiro só com seu cheiro. Tem até pele, e aveludada. “Pele de pêssego”, fala a adolescente sedutora e debochada passando o dorso da mão no rosto. Pêssego combina mais com o universo de Vênus do que com o da cozinha. Em inglês, amantes se chamam de “peach” — meu pêssego, meu docinho —, um apelido que cola na fruta toda a intimidade de um amor.


Mas eu não vejo nele a sedução. Vejo outra coisa — um universo de afeto e pertencimento. Uma lenda pessoal, uma ancestralidade que só eu e a minha família podemos entender. Uma possibilidade de reviver meu avô. E, na obsessão dele por distinguir cada variedade, lembrar que sinto muita falta dele chegando em casa carregado de sacolas de frutas e da necessária caixa de branco duros da feira.


Pêssegos assados


6 pêssegos branco duros maduros 150 g de açúcar demerara 50 ml de gin 25 ml de licor Peachtree


Corte os pêssegos ao meio. Retire o caroço. Disponha as metades com os buracos dos caroços para cima. Regue com o gin e o Peachtree. Polvilhe o açúcar demerara e leve ao forno a 180 graus até o açúcar começar a caramelizar.


Sirva com sorvete de iogurte ou nata.

author: Wanessa Celina
title: Políticos, empresários e a Meta estão por trás dos boicotes a eleitores do PT nas redes
content:
As estratégias de intimidação eleitoral atingiram um novo patamar no Brasil em 2026 com o surgimento, nas redes sociais, de listas de boicotes e postagens incitando a demissão de eleitores do presidente Lula. Isso porque desta vez não se tratou, como em eleições anteriores, apenas de manifestações de insatisfação do campo bolsonarista com a derrota nas urnas, mas de influenciadores, políticos e empresários motivando seus seguidores a punir funcionários e fornecedores em função de seus votos, o que é ilegal.


Essa é a conclusão da procuradora de Geny Helena Barroso Marques, dirigente da Associação Nacional dos Procuradores e das Procuradoras do Trabalho (ANPT). “O resultado da urna não pode autorizar ninguém a transformar o emprego em instrumento de vingança política”, afirma. “O que a gente vê posteriormente à eleição são influenciadores, são membros da sociedade, insatisfeitos com o resultado da eleição que começaram a promover uma campanha de discriminação contra trabalhadores”, relata Marques.


Um exemplo é a publicação no Instagram do deputado federal reeleito Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) em que declarou apoio aos boicotes comerciais: “Nós [de direita] temos o direito de escolher para onde vai o nosso salário. […] Agora a gente não quer mais consumir ou fortalecer pessoas que não condizem com os nossos princípios”.


Procuradora e diretora da Associação Nacional dos Procuradores e das Procuradoras do Trabalho (ANPT), Geny Marques diz que movimento é de “vingança política”


Já a presidente do diretório municipal do PL em Ananindeua (PA), Carolina Pereira Arruda da Costa, publicou um vídeo no Instagram em que orientava empregadores a dispensar funcionários por razões político-partidárias – mas sem revelar a verdadeira motivação da demissão, para esquivar-se de eventuais multas e sanções por assédio eleitoral. A

Justiça

 do Trabalho determinou a retratação nos canais oficiais de comunicação de Costa e a remoção do vídeo.


Costa também usou as redes sociais para informar que havia suspendido iniciativas de assistência social na região, justificando a decisão pela vitória de Lula no segundo turno. Entre as ações, está um projeto natalino que realizava a distribuição de brinquedos, cestas básicas e festas para crianças de comunidades locais. Na publicação, ela ironizou a expectativa em torno do novo governo e questionou se a população vulnerável não teria deixado a pobreza após o resultado das urnas. O Ministério Público do Trabalho chegou a ajuizar uma ação contra Carolina Costa, porém, até o momento da publicação desta reportagem, as imagens seguiam disponíveis em suas redes sociais.


Para a procuradora Geny Marques é importante distinguir esse movimento envolvendo políticos de uma “simples insatisfação pós-eleição”. “Isso carrega uma discriminação da sociedade que a gente tem que barrar de pronto, […] para entender que não é um movimento simples, banal, mas sim, que pode acarretar um movimento de ódio”, salienta.


A participação de parlamentares como incentivadores do desligamento de trabalhadores em função do voto ou convicções políticas, ou de boicotes a empresas, deve provocar o Ministério Público Eleitoral e do Ministério Público Federal a adotar uma nova etapa de verificação: a etapa da insatisfação. “Dentro da democracia, cabe essa insatisfação, mas é importante respeitar e não punir um trabalhador pela sua escolha. Mostrar que o trabalhador não se despe da condição dele de cidadão quando ele está trabalhando”, compreende Marques.


Diante da ofensiva contra eleitores do campo progressista, o Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) registrou, em apenas quatro dias após a votação de segundo turno, 1.817 denúncias de assédio eleitoral. Em duas semanas após as eleições, o número chegou a 5.018 denúncias, 1.645 a mais do que no ano de 2022, quando o órgão recebeu 3.373 denúncias, um crescimento de 48,7%. Além dos parlamentares, os alvos das denúncias incluem empresários e influenciadores digitais acusados de promover assédio eleitoral em suas plataformas.


Boicotes remetem à Alemanha Nazista


As listas de boicotes a empresas ou lojas “dos eleitores do PT ou do presidente Lula” circularam em várias cidades por todo o país por conversas no WhatsApp, posts no X (antigo Twitter) e até em publicações no Instagram após o fim do segundo turno. Além das listagens, foi criado um site chamado “Meu dinheiro não”, com supostos apoiadores da campanha do presidente reeleito.

title: Se realizará el 8vo Encuentro del Libro y la Propaganda Anarquista de Santiago en el Espacio Comunitario Pablo Vergara Toledo
content:
¡Atención, compañerxs!

author: Rizomatica
title: Maestras en Isla Lemuy: un podcast para reconocer los aportes de las maestras rurales en la educación pública de Puqueldón
content:
El podcast presenta un recorrido histórico a través de seis capítulos donde se entrelazan las memorias de maestras normalistas, universitarias, jubiladas y en ejercicio.


Durante el año 2026, la comuna de Puqueldón ubicada en Isla Lemuy, Archipiélago de Chiloé, experimenta dos hitos históricos en materia de Educación Pública. Por un lado, el Liceo Puqueldón realizará la ceremonia de egreso de la primera generación de 4to medio, saldando una brecha de desigualdades que, hasta el año 2023, posicionaba a Puqueldón como la única comuna de la Región de Los Lagos carente de enseñanza media. Por otro lado, la Escuela San Juan de Lincay, con una trayectoria de 99 años, despedirá a los únicos dos estudiantes que cursan 6to básico y cerrará sus puertas a finales del año.


Estos dos acontecimientos constituyeron una motivación para que Revista Territorio Sur elaborara una propuesta al Fondo de Fomento de Medios de Comunicación Social de la SEGEGOB – Los Lagos. De esa manera, fue posible obtener financiamiento para ejecutar la iniciativa de conversar con seis maestras de Isla Lemuy; dos maestras normalistas (jubiladas) que ejercieron sus funciones como profesoras en la Escuela Puqueldón (actual Liceo Puqueldón), dos maestras universitarias (jubiladas) que ejercieron funciones en la Escuela Rural de Detif, Chulchuy, Aldachildo y Puqueldón y, finalmente, dos maestras universitarias (en ejercicio) que cumplen labores en la Escuela Rural Santa Rosa de Liucura y San Juan de Lincay.


A través de los seis episodios del podcast se logran apreciar elementos característicos de distintas épocas, describiendo aspectos como por ejemplo: conectividad, transporte, tecnologías, relaciones sociales y comunitarias entre las escuelas y las familias de sectores rurales, así como también, las transformaciones que experimentaron las escuelas públicas y rurales a lo largo de la historia. El podcast recorre episodios de la vida antigua, desde la década del 70 hasta la actualidad, donde por un lado se reconocen los aportes de la enseñanza media y por otro lado se lamenta el cierre de escuelas por falta de matrícula.


Finalmente, el podcast permite reflexionar sobre los desafíos actuales que presenta la Educación Pública y a su vez, proyecta futuras oportunidades para una educación con perspectiva e identidad territorial.

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: ‘It’s all fake, It’s all rhetoric:’ MP Billy Morin doesn’t have much good to say about Budget 2026
content:
Conservative MP Billy Morin says Budget 2026 reveals a pattern of performative reconciliation that leaves Métis governments on the sidelines.

Morin, the opposition critic for Indigenous Services and former chief of Enoch Cree Nation in Alberta, went further while holding a copy of the budget.

“It is ironic that it says ‘Masters of Our Destiny,’ he said. “I have crossed out destiny and put the masters of our deficit, debt, and deceit. And when it comes to Indigenous people in particular, the deceit one really, I think, is highlighted.”

In Thursday’s budget, the federal government announced nearly $50 billion in spending over the next ten years, with $32 billion in new investments for First Nations housing and infrastructure.

“The prime minister said he was going to do $32 billion of investments, and he portrays that as new spending. I see very minimal new spending in that… All he did is keep the funding going. They had two options: cut it or keep it going. And they portray it as an investment or new funding. It’s not.”

APTN reached out to Indigenous Services Canada to ask whether the $32 billion announced in the budget was new spending or not. We were told that, at the moment, all questions related to the budget are to be directed to Finance Canada.

According to the department that responded after the story was published, “Budget 2026 newly allots $32 billion worth of new cash into community infrastructure that wasn’t previously there. This includes $1.3 billion of new money going towards First Nations off reserve, Inuit, Métis and modern treaty and self governing partners to invest in affordable, supportive and transitional housing – which represents 10% of BCH’s new capital,” said the department. “How that money was derived or pooled is immaterial to the point, what matters is that community money that wasn’t available just yesterday now is – and is already flowing into Indigenous communities across the country.

“This is new money. Suggesting otherwise is patently false.“

Manitoba Métis Federation president David Chartrand said Friday that his government was “appalled” by being left out of the budget.

“In recent years, Canada has finally started to address the long-overlooked needs of the Red River Métis in areas such as housing, early learning and childcare, and post-secondary education,” Chartrand said in a statement. “However, a significant gap still exists between our Nation and the general population. There’s no doubt our people will be angered that their needs have been dismissed by this Budget.”

The MMF noted that Métis appear only once in the 532-page document — “as part of the title for a piece of legislation, An Act Respecting First Nations, Inuit and Métis children, youth and families – a piece of legislation that Canada has claimed they do not have a mechanism to fund us for.”

“The hugely successful distinctions-based approach has vanished, and government is reverting to phrases like ‘Indigenous’ when, in reality, they mean First Nations and Inuit,” Chartrand said. “The Red River Métis pay billions in taxes in this country, yet we have been forgotten by this government.”

Budget 2026 delivers $32B to First Nations, but Métis, Inuit largely left out

Manitoba Métis Federation ‘appalled’ they were left out of budget

The MMF said it had met with “numerous Ministers as well as the Prime Minister” ahead of the budget to discuss infrastructure, housing, health, and child and family services.

Morin said he understands the Métis questioning the government.

“How serious is this government about partnering with the Métis when they can’t even put them and acknowledge them in the budget? Morin said. “President Chartrand has every right to be appalled with this budget because every indication from this government is just like it treats First Nations people; it’s all fake. It’s all rhetoric and they don’t really mean it.”

Keelan is Anishinaabe from Walpole Island First Nation (Bkejwanong Territory). He graduated with an Honours B.A. In Political Science from the University of Toronto and follows the stories where power, money and public policy meet. Keelan has a strong interest in economics and finance, and is a lifelong hockey and sports fan.

title: Bafel Talabani: We are withdrawing from this government
content:
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) Executive Council convened with the participation of its President, Bafel Talabani. Following the meeting, Talabani released a video statement in which he commented on political developments in the Kurdistan Region and the process of forming a government.


Talabani stated that they had held several meetings with officials in Erbil (Hewlêr), but despite progress in the discussions, no agreement had been reached and parliament had been unable to convene. “On every occasion, progress was made in the discussions, but no results were achieved, and parliament could not convene. It has been demonstrated that the KDP does not know how to govern. We had previously warned that such a situation would arise. We do not recognise this session,” Talabani said.


‘We are withdrawing from this government’


Stating that the PUK Executive Council had authorised him to make the decision, Talabani announced the party's withdrawal from the government in the following terms: “Today, the PUK Executive Council authorised me, and we declare that we do not recognise this session. This government has failed. Therefore, our decision is to withdraw from this government. We are prepared to make any sacrifice. We are concerned with resolving the Rojava issue, the peace process, and our brothers and sisters in Rojhilat.”


‘Do not intimidate the people’


Addressing the KDP, Talabani called on the party to abandon any attempts to use force, saying: “I have a message for you: you have made an unjust decision. I am telling you, do not intimidate the people. Abandon your attempts to use force. We do not recognise this session or the government that will be formed as a result of it. I ask that you do not force us to take action in response. Whatever position you appoint in Erbil, we will appoint an equivalent position in Sulaymaniyah.”
